name: Kings Cup (Ring of Fire)
needs: Deck of cards, one center cup
howToPlay: Fan the deck face down around a center cup. Take turns drawing a card and following its rule: 2 = you (pick someone to drink), 3 = me (you drink), 4 = floor (last to touch the floor drinks), 5 = guys drink, 6 = chicks drink, 7 = heaven (last to raise a hand drinks), 8 = mate (pick a drinking buddy), 9 = rhyme (go around rhyming a word), 10 = categories, J = make a rule, Q = question master (anyone who answers your question drinks), K = pour some of your drink into the center cup. Whoever draws the fourth King drinks the center cup.
tip: The universal starter. Agree on your group's card meanings before you begin.
setup: Put an empty cup (the King's Cup) in the middle of the table.
Shuffle the deck and spread all 52 cards face down in a ring around the cup, each card touching the next.
Everyone gets a full drink in hand.
Agree on what each card means before you start (the list below is the common set). Write it down if people are fuzzy.
Pick who draws first; play goes clockwise.
rules: On your turn, slide one card out of the ring and show it. Do what that card says, then the next player draws.
Ace is Waterfall: everyone starts drinking at once. You stop when you want, the person to your left can only stop after you stop, and so on around the table.
2 is You: pick one person to drink 2, or two people to drink 1 each. 3 is Me: you drink 2.
4 is Floor: everyone touches the floor, last one drinks. 5 is Guys: everyone who identifies as a guy drinks. 6 is Chicks: everyone who identifies as a woman drinks.
7 is Heaven: everyone points to the sky, last one drinks. 8 is Mate: pick a buddy; whenever either of you drinks, the other drinks too, for the rest of the game.
9 is Rhyme: say a word, go around the table saying words that rhyme with it. First person to repeat a word or blank drinks.
10 is Categories: name a category (beer brands, Pokemon, anything). Go around naming one each. First to repeat or blank drinks.
Jack is Make a Rule: invent a rule that lasts the whole game (no first names, drink with your left hand). Anyone who breaks it drinks 1.
Queen is Question Master: until the next Queen is drawn, anyone who answers a question you ask drinks 1. Answering with a question is safe.
King: pour some of your drink into the center cup. The first three Kings just add to the cup.
Whoever draws the fourth King drinks the whole center cup. That ends the game. Reshuffle and start over or switch games.
drinkTriggers: Lose a mini game (rhyme, categories, floor, heaven): drink 1
2 drawn: the drawer hands out 2 drinks
3 drawn: the drawer drinks 2
5 or 6 drawn: all guys or all women drink 1
Ace drawn: waterfall, everyone drinks until the person to their right stops
Break a Jack rule: drink 1
Answer the Question Master: drink 1
Your mate drinks: you drink the same
Fourth King: the drawer drinks the entire center cup
variations: Ring of Fire (UK): put an unopened can in the center instead of a cup and slide each drawn card under the tab. Whoever pops the tab drinks the can. Breaking the ring of cards also means you finish your own drink.

Card swaps that many groups use: 5 is Thumb Master (whenever you put your thumb on the table everyone must follow, last one drinks, until the next 5), Jack is Never Have I Ever (one round, first to drop five fingers drinks), and 4 is Whores or Give 2 Take 2.
Circle breaker: whoever breaks the ring of cards while drawing drinks the center cup (or a full drink) immediately.
watchOut: The center cup is usually a nasty mix, so agree on what goes in it. The game can drag past 45 minutes; most groups stop at the fourth King rather than drawing every card. Mates and stacked Jack rules add up fast.
duration: 30 to 60 min per game; it usually ends at the fourth King, not the last card
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine but on the low end; the mini games (rhyme, categories, waterfall) are a little flat with few people. Swap the guys and chicks cards for left and right if your group is lopsided.
notes: Card meanings vary a lot by region. The main rules keep the set from the seed entry and add Ace as Waterfall, which both sources list as standard.

name: Ride the Bus
howToPlay: Round 1: each player is asked four questions on four dealt cards: red or black, higher or lower, in between or outside, and which suit. Wrong = drink, right = give drinks. Round 2: a pyramid of face-down cards is flipped row by row; if you hold a matching card you assign drinks equal to the row number. Round 3: the player with the most cards left rides the bus, flipping cards from a row and drinking on every face card, restarting on each miss.
tip: Brutal for whoever rides the bus. Cap the bus at 5 or 6 cards if you want to survive.
setup: Pick one dealer who keeps the deck for the whole game. The dealer can also play.
Shuffle a 52-card deck, no jokers. No cards are dealt yet.
Everyone has a drink in hand.
Clear space for a 15-card pyramid and a row of cards for the bus.
Agree on the pyramid drink values (1 to 5 is standard) and how long the bus is (four questions is standard).
rules: Phase 1 has four question rounds. Each round the dealer goes around the table starting on their left, asks the question, then flips the top card face up in front of that player. By the end everyone has 4 face-up cards.
Round 1: Red or black? Right: hand out 1 drink. Wrong: drink 1.
Round 2: Higher or lower than your first card? Ace is high, 2 is low. Right: hand out 1. Wrong: drink 1. Same value as your first card counts as wrong.
Round 3: Is the next card in between your first two cards or outside them? Right: hand out 1. Wrong: drink 1. An exact match with either card counts as wrong.
Round 4: Which suit? Right: hand out 5 drinks, split however you like. Wrong: drink 1.
Phase 2, the pyramid: the dealer lays 15 cards face down in rows of 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 from the bottom up. Bottom row is worth 1 drink, next row 2, then 3, 4, and the top card 5.

The dealer flips pyramid cards one at a time, bottom row first, left to right. If a flipped card matches the value of a card in your hand, put your card on it and hand out that row's drinks to anyone. Several players can match the same card.
You may hold a match back hoping for a higher row, but every card still in your hand when the pyramid is done counts against you.
After the top card, count cards left in hand. Most cards rides the bus. Tie: highest card rides; still tied, draw a card, highest rides.
Phase 3, the bus: the dealer flips fresh cards for the rider, asking the same four questions in order: red or black, higher or lower, in between or outside, suit.
Every wrong answer: the rider drinks 1, the cards are cleared, and the rider starts again from question 1 with new cards.
The ride ends when the rider gets all four right in a row, or when the deck runs out. Shuffle discards back in if you need more cards.
drinkTriggers: Wrong guess in Phase 1: drink 1
Right guess in Phase 1: hand out 1 drink (suit round: hand out 5)
Pyramid match: hand out 1 to 5 drinks depending on the row
Wrong answer on the bus: rider drinks 1 and restarts from question 1
Face card bus variant: Jack 1, Queen 2, King 3, Ace 4 drinks for the rider
variations: Face card bus: instead of questions, lay 10 cards face down in a row. The rider flips them one by one. Number cards are safe. A Jack means drink 1 and the row restarts with fresh cards, a Queen 2, a King 3, an Ace 4. The rider gets off the bus when they flip a whole row with no face cards. Cap the row at 5 or 6 cards if you want a shorter ride.

Red or black bus: the dealer lays out 5 (or 10) face-down cards and the rider calls red or black for each. Every miss is a drink. Some groups make the rider restart the row after a miss, others just count drinks.
Doubling pyramid: rows are worth 2, 4, 8, 16 drinks and the top card is a shot. Only for groups who want it heavy.
watchOut: The bus is brutal and can go on for a long time; set a cap (for example 10 drinks or 5 restarts) before it starts, and stop early if the rider is clearly done. The pyramid rows above 3 hand out a lot at once.
duration: 20 to 40 min per full game; the bus alone can be 5 to 15 min
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine and a common size. With only 4 hands, pyramid matches are rarer and everyone keeps more cards, so expect close calls for who rides. The dealer should play too.

notes: The seed text describes the face card bus. Three of three sources read treat the four-question bus (wrong answer means drink and restart from question 1) as the standard, so that is the main version here and the face card bus is listed as a variation. Sources disagree on whether a correct suit guess hands out 1 or 5 drinks; 5 is used here because two of three sources say so.

name: Pyramid
howToPlay: Deal 4 cards to each player; they look once and lay them face down. Build a face-down pyramid (5 cards in the bottom row up to 1 at the top). Flip the pyramid one card at a time. If you have a matching card in your hand (or claim to) you assign drinks equal to that row number. The target can call bullshit; if you were lying you drink double, if you were telling the truth they drink double.
tip: Great with 4 because everyone remembers everyone's tells.
setup: Shuffle a 52-card deck, no jokers.
Deal 4 cards face down to each player.
Each player looks at their 4 cards once, then lays them face down in a line in front of them. No peeking after that.
Build a face-down pyramid from the rest of the deck: 5 cards in the bottom row, then 4, 3, 2, and 1 on top (15 cards).
Agree on the row values: bottom row 1 drink, then 2, 3, 4, and the top card 5.
rules: The dealer flips the bottom row one card at a time, left to right, then moves up a row.
After each flip, anyone who has a card of the same rank (suit does not matter) can say so and point at someone: that person owes the row's drinks.
You can also lie and claim a card you do not have.
The person you pointed at either drinks, or calls bullshit.
If they call bullshit and you really have it, flip the matching card from your line to prove it. The caller drinks double the row value. Turn your card face down again; it can be used again later.
If they call bullshit and you were lying, or you flip the wrong card from your line, you drink double the row value.
More than one player can claim the same flipped card; settle each claim separately. If you hold two of the same rank you can claim twice.
Keep going up the pyramid. The top card is worth 5 drinks, so a called bluff there is 10.
The game ends after the top card is flipped and all claims are settled.
drinkTriggers: Accept a claim: drink the row value (1 at the bottom up to 5 at the top)
Call bullshit and the claimer proves it: you drink double the row value
Get caught bluffing, or pull the wrong card when proving: drink double the row value
Memory finale (optional): 2 drinks for each of your 4 cards you cannot name at the end
variations: Wikipedia version: deal 3 cards each and build a 6-row pyramid (6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1). Played cards go face up on the pyramid card and you draw a replacement from the deck.
Reverse pyramid: 1 card on the bottom row and 5 on top, so stakes start high and fall.
Memory finale: after the pyramid, each player names their 4 cards in order without looking. Each mistake is 2 drinks.
watchOut: Needs honest players about not re-checking cards. Double penalties on the top rows reach 8 to 10 drinks, so agree on what a drink is. It is a short game, so plan to run it twice.
duration: 10 to 15 min per game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal. With few players you learn everyone's tells fast and almost every card gets a claim or a bluff. Sites list 3 to 6 as the range.

links.label: A Little Bit Human: Pyramid rules

notes: Sources differ on cards dealt (3 or 4) and pyramid height (5 or 6 rows). The 4-card, 5-row version matches the seed and the more detailed source and is used as the main version.

name: Horserace
howToPlay: Pull the four Aces and line them up as horses. Lay 7 cards face down as the track. Each player bets a number of drinks on a suit. Flip cards from the deck; whichever suit comes up, that Ace advances one space. When a horse passes a track card, flip it; the matching suit's horse moves back one. First horse to the end wins. Losers drink their bet; the winner hands out theirs.
tip: Have one person narrate like a race commentator.
setup: Pull the four Aces out and lay them face up in a row at one end of the table. They are the horses, one per suit.
Shuffle the rest of the deck. Lay 7 cards face down in a column running away from the Aces, so the layout makes an L. That column is the track.
Pick an announcer who flips the cards and calls the race. With 4 people the announcer also bets.
Each player bets a number of drinks on a suit, for example 3 on hearts. Say bets out loud. Cap bets at 5 or so.
Keep the rest of the deck face down with the announcer.
rules: The announcer flips the top card of the deck. Only the suit matters.
The Ace of that suit moves forward one space along the track.
The first time any horse reaches a track space, flip the face-down track card on that space. The horse of that suit moves back one space. A horse at the start line cannot go back further.
Each track card is flipped only once, when the first horse gets there.
Keep flipping deck cards and moving horses. If the deck runs out, shuffle the flipped cards and keep going.
The first horse to move past the last track card wins the race.
Everyone who bet on the winner hands out drinks equal to their bet, split however they like. Everyone else drinks their bet.
Reshuffle everything, pick a new announcer, bet again, and run another race.
drinkTriggers: Your horse loses: drink the number you bet
Your horse wins: hand out the number you bet
Optional: drink half your bet before the race starts as the entry fee
Optional stumble card: when a Joker is flipped, every horse except the leader moves forward one
variations: No setbacks: skip the track card flips and just race. Shorter and simpler.

Bet the odds: flip the 7 track cards face up before betting. The suit with the fewest cards showing has the most left in the deck and is the favorite. The favorite pays double if it wins and costs double if it loses.
Stumble cards: shuffle both Jokers into the deck. When one is flipped, every horse except the leader moves up one space.
watchOut: Needs a bit of table space for the L shape. A good announcer makes the game; a quiet one kills it. Bets can get silly, so cap them. With setbacks a race can see-saw for a while.
duration: About 3 to 5 min per race; run 4 to 6 races
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: one person per horse if you want, and the announcer can still bet. It works just as well with everyone piling onto the same suit.

links.label: A Little Bit Human: Horserace rules

notes: The number of track cards is not fixed; sources say 7 or 8. The setback (faltering) rule is listed as a variation on Wikipedia but is the most common way the game is played, so it is in the main rules.

name: Blind Man's Bluff (Indian Poker)
howToPlay: Each player holds one card against their forehead facing outward without looking at it. Everyone can see every card except their own. Bet drinks on whether you have the highest card. Lowest card drinks the total pot.
tip: Bluff about other people's cards to mess with them.
setup: Shuffle a 52-card deck. Agree that Ace is high.
Agree on a bet cap, for example 5 drinks, and whether suits break ties (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs is the usual order).
The dealer gives each player one card face down. Do not look at it.
On the dealer's signal, everyone lifts their card to their forehead facing out. You can see every card but your own.
rules: Look at the other three cards and guess whether yours is likely the highest. If everyone else is low, yours is probably high.
The dealer bets first, then clockwise. On your turn you can bet a number of drinks, raise the current bet, or fold.
If you fold, drink the current bet right away and sit out the hand.
Go around once, then let anyone who was raised match the bet or fold. Then stop betting.
Everyone still in takes their card down and looks. Highest card wins.
The winner drinks nothing. Everyone else still in drinks the final bet.
Tie for highest: split the win, or use suit order if you agreed to.
If you peek at your own card, you are out of the hand and drink the current bet.
Collect the cards, shuffle, move the deal left, and play again.
drinkTriggers: Fold: drink the bet as it stood when you folded
Stay in and lose: drink the final bet
Peek at your own card: drink the current bet and sit out
Difference variant: losers drink the gap between their card and the winning card
variations: Lowest drinks the pot: only the single lowest card drinks, and they drink the total of all bets. Everyone else is safe. Faster and meaner.
Drink the difference: losers who stayed in drink the difference between their card value and the winner's card (Ace is 14), instead of the bet.
High low split: both the highest and the lowest card win, and the players in the middle drink.
watchOut: The betting round has no formal end, so agree on one lap plus calls. Keep a bet cap or one bad bluff turns into 8 drinks. Guides say it shines with 5 to 8 people.
duration: About 1 to 2 min per hand; play 10 to 20 hands
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine. You only see three other cards, so reading your own is a real guess, which makes the bluffing better. It gets thin with fewer than 4.

links.label: A Little Bit Human: Blind Man's Bluff drinking rules

notes: Who drinks what at the showdown varies by source (losers drink the bet, losers drink the difference, or only the lowest card drinks the pot). The simplest version is the main rule and the others are variations.

name: Across the Bridge
howToPlay: Lay 10 cards face down in a line. Players take turns flipping the next card. Number cards are safe. Face cards mean you drink and extend the bridge: Jack = drink 1 and add 1 card, Queen = 2, King = 3, Ace = 4. Reach the far side to win.
tip: Easy to teach, surprisingly long if the face cards keep coming.
setup: Shuffle a 52-card deck.
Lay 10 cards face down in a straight line. That is the bridge.
Keep the rest of the deck face down next to it.
The player to the dealer's left starts.
rules: On your turn, flip the next unflipped card on the bridge, starting from the near end.
Number card (2 to 10): safe. Toss it aside and flip the next one.
Jack: drink 1 and add 1 face-down card to the far end of the bridge. Queen: drink 2, add 2. King: drink 3, add 3. Ace: drink 4, add 4.
Hitting a face card or Ace ends your turn. Remove that card from the bridge. The new cards go on the far end, not where the face card was.
The next player clockwise picks up where you left off; nobody goes back to the start.
If the deck runs out, shuffle the discards to make a new deck.
When someone flips the last card of the bridge and it is a number card, they have crossed. Everyone else drinks 1 and the game ends. Play again with a fresh bridge.
drinkTriggers: Flip a Jack: drink 1
Flip a Queen: drink 2
Flip a King: drink 3
Flip an Ace: drink 4
Someone crosses the bridge: everyone else drinks 1
variations: Solo attempts: each player crosses the whole bridge alone and restarts from the first card after every face card. Much longer and heavier.
Speed bridge: 30 seconds per turn. If time runs out before you cross or hit a face card, drink 2 and pass.
Double down: after hitting a face card, call red or black and flip the top card of the deck. Right halves the penalty (round up), wrong doubles it.
watchOut: Pure luck with no decisions, so it is filler, not a main event. A run of Aces adds 4 cards each and can make the bridge drag. Whoever hits two face cards in a row takes a beating.
duration: 10 to 20 min per bridge
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine. Turns are quick and come around often, so nobody sits idle, and the shared bridge keeps it from running too long.

links.label: A Little Bit Human: Across the Bridge rules

notes: Only one detailed rules page could be fetched. Sources disagree slightly on the ending: some say the crosser simply wins, others say everyone else drinks 1.

name: Screw the Dealer
howToPlay: The dealer looks at the top card. The player to their left guesses its rank. If wrong, the dealer says higher or lower and the player guesses again. Miss both and drink the difference between your guess and the card. Guess right on the first try and the dealer drinks 5, second try the dealer drinks 2. Lay used cards face up by rank. If three players in a row guess wrong, the deck passes.
tip: The dealer role is the dangerous one.
setup: Everyone draws a card; lowest card is the first dealer. Put the cards back and shuffle.
Agree on the dealer penalties. Common default: dealer drinks 5 if you guess right first try, 2 if you guess right second try.
Clear a strip of table where revealed cards will be laid face up in rank order from Ace to King.
The dealer holds the deck face down. The player on the dealer's left guesses first.
rules: The dealer peeks at the top card without showing it.
The guesser names a rank (Ace through King). Suit does not matter.
Right on the first guess: the dealer drinks 5.
Wrong: the dealer says higher or lower, truthfully. The guesser guesses once more.
Right on the second guess: the dealer drinks 2.
Wrong again: the guesser drinks the difference between their second guess and the card. Ace is 1, Jack 11, Queen 12, King 13. Guess 9, card is Queen: drink 3.
Reveal the card and lay it face up in the rank row so everyone can see what is gone.
The next player clockwise guesses the next card. The dealer keeps dealing.
If three guessers in a row miss both guesses, the dealer passes the deck to the left. Any correct guess resets that count.
The game ends when the deck runs out.
drinkTriggers: Guesser right on first try: dealer drinks 5
Guesser right on second try: dealer drinks 2
Guesser wrong twice: guesser drinks the difference between their second guess and the card
Guess a rank that is already fully used up (all four showing): drink 1 extra (common house rule)
variations: Hardcore (the classic college version): dealer drinks 10 on a first-try hit and 5 on a second-try hit. Expect the dealer to get wrecked late in the deck.
Difference from the first guess: some groups make a double miss cost the gap between the first guess and the card, which is usually bigger.
No mercy: the dealer never passes after three misses and keeps the deck until someone guesses right.
watchOut: The dealer seat is the dangerous one, especially late in the deck when the face-up row makes guessing easy. Keep the rank row tidy or the game falls apart. Plan on beer, not spirits.
duration: 15 to 30 min for one deck
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine. Each person guesses often and the deck passes quickly on a bad streak. Guides prefer bigger groups so the dealer suffers less.

links.label: A Little Bit Human: Screw the Dealer rules

notes: This is the same game as Fuck the Dealer (library entry drunk-driver-fuck-the-dealer). Dealer penalty sizes vary by source (4/2, 5/2, 10/5); 5/2 matches the seed and sits in the middle. Sources are split on whether the difference is measured from the first or second guess; the second guess is used here because it is the one with the hint.

name: Higher or Lower
howToPlay: Flip one card. Guess whether the next is higher or lower. Wrong = drink, right = pass the turn. Streaks of 3 or more let you hand out drinks.
tip: Good warm-up or filler game.
setup: Shuffle a 52-card deck and put it face down.
Flip the top card face up next to it. That is the card everyone guesses against.
Agree that Ace is high and that an equal card counts as a miss.
Pick who goes first; play goes clockwise.
rules: On your turn, say whether the next card will be higher or lower than the face-up card.
Flip the top card onto the face-up card.
Right: nothing happens, and you guess again on the new card. Keep going as long as you are right.
Wrong, or the same value: drink 1. Your turn ends and the next player guesses.
Watch the pile; cards already gone change the odds.
When the deck runs out, shuffle and start again, or stop.
drinkTriggers: Wrong guess: drink 1
Same value as the card showing: drink 1
Streak house rule: every 3 correct guesses in a row, hand out 1 drink
variations: Streak bonus: after 3 correct in a row you may hand out 1 drink per extra correct guess, or stop and pass the turn safely.
Drink the difference: on a miss, drink the gap between the two cards instead of 1 (Ace is 14), which makes close misses cheap and big misses expensive.
Extra calls: guess red or black before each card, or number card versus face card, for an extra drink each way.
watchOut: Almost no decisions and no interaction, so it goes stale after 10 minutes. Use it as a warm-up or as a tie-breaker, not the whole night.
duration: 5 to 15 min per deck
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine; turns move fast enough that nobody waits long. It works with any number from 2 up.

links.label: Bar Games 101: Higher or Lower card game

notes: The streak rule in the seed is a house rule; the rules page read does not mention it, so it is listed as a variation. Sources differ on whether Ace is high; high is more common.

name: President (Asshole)
howToPlay: Deal the whole deck. Shed cards by beating the previous play with equal or higher rank; the first to empty their hand is President, last is Asshole. Each round the Asshole deals, hands their two best cards to the President, and fetches drinks. The President can order anyone to drink. Standard extra rules: skips, bombs, and "drink when you can't play".
tip: With 4 you get President, Vice President, Vice Asshole, and Asshole, so every seat has a rule.
setup: Use a 52-card deck, jokers out. Card order from high to low is 2, Ace, King, Queen, Jack, 10 down to 3. Suits do not matter.
For the first hand pick any dealer. Deal the whole deck one card at a time; some players get one extra card, that is fine.
Decide the drink rule for passing (drink 1 each time you pass is common) and what the Asshole owes at the end of a hand.
After the first hand, seats go in rank order: President, Vice President, Vice Asshole, Asshole, clockwise.
rules: The player left of the dealer (or the President after the first hand) leads one card, a pair, or three of a kind.
Going clockwise, you must play the same number of cards at a higher rank, or pass. A pair needs a higher pair, three needs higher three.
Passing does not knock you out. If play comes back around you can play again.
When everyone else passes after a play, the pile is cleared and the last player to play leads again.
Playing a 2 (single or set) clears the pile immediately and you lead again. You cannot lead with a 2.
When you run out of cards you are done for the hand. Keep playing until one person is left holding cards.
First out is President, second is Vice President, third is Vice Asshole, last is Asshole.
Next hand: the Asshole shuffles and deals, then gives their 2 best cards to the President. The President gives back any 2 cards. The Vice President and Vice Asshole swap 1 card the same way.
The President leads the new hand. The Asshole fetches and pours drinks for the table.
The President can tell anyone to drink at any time. The Vice President can tell anyone except the President. The Asshole can tell no one.
Play as many hands as you like; roles update every hand.
drinkTriggers: Pass on your turn: drink 1
Cannot play when it is your turn: drink 1 (same as passing)
President tells you to drink: drink 1, no arguing
Finish last: the Asshole finishes their drink (or drinks 3, agree beforehand)
Asshole gets told to drink by anyone: drink 1
Get skipped or bombed (if you use those rules): drink 1
variations: Revolution: playing four of a kind flips the ranking, so 3 is highest and 2 lowest until the next four of a kind.
Skips: playing a card of the same rank as the last card skips the next player, who drinks 1. Some groups also let a 4 reverse direction.
Jokers wild: add both jokers above the 2. A single joker beats anything and a pair of jokers cannot be beaten.
watchOut: Skill matters, so the same person can stay Asshole for an hour and get hammered; rotate or cap the Asshole penalty if that happens. Hands take 5 to 10 minutes, and new players need one practice hand.
duration: 5 to 10 min per hand; play 5 or more hands
playerSweetSpot: 4 is the minimum most guides give and it works well: every seat has a role (President, Vice President, Vice Asshole, Asshole) and there is no neutral middle. Hands are short with 13 cards each.

links.label: A Little Bit Human: President drinking game rules

notes: Drink amounts are house rules everywhere; no source gives a fixed number, so the 1-drink defaults are a reasonable starting point. The Vice President and Vice Asshole 1-card swap is standard in President but not every drinking guide mentions it.

name: Circle of Death
howToPlay: A Kings Cup variant with a different rule sheet, usually: Ace = waterfall, 2 = you, 3 = me, 4 = floor, 5 = guys, 6 = chicks, 7 = heaven, 8 = mate, 9 = bust a rhyme, 10 = categories, J = never have I ever, Q = question master, K = make a rule.
tip: Pick either Kings Cup or Circle of Death, not both; they are too similar.
setup: Put an empty cup (the center cup) in the middle of the table.
Shuffle a full deck and spread the cards face down in a circle around the cup, touching each other.
Everyone grabs a drink and sits around the circle.
Agree the rule sheet out loud before the first draw (the one below is the common one). Say it once, then stick to it.
Pick who draws first; play goes clockwise from there.
rules: On your turn, slide one card out of the circle and flip it so everyone sees it.
Do what that card says, then play passes to the left.
Ace: waterfall. Everyone starts drinking at the same time. You stop when you want; the person on your left can only stop after you stop, and so on around the table.
2: you. Pick someone to drink. 3: me. You drink.
4: floor. Last person to touch the floor drinks. 5: guys drink. 6: chicks drink (or swap 5 and 6 for any two groups, like left side vs right side of the table).
7: heaven. Last person to point at the ceiling drinks. 8: mate. Pick a buddy; whenever one of you drinks the other drinks too, for the rest of the game.
9: bust a rhyme. Say a word; go around the table, each person rhymes with it. First to fail or repeat drinks.
10: categories. Name a category (beers, car brands). Go around naming things in it. First to fail or repeat drinks.
Jack: never have I ever. Everyone holds up three fingers. Go around saying things you have never done; anyone who has done it drops a finger. First to drop all three drinks.
Queen: question master. Until the next Queen, anyone who answers a question you ask drinks. The right move is to answer with a question or ignore you.
King: make a rule that lasts the rest of the game (no first names, drink with your left hand). Breaking a rule costs a drink. Many groups also have each King pour some drink into the center cup.
If you break the circle (pull a card so a gap opens), you drink. Game ends when the last card is drawn or when the fourth King comes up, whoever draws it drinks the center cup.
drinkTriggers: Ace waterfall: everyone drinks until the person before them stops.
2: someone you pick drinks 1. 3: you drink 1.
4, 5, 6, 7: last person (or the named group) drinks 1.
8 mate: your buddy drinks whenever you do, for the rest of the game.
9 rhyme, 10 categories, Jack never have I ever: the person who fails drinks 1.
Queen: answering the question master costs 1.
King: breaking a standing rule costs 1 whenever it happens. Fourth King: drink the center cup (if you are using one).
Breaking the circle: drink 1 (or the center cup, house choice).
variations: No center cup: a lot of Circle of Death groups skip the Kings Cup entirely. Kings just make rules and the game ends when the deck is gone. Lighter and simpler.
Number cards as sips: some groups ignore the word rules for 2 to 10 and just say the drawer hands out (black cards) or drinks (red cards) that many sips. Faster and heavier.

Card swaps: the sheet moves around a lot between groups. Common swaps are Jack for make a rule and King for waterfall, or 5 as thumb master (when you put your thumb on the table everyone copies, last one drinks). Agree yours before you start.
watchOut: It is basically Kings Cup with a different sheet, so do not play both in one night. Rules pile up after a few Kings and nobody remembers them; keep a phone note or cap it at three active rules.
duration: 30 to 45 min for one deck
playerSweetSpot: Four is fine. The social cards (rhyme, categories, never have I ever) come back around fast with four people, so rounds are quicker and everyone drinks a bit more than in a bigger group.
notes: There is no single official sheet. Wikipedia treats Circle of Death as another name for Kings and lists card meanings that mostly match the seed (Ace waterfall, 2 you, 3 me, 4 floor, 7 heaven, 8 mate, 9 rhyme, 10 categories, Queen questions) but puts make a rule on the Jack and the cup rule on the King. The seed's Jack = never have I ever and King = make a rule is a common house sheet, kept as the main version here.

name: Drunk Driver (Fuck the Dealer)
howToPlay: The dealer lays 5 cards in a row face down and flips them one at a time for the "driver". Number cards are safe. Face cards mean the driver drinks (J=1, Q=2, K=3, A=4) and the dealer adds that many new cards to the row. The driver keeps going until the row is cleared without a face card or the deck runs out.
tip: Take turns driving so nobody gets wrecked by bad luck.
setup: Shuffle a full deck. Jokers are optional; if you leave them in, agree what they do (common: everyone finishes their drink).
Pick a driver and a dealer. The other two players just watch and heckle this round.
The dealer lays 5 cards face down in a row in front of the driver (some groups use 6).
The rest of the deck stays with the dealer as the draw pile.
Everyone has a drink in hand; the driver should have a full one.
rules: The driver flips the leftmost face-down card so everyone can see it.
Number card (2 through 10): safe. Move on to the next card in the row.
Face card or Ace: the driver drinks and the dealer adds new cards to the end of the row. Jack: drink 1 and add 1 card. Queen: drink 2 and add 2. King: drink 3 and add 3. Ace: drink 4 and add 4.
Keep flipping left to right. Added cards count the same as the originals, so one bad streak can make the row very long.
The drive ends when the driver has flipped every card in the row (including all the added ones).
If the draw pile runs out, the drive ends early. Shuffle the flipped cards back in for the next driver.
Pass the driver seat to the left and pick a new dealer. Play until everyone has driven once, or twice if you are feeling brave.
drinkTriggers: Flip a Jack: driver drinks 1 (and 1 card is added to the row).
Flip a Queen: driver drinks 2 (2 cards added).
Flip a King: driver drinks 3 (3 cards added).
Flip an Ace: driver drinks 4 (4 cards added).
Joker (if used): everyone, dealer and driver included, finishes their drink.
Number cards: nobody drinks.
variations: Doubles rule: if the flipped card matches the rank of the card before it (two 7s in a row, or two Queens), the driver drinks 2 extra. Some two-player versions use this as the main spice.

Fuck the Dealer, the other game: the name usually means a different guess-the-rank game. The dealer looks at the top card, the player to their left guesses the rank; wrong once, the dealer says higher or lower and they guess again; wrong twice, the guesser drinks the gap between guess and card; right on the first guess the dealer drinks 10 (or 5), right on the second the dealer drinks 5 (or 2). Three wrong guesses in a row and the deck passes left. That game is already in this library as Screw the Dealer.
Short drive: deal a 3 or 4 card row for a quick, lighter version, or let the driver choose the row length (4 to 8) as a bravery call.
watchOut: The driver can get destroyed by one bad run (an Ace into a King is 7 drinks and 7 more cards). Set a cap, for example a drive ends at 10 drinks no matter what, and never let the same person drive twice in a row.
duration: About 3 to 5 min per drive; a full round of four drivers is 15 to 20 min
playerSweetSpot: Four is fine but two people are spectators each drive, so keep drives short and rotate fast. Spectators can take a sip on each face card to stay involved.

links.label: Fuck the Dealer on Davis Wiki (the guessing game)

notes: The two names in the title are usually two different games. Drunk Driver is the row-of-cards face-card game described here (sources agree on J=1, Q=2, K=3, A=4 drinks and the same number of cards added; row length varies from 4 to 8, with 5 or 6 most common). Fuck the Dealer almost always means the guess-the-rank game that this library covers as Screw the Dealer. No source was found that uses Fuck the Dealer as a name for the row-of-cards game, so that pairing is treated as a house nickname.

name: Give and Take
howToPlay: Deal 4 cards to each player. Lay two rows of 6 cards face down: the Give row and the Take row. Flip row cards alternately, left to right. If you hold a matching rank for a Give card, give out drinks equal to that card's position (1 to 6). For a Take card, you drink that many.
tip: Row position 6 is the big one; keep an eye on who's holding doubles.
setup: Shuffle a full deck and deal 4 cards face up in front of each player (face up is the common rule; face down works too if you want bluffing).
Lay two rows of 6 cards face down in the middle, one above the other.
The top row is the Give row. The bottom row is the Take row.
Agree the drink scale across each row, left to right: position 1 = 1 sip, 2 = 2 sips, 3 = 3 sips, 4 = 4 sips, 5 = 5 sips, 6 = finish your drink (or 6 big sips if you want to survive).
Decide whether truths and dares are in play (see variations) and keep the leftover deck nearby for replacements.
rules: Flip the first card of the Take row (position 1).
Anyone holding a card of the same rank (suit does not matter) takes that many drinks. Two of that rank in your hand means you drink twice.
Next, flip the first card of the Give row. Anyone holding that rank gives out that many drinks to whoever they choose. Doubles in hand means you give twice.
Keep alternating: Take row position 2, then Give row position 2, and so on across to position 6.
If nobody holds the flipped rank, nothing happens. Move on (or replace the card from the leftover deck, house choice).
Position 6 is the big one: Take 6 means finish your drink, Give 6 means you can make someone else finish theirs.
The round ends when both rows are flipped. Shuffle everything, re-deal 4 cards each and lay new rows for another round.
drinkTriggers: Hold a rank matching a Take row card: drink the position number (1 to 5 sips; position 6 is finish your drink).
Hold a rank matching a Give row card: hand out that many sips to anyone (position 6 lets you make someone finish their drink).
Holding two or more of the matched rank: the drinks apply once per card.
Nobody matches: no one drinks that flip.
variations: Truth or Dare version (very common): the Take row is the Truth row and the Give row is the Dare row. Match a Truth card and answer a question the group picks or drink the position amount. Match a Dare card and you give out the drinks, then do a dare picked by the people you gave them to. Position 6 dares get wild, so agree limits first.
Long rows: some groups lay 12 cards per row, with the drink scale running 1 to 12 seconds of drinking instead of sips. Longer game, more matches.

Ace rule: anyone dealt an Ace gets to make a standing rule for the round. If an Ace is flipped in a row, the player holding the most cards of that suit makes the rule, then the Ace is replaced from the deck.
watchOut: With 4 cards each and only 16 cards in hands, lots of flips match nobody, so the game can go quiet; replacing dead cards from the deck keeps it moving. Position 6 is a full drink either way; swap it for 6 sips if the night is young.
duration: About 10 min per round; play 2 or 3 rounds
playerSweetSpot: Four is fine. Fewer hands means fewer matches, so each flip is lower pressure, but when you do match a 5 or 6 it hits hard. Three rounds with re-deals balances it out.

notes: Sources agree on two rows and 4 cards per player but not on row length or the scale. GameRules.com uses two rows of 6 with the Take side as Truth and the Give side as Dare, scaling 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 seconds then a full beer. A Beerwulf article (page could not be fetched, seen only in search summaries) uses two rows of 12 with truth and dare rows and 1 to 12 seconds. The main version here matches the seed (6 per row, position number = drinks) and the truth/dare layout is given as a variation.

name: Bullshit (Cheat) with drinks
howToPlay: Deal the whole deck. Play cards face down in rank order (Aces, then 2s, and so on), announcing what you're playing. Anyone can call bullshit. If the caller is right, the liar drinks and picks up the pile. If wrong, the caller drinks and picks up the pile. First to empty their hand wins; the rest finish a sip per card left.
tip: Four people means fewer cards per rank, so lying is more tempting.
setup: Shuffle a full deck and deal every card out. With four players everyone gets 13.
Sort your hand by rank so you can find cards fast.
Agree the pickup penalty: 1 sip per card you pick up, capped at 5, is the sane default.
Whoever holds the Ace of Spades (or just the player left of the dealer) goes first.
rules: The first player puts one or more cards face down on the pile and says what they are, for example two Aces.
The next player must play 2s, the next 3s, and so on up through Kings, then back to Aces.
You have to play at least one card every turn. If you do not have the rank, you lie.
Anyone can shout Bullshit before the next player plays. Flip the cards just played.
If the player lied, they pick up the whole pile and drink for it. If they told the truth, the caller picks up the whole pile and drinks for it.
Once the next player has played, the previous play can no longer be challenged.
First player to get rid of all their cards wins. Everyone else drinks 1 sip per card left in their hand, capped at 5.
drinkTriggers: Caught lying: pick up the pile and drink 1 sip per card picked up (cap 5).
Wrong call: pick up the pile and drink 1 sip per card picked up (cap 5).
Game over: losers drink 1 sip per card still in hand (cap 5).
Optional: the winner hands out 3 sips.
variations: Pass allowed: if you do not want to lie (or the rank is used up), you may pass. Playing cards every turn is the standard, this makes the game friendlier.
Flexible rank: you may play the current rank, one higher or one lower. Fewer forced lies, more mind games.
Full reveal: on a call, flip every card in the player's play, not just one. Some groups also let you lie about how many cards you put down.
watchOut: Chill but can drag past 20 minutes when nobody calls. Make a house rule that at least one call must happen per lap around the table. Loud callers tend to pick up big piles, so keep the cap.
duration: 10 to 20 min per game
playerSweetSpot: Four is ideal. 13 cards each and only four of each rank means you are forced to lie often, which is the whole fun.

name: Drunk Spoons
needs: Deck of cards, 3 spoons (or any objects)
howToPlay: Pass cards around trying to collect four of a kind. When someone gets it they grab a spoon; everyone else scrambles. Whoever is left without one drinks and takes a letter (S-P-O-O-N). Spell it and you finish your drink.
tip: Chaotic and short. Keep breakables away from the table.
setup: Put 3 spoons (one fewer than players) in the middle of the table, within reach of everyone.
Clear glasses and anything breakable away from the spoons.
Shuffle a full deck and deal 4 cards to each player. The dealer keeps the rest as a face-down draw pile on their right.
Everyone keeps a drink nearby but not on the table edge.
Agree the penalty ladder: lose a round, drink and take a letter; spell S-P-O-O-N and finish your drink.
rules: The dealer draws the top card of the pile, decides whether to keep it, then passes one card face down to the left. You always hold 4 cards.
Each player does the same: pick up the card passed to you, keep or pass one card to your left. The last player discards into a trash pile instead.
Keep passing fast. Nobody waits for the full table; cards flow continuously.
You are trying to get four of a kind (four 9s, four Queens).
When you get four of a kind, grab a spoon. Try to do it quietly.
The second anyone grabs, everyone else grabs. Whoever ends up with no spoon loses the round.
The loser drinks and takes a letter. Grabbing a spoon when nobody had four of a kind means you lose the round instead.
Shuffle and deal again. A player who spells SPOON finishes their drink. Then either they are out and a spoon is removed, or (friendlier) their letters reset and they keep playing.
If the draw pile runs out, shuffle the trash pile and keep going.
drinkTriggers: Lose a round (no spoon): drink 3 and take a letter.
Grab a spoon with no four of a kind: drink 3 and take a letter.
Spell S-P-O-O-N: finish your drink.
Knock over a drink in the scramble: drink 2 and clean it up.
variations: Hidden spoons: put the spoons somewhere inconvenient, like the next room or on top of the fridge. Great with four because the race is a sprint.
Tongues: no spoons. When you have four of a kind, stick your tongue out and keep playing. Last person to notice and stick their tongue out loses.
One strike: skip letters, the loser of each round drinks 5 and the game resets. Shorter and simpler.
watchOut: Needs space and sober-ish reflexes; drinks get knocked over. Spoons fly, so no metal near faces. Rounds take under a minute, so the letter ladder matters or it is over too quickly.
duration: About 1 min per round; a full game to SPOON is 10 to 15 min
playerSweetSpot: Four is great. Three spoons, fast passing and the circle is small enough that the scramble is instant.
notes: No published source describes a drinking version; the drink amounts here are a house layer on the standard letter rules. Sources differ on whether a spelled-out player is eliminated or simply resets; both are given.

name: Slapjack with drinks
howToPlay: Flip cards into a center pile. When a Jack appears, slap it. Slowest hand drinks. Slapping a non-Jack means you drink.
tip: Add doubles (two of the same rank in a row) as a second slap trigger.
setup: Shuffle a full deck and deal it all out face down, one pile per player, as evenly as possible.
Do not look at your cards. Keep your pile in one hand.
Clear the middle of the table and move drinks back from the edge.
Agree the slap triggers: Jacks only, or Jacks plus doubles (two of the same rank in a row).
Pick someone to go first; play goes clockwise.
rules: On your turn, flip your top card onto the center pile. Flip it away from you so everyone sees it at the same time.
If it is a Jack, slap the pile. The first hand on the pile wins it. If hands stack up, the bottom hand wins.
The slowest hand (or anyone who did not slap at all) drinks.
Slap a card that is not a Jack and you drink, and you give your top card to the player who flipped it.
The slap winner shuffles the pile into the bottom of their own stack. Play restarts with the player to their left.
If you run out of cards you can still slap. Win a slap and you are back in. Miss and you are out and finish your drink.
The game ends when one player has every card. Everyone else drinks 2; the winner hands out 3.
drinkTriggers: Slowest hand on a Jack: drink 1.
Did not slap a Jack at all: drink 2.
Slapped a card that is not a Jack: drink 1 and lose your top card.
Knocked out (no cards and missed a slap): finish your drink.
Game over: non-winners drink 2, winner gives out 3.
variations: Doubles: two cards of the same rank in a row are also a slap. With sandwiches too (same rank with one card between, like 5, 9, 5) the game is a lot more alert and a lot more false slaps.
Say it: you must shout Slapjack as you slap. Slap without saying it and you do not win the pile.
Irish Snap: count Ace, 2, 3 and so on out loud as each card is played; slap when the card matches the number called. Here the slowest hand picks up the pile and the aim is to lose your cards.
watchOut: Fingers get smacked and drinks get knocked. Fast games with very few drinks per minute until you add doubles, so start with Jacks only and add triggers if it feels slow. Needs an honest ref for close slaps.
duration: 5 to 10 min per game
playerSweetSpot: Four is ideal. Everyone can reach the pile, 13 cards each gives a decent game length, and slaps are a real scramble.
notes: The doubles slap is a common house rule rather than part of the standard rules on Wikipedia or Pagat, so it is listed as a variation. Drink amounts are a house layer.

name: Any normal card game with a loser-drinks rule
howToPlay: Golf, Rummy, Crazy Eights, Go Fish, Egyptian Ratscrew, Hearts, Spades, Durak, Big Two. House rule: loser of each hand drinks, each penalty card is a sip, and the overall loser finishes their drink.
tip: Hearts and Spades are ideal for exactly 4 players.
setup: Pick a game everyone already knows. For four people Hearts or Spades are the best fit; Crazy Eights, Go Fish, Rummy and Golf also work.
Agree the penalty scale before you deal: usually 1 sip per penalty point or per card left in hand, capped at 5 per hand, and the overall loser finishes their drink.
Agree how long you are playing: a set number of hands (4 is tidy, one deal each) or until someone hits a score.
Shuffle and deal according to the game. The example below is Hearts: deal all 52 cards, 13 each.
Keep a score sheet on a phone or paper so the drinks are not up for argument.
rules: Hearts example. Before play, each player passes 3 cards face down: left on hand 1, right on hand 2, across on hand 3, no pass on hand 4.
Whoever holds the 2 of clubs leads it. Go clockwise; you must follow suit if you can. Highest card of the led suit wins the trick and leads next.
You cannot lead a heart until a heart has been played on another suit (hearts are broken), unless you only have hearts. No hearts or Queen of spades on the first trick.
Hand over: count 1 point for each heart you took and 13 for the Queen of spades. Low score is good.
Drinks for the hand: the player with the most points drinks 1 sip per point, capped at 5. Anyone who took the Queen of spades drinks 2 extra.
Shoot the moon (take all 13 hearts and the Queen): you score 0, everyone else gets 26 points and drinks 3.
Play until someone passes 100 points or you finish your agreed number of hands. Lowest total wins and hands out 3 sips; highest total finishes their drink.
Playing something else? Same shape: loser of each hand drinks for their penalty cards or points, cap it, and the overall loser finishes their drink.
drinkTriggers: Each hand: worst score drinks 1 sip per point or penalty card, capped at 5.
Hearts: whoever takes the Queen of spades drinks 2 extra.
Hearts: someone shoots the moon, the other three drink 3.
Game over: overall loser finishes their drink; winner hands out 3 sips.
Optional: misdeal or renege (failing to follow suit when you could), drink 2.
variations: Spades instead: 2 vs 2 partners sitting across from each other, bid tricks, spades are trump. The losing team drinks 1 per 10 points they are behind at the end, and any player who bids nil and fails drinks 3. Great with exactly four.
Crazy Eights or Go Fish: 1 sip per card left in hand when someone goes out, cap 5. Quick and chill.
Golf (6 or 9 card): your score for the hand is your sips, cap 5. The person who knocks and does not win drinks double.
watchOut: Chill by design; it only gets heavy if you skip the cap. Hearts takes concentration, so it fades after the fourth drink. Keep score honestly and stop when hands get sloppy.
duration: Hearts: about 10 min per hand, 40 to 60 min for a 4-hand game
playerSweetSpot: Four is ideal. Hearts and Spades are built for exactly four players and the whole deck deals out evenly.
notes: The 2 of clubs lead, the three-hand pass rotation and 100-point end are the common American rules and are listed as variants on Wikipedia, which gives the older eldest-hand lead as the base rule. Drink amounts are a house layer with no published source.

name: Drunk Poker
howToPlay: Texas Hold'em with sips instead of chips. Folding costs a sip. Losing a showdown means drinking the pot (the sum of all bets).
tip: Set a per-hand cap so pots don't become unreasonable.
setup: Shuffle a full deck and pick a dealer. Put a coin or cap in front of them as the dealer button.
Agree the currency: 1 chip = 1 sip. No real chips needed, but a few coins or bottle caps make the pot easy to count.
Set the stakes: small blind 1 sip, big blind 2 sips, max raise 2 sips, and a hard cap of 10 sips in any single pot.
Agree that drinks are paid at the end of the hand, not during betting, and that you can swap a sip for water any time you are done.
Everyone needs a drink and a glass of water.
rules: The player left of the dealer posts the small blind (1), the next player posts the big blind (2). Blinds are sips that go into the pot.
Deal 2 cards face down to each player.
Betting round 1, starting left of the big blind: fold, call (match the biggest bet so far) or raise (up to 2 more). Folding costs you 1 sip right away.
Flop: burn one card, deal 3 face up in the middle. Bet again, starting left of the dealer.
Turn: burn one, deal 1 more face up. Bet again. River: burn one, deal the fifth card face up. Last betting round.

Showdown: anyone still in shows their cards. Best 5-card hand from your 2 plus the 5 on the table wins. Hand order high to low: royal flush, straight flush, four of a kind, full house, flush, straight, three of a kind, two pair, pair, high card.
The loser of the showdown drinks the pot (all sips bet by everyone that hand, capped at 10). If three people reach showdown, the worst hand drinks the pot and the middle hand drinks 2.
If everyone else folds, the last player standing wins and hands out 2 sips. Move the button left and go again. Play a set number of hands (10 is plenty) or until someone wants out.
drinkTriggers: Fold at any point: drink 1 immediately.
Lose the showdown: drink the pot (total sips bet that hand, cap 10).
Third-best hand at a 3 or 4 way showdown: drink 2.
Win because everyone folded: hand out 2 sips.
Optional: lowest hole cards shown at the end of a hand drink 1 extra.
variations: Shot glass stakes: the heads-up version where bets are literal pours into a shot glass. Each raise is a splash more; the showdown loser drinks the glass. Only sane with beer or something weak.
Dealer's choice: rotate between Hold'em, Omaha (4 hole cards, use exactly 2) and five-card draw. Same sip rules.
Winner assigns: instead of the loser drinking the pot, the winner splits the pot's sips among the other players however they like. Gentler and more social.
watchOut: Pots balloon fast if raises are uncapped, hence the 10-sip cap and max raise. Bluffing goes out the window after a few hands, so expect calling stations. Needs someone who actually knows hand rankings; keep a cheat sheet on a phone.
duration: About 3 to 5 min per hand; 10 hands is 30 to 45 min
playerSweetSpot: Four is fine. Enough people for real bluffing but hands move fast and nobody waits long between deals. Blinds come around every four hands, which keeps the pace up.

links.label: Single Shot Texas Holdem (shot glass version)

notes: There is no standard rulebook for drunk poker; the sip numbers, cap and fold penalty are the seed's rules fleshed out with sane defaults. The poker flow itself is standard Texas Hold'em from Wikipedia. The shot-glass variation page was found in search but not fetched.

name: Up and Down the River
howToPlay: Everyone gets 4 cards face up in front of them. The dealer flips 4 cards one at a time going up the river: if a flipped card matches the rank of one of yours you drink 1, then 2, then 3, then 4. Then the dealer flips 4 more coming down the river: a match now lets you hand out 4, then 3, then 2, then 1. Redeal and rotate the dealer.
tip: With 4 people and one deck you get a match about a third of the time, so it stays fair and quick; use the 3-card version if you want it lighter.
setup: Shuffle a 52-card deck.
Deal 4 cards face up in a row in front of each player. Leave them face up for the whole round.
Put the rest of the deck face down in the middle as the draw pile.
Pick a dealer; the dealer plays too.
rules: Up the river: the dealer flips the top card of the pile face up. Anyone with a card of the same rank drinks 1 for each matching card they have. Suit does not matter.
The dealer flips a second card. Matches drink 2 each.
Third card: matches drink 3 each. Fourth card: matches drink 4 each.
Down the river: the dealer flips a fifth card. Anyone with a match hands out 4 drinks per matching card, split however they like.
Sixth card: matches hand out 3. Seventh: hand out 2. Eighth: hand out 1.
That is one round. Collect all cards, shuffle, pass the deal left, and deal 4 new cards each.
Play as many rounds as you like.
drinkTriggers: Match on up-river card 1, 2, 3, 4: drink 1, 2, 3, 4 per matching card
Match on down-river card 1, 2, 3, 4: hand out 4, 3, 2, 1 per matching card
Counting round (optional): everyone drinks the number called if the flipped card matches it
variations: Three-card version: deal 3 cards each and flip 3 up (drink 1, 2, 3) and 3 down (give 3, 2, 1). Lighter and quicker.
Counting round: after the river, the dealer shuffles and counts 1 to 13 while flipping a card per number (Ace is 1, King is 13). If the card matches the number called, everyone drinks that many.
Big groups: use two decks and double the down-river drinks.
watchOut: A pair in your hand doubles every hit, so one unlucky deal can mean 7 or 8 drinks on the way up. It is pure luck with no decisions, so it is a filler between bigger games.
duration: About 3 min per round; play 4 to 6 rounds
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine. Guides suggest 6 or more for maximum chaos, but with one deck and 4 cards each there are plenty of matches, and the drinks stay manageable.

name: Three Man
howToPlay: Roll two dice in turn. The first person to roll a 3 becomes the Three Man and drinks whenever any 3 shows up. A total of 7 means the person to the left drinks, 11 means the right drinks, doubles let you hand out that many drinks, and a 1 and a 2 passes the Three Man title.
tip: Being Three Man for a long time is the real punishment.
setup: Sit in a circle around a table with two dice and everyone's drink in reach.
Decide a direction of play (clockwise is standard).
Pick a starting roller. Each player rolls one die in turn; the first person to roll a 3 is the Three Man.
Optional: give the Three Man a hat or other marker so nobody forgets who it is.
Agree on your roll table before starting, especially what 1-2, 4-1 and 5-1 do, since groups differ.
rules: The player after the Three Man rolls both dice.
Check the roll against the table. If it matches anything, the drinks happen and the same player rolls again.
If the roll matches nothing, the dice pass to the next player.
Any 3 showing on either die, or a total of 3: the Three Man drinks.
Total of 7: the player to the roller's left drinks. Total of 11: the player to the roller's right drinks.

Doubles: the roller hands one die each to two players (or both dice to one player). They roll, and each drinks the number they rolled. If that roll is also doubles, the original roller drinks the total instead.
1 and 2: the roller becomes the new Three Man. The old Three Man is free.
4 and 1: everyone puts a thumb on the table. Last one to do it drinks.
5 and 1: nothing happens. Pass the dice.
Total of 10: social, everyone drinks.
The Three Man also gets out of the job by rolling a 3 on their own turn. The next person to roll a 3 takes over.
There is no winner. Play until the group wants to stop or switch games.
drinkTriggers: A 3 on either die or a 3 total: Three Man drinks 1 (on 3-4, which is also a 7, the Three Man and the left neighbor both drink)
Total of 7: player to the left drinks 1
Total of 11: player to the right drinks 1
Doubles: the two chosen players each drink the number they roll on one die (1 to 6)
Doubles rolled again by a chosen player: original roller drinks the total of both dice
Total of 10: everyone drinks 1
4 and 1: last thumb on the table drinks 1
Dice fall off the table: roller drinks 1 per die
variations: Hat version (bargames101): any 3 makes the roller the new Three Man instead of making the current one drink. Extra rolls: 4 makes the roller Thumbmaster, 6 means left drinks, 7 means right drinks, 9 is a social, 10 the roller drinks and picks a partner, 11 or 12 the Three Man drinks.

Sloppy jalopy: if you knock a die off the table you become the new Three Man on top of drinking for it. Some groups also make 1-6 a left-neighbor drink and let the Three Man pass the title to anyone after drinking.
Doubles with a twist: the player you hand the dice to rolls to set how many drinks YOU take. If they roll doubles back at you, you drink double the total.
watchOut: The Three Man can get hammered fast since any 3 on either die hits them and 3s show up on roughly a third of all rolls. Keep the 1-2 pass rule in so the title rotates, and switch to sips rather than gulps if the same person stays stuck.
duration: Open ended; 20 to 40 min is typical before people want a change
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine. With 4 the dice come around quickly and left and right neighbors are real people rather than the same person twice, which happens with 3.
notes: Sources disagree on which neighbor drinks on 7 versus 11 (Wikipedia says 7 is left and 11 is right; gamerules.com flips them) and on whether 9 or 10 is the social. The main rules follow Wikipedia; the 4-1 and 5-1 lines come from its one-roll variant table.

name: Liar's Dice (Perudo)
howToPlay: Everyone rolls under a cup. Bid on how many of a face are on the table in total. Raise or call. The loser of a call loses a die and drinks. Lose all your dice and finish your drink.
tip: Treat 1s as wild for faster rounds.
setup: Give every player 5 dice and an opaque cup.
Everyone rolls one die; highest goes first. Re-roll ties.
Agree whether 1s are wild (standard Perudo: yes) and whether you use the exact-call rule.
Everyone shakes their dice in their cup and slams it face down, then peeks at their own dice only.
rules: The first player makes a bid: a quantity and a face, for example 'four 5s'. It means they think at least four dice on the whole table show a 5 (1s count as 5s if wild).
Play moves left. Each player must raise the bid or call the previous bidder a liar.
A raise means a higher quantity, a higher face at the same quantity, or both.
Bidding 1s: you can switch to 1s at half the current quantity rounded up (five 3s becomes three 1s). Switching back from 1s needs double the quantity plus one.
Call 'liar' (or 'dudo') and everyone lifts their cup and counts the named face plus wilds.
If the bid was true, the caller loses a die and drinks. If the bid was short, the bidder loses a die and drinks.
Optional exact call ('calza'): any player other than the bidder may say the bid is exactly right. If correct they get a lost die back; if wrong they lose a die.
The player who just lost a die starts the next round.
When you lose your last die you are out and finish your drink.
Last player with dice wins.
drinkTriggers: Lose a die on a call: drink 2
Wrong exact call: drink 2
Lose your last die: finish your drink
Optional: the winner hands out 3 drinks at the end
variations: No wilds: 1s are just 1s. Bids are smaller and bluffs are easier to read, which speeds up play.
Palifico: when a player drops to one die, that round has no wilds and only players on one die may change the face bid. Some groups also play the last die blind, bidding without looking.
Drink per die instead: every die you lose is one drink, and when a bidder gets caught by a big margin they drink the difference between the bid and the real count.
watchOut: Rounds get slow if people deliberate; set a 10 second limit on bids. Keep the cups on the table or dice end up on the floor every round.
duration: 10 to 20 min per game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is a sweet spot. 20 dice on the table is enough to make bids interesting without rounds dragging the way they do with 6 or more.

name: Mexico (Mexicali)
howToPlay: Each player rolls two dice. Read the higher die first (6 and 4 = 64). Doubles beat regular rolls; 2-1 "Mexico" is highest and doubles the stakes. Lowest roll of the round drinks.
tip: Add a "roll under the cup and bluff" rule for more tension.
setup: Get two dice and a cup to roll under; sit around a table.
Give everyone the same number of lives (3 is standard) or just agree to play for drinks.
Agree on how a Mexico (2-1) is treated: it is the highest roll and doubles the penalty for that round.
Pick a starter by rolling one die each; highest leads the first round.
rules: Read any roll as a two digit number with the higher die first: a 4 and a 2 is 42.
Ranking from low to high: mixed rolls 31 up to 65, then doubles 11 up to 66, then Mexico (21) on top.
The lead player rolls first and may roll up to three times, stopping whenever they like. Only their last roll counts.
The number of rolls the leader used is the limit for everyone else that round.
Everyone else takes their turn in order, within that roll limit.
The lowest roll of the round loses: they drink and lose a life.
If two players tie for lowest, they roll off against each other.
The loser leads the next round.
A Mexico during the round doubles the loser's penalty (2 drinks and 2 lives).
When you lose your last life you are out. Last one standing wins.
drinkTriggers: Lowest roll of the round: drink 1 and lose a life
Lowest roll in a round where someone rolled Mexico: drink 2 and lose 2 lives
Lose your last life: finish your drink
Rolling three times and still being lowest: drink 1 extra (house rule, optional)
variations: Bluffing version (Mia / Mexican Dice): roll under the cup, peek, and announce a number that must beat the previous claim. The next player either believes you and rolls, or lifts the cup. A liar caught drinks; a truthful roll challenged means the challenger drinks. A challenged Mexico means a whole drink.
No lives: just play round by round, lowest drinks, and keep going. Simpler for a casual night.
Money or chips: each round's loser pays one unit into a pot and the last player with chips takes it.
watchOut: Rounds are quick, so the drinks add up. With a 3 roll limit the leader can burn through dice time; tell people to stop on a decent roll.
duration: About 1 min per round; a 3 life game runs 10 to 15 min
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal. Each round has enough rolls to produce a clear loser but not so many that the leader's roll limit drags.

name: Beer Die
needs: One die, a long table, cups
howToPlay: 2v2 at opposite ends of a table. Toss the die so it bounces once on the table and lands off the far end past your opponents' cups. Opponents try to catch it. Points for uncaught lands; drinks for sinking into a cup or dropping a catch.
tip: Needs space. Great outdoor game.
setup: Set up a long table: the classic is a 4 by 8 foot sheet of plywood on sawhorses at roughly table height, but a beer pong table works.
Mark or imagine a line across the middle; defenders cannot reach across it.
Fill 4 cups and put one at each corner, about a hand width in from both edges.
Split into 2 teams of 2. Each team stands at one end next to its two cups.
Agree on a minimum toss height (head height or a ceiling line is common) and on whether FIFA is allowed.
One team rolls the die, the other calls high or low. The winner tosses first.
Grab 1 die (2 if you want to keep play moving while one is retrieved).
rules: Teams alternate tosses. One player tosses, then the other team's player tosses, and so on.
Toss the die underhand so it goes above the height line, lands on the opponents' half of the table, and bounces off the table.
The defenders try to catch the die with one hand after it leaves the table and before it hits the floor. No trapping it against your body, no two hands.
If the die lands on their half, bounces off, and is not cleanly caught: 1 point to the tossing team.
If the die lands short of the line, misses the table, or stays on the table: no point, the die is dead.
If the die hits a defender's cup and falls off uncaught (a 'dink'): 2 points.
If the die lands in a defender's cup (a 'sink'): 3 points, and that team finishes their drinks and refills.
Hitting your own cup scores nothing. Sinking your own cup is a self sink and the other team gets the points (some groups say it loses the game).
First team to 11, winning by 2, wins. Losers leave the table.
Any dispute about height or a catch: re-toss if you cannot agree.
drinkTriggers: Opponent scores a point on you: both defenders drink 1 (every point scored against you)
Sink against your team: both defenders finish their cups and refill
Your toss misses the table completely: drink 1
Toss out of turn or a dropped catch where the die was clearly catchable: drink 1 (house rule)
Saying the words 'five' or 'seven' out loud: drink 1 (call them 'bizz' and 'buzz')
Die lands showing a 5 after a dead toss: everyone drinks unless someone calls 'bizz' first (optional)
Losing 11 to 0: finish your drink and do whatever the table agreed, traditionally a lap
variations: Snappa: same game played sitting down with a chair at each corner. Sinks are usually 1 point, games go to 7 and win by 2 (some groups go to 11), and the usual drink is 1 fifth of a cup per point. Slower and calmer, better for indoors.

FIFA: if the toss misses the table completely, a defender may kick (foot or head only) the die into the air and their PARTNER has to catch it. A successful FIFA is worth 1 point to the defense, or in other versions the thrower sits out their next toss. Usually capped at 3 per team, and you cannot win a game on a FIFA.
Kill and fill: instead of a sip per point, everyone finishes and refills their cup every time a team hits a multiple of 3 (to 9) or 4 (to 11), plus on every sink.
watchOut: Needs a big sturdy table and room to dive, so play outside or in a garage. Height calls cause arguments; set a visible line. A sink is a full drink for two people, so slow the sip-per-point rule if the score runs high.
duration: 15 to 25 min per game to 11
playerSweetSpot: 4 is exactly right: it is a 2v2 game and that is the whole player count.

links.label: Beer Die rules at Dye Is Life (detailed house rules and FIFA)

notes: Point values are not standard: Wikipedia and the Snappa tradition give 1 point for a sink and play to 7, while gamerules.com and Dye Is Life give 1 for a plain point, 2 for a dink and 3 for a sink and play to 11 (Dye Is Life also allows 9). The main rules use the 1-2-3 scoring to 11 since it is the more common standing version. FIFA details and the bizz/buzz drink are house rules and vary.

name: Ship, Captain, Crew
howToPlay: Three rolls to get a 6 (ship), 5 (captain), and 4 (crew) in that order. The remaining two dice are your cargo score. Lowest cargo drinks.
tip: Fast rounds; play best-of-5.
setup: Get five dice and a flat surface.
Agree on a drink size for losing a round (1 drink is standard) and how many rounds you play.
Roll one die each; highest goes first and play moves left.
rules: On your turn, roll all five dice. You get up to three rolls.
You need a 6 (the ship), then a 5 (the captain), then a 4 (the crew), and they must be banked in that order.
If a roll shows a 6, set it aside. If it shows a 6 and a 5, set both aside. If it shows a 5 but no 6 yet, you cannot keep the 5.
Keep rolling the dice you have not banked until you have 6, 5 and 4 or run out of rolls.
Once you have all three, the remaining two dice are your cargo. Their total is your score.
If you have rolls left you may re-roll the cargo dice to try for a higher total, but you must take the new result.
If you fail to get ship, captain and crew in three rolls you score 0.
Everyone takes a turn, then compare scores. Highest cargo wins the round; lowest drinks.
Ties for lowest: those players drink. Ties for highest: roll off or share the win.
Play a set number of rounds (5 is good) and the player who drank the least wins.
drinkTriggers: Lowest cargo score in the round (including a 0): drink 1
Scoring 0 when someone else scored 12: drink 2
Round winner rolled ship, captain and crew on the first throw: everyone else drinks 1 extra
Optional: round winner rolls one die and hands out that many drinks
variations: Everyone but the winner drinks: instead of only the lowest drinking, all losers take 1 and the loser with the lowest score takes 2.
Winner rolls for drinks: the round winner rolls one die and the losers drink that many between them, winner's choice.
Pot version: everyone antes a chip each round and the highest cargo takes the pot; a tie carries it over.
watchOut: Very luck driven, so it is a background game rather than a main event. Rounds end fast; cap it at 5 or 10 rounds so it does not become a pure chug counter.
duration: About 2 min per round; play 5 to 10 rounds
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine. Rounds are short enough that waiting for three other turns is no problem.
