name: Drunken Yahtzee
howToPlay: Normal Yahtzee. Every zero on your sheet is a drink. A Yahtzee lets you hand out 5.
tip: Slow burn, good background game.
setup: Get five dice, a Yahtzee scoresheet (or draw one: 13 categories per player) and a pen.
Agree on the drink rules: standard is every zero scored is a drink, a Yahtzee hands out 5.
Roll one die each; highest starts.
rules: On your turn roll all five dice. You may re-roll any dice up to two more times (three rolls total).
After your last roll, write the result into one empty category on your sheet.
Upper section: ones through sixes, score the total of matching dice. 63 or more in the upper section earns a 35 bonus.
Lower section: three of a kind and four of a kind score the dice total, full house 25, small straight 30, large straight 40, Yahtzee 50, chance is the dice total.
If your dice fit nothing you must put a 0 in a category. That is a drink.
Rolling a Yahtzee (five of a kind) lets you hand out 5 drinks.
A second Yahtzee is a 100 bonus and you hand out 5 again.
After 13 rounds everyone adds up. Lowest total finishes their drink; highest hands out 3.
drinkTriggers: Write a 0 in any category: drink 1
Miss the upper bonus (under 63) at game end: drink 2
Roll a Yahtzee: hand out 5 drinks, split however you like
Lowest final score: finish your drink
Highest final score: hand out 3
variations: Score difference: at the end, everyone drinks the difference between their score and the winner's divided by 20, rounded down.
Bar version: anyone who rolls a Yahtzee buys themselves a shot, and five 1s means they buy the whole table a round (unverified folk rule).
Fast game: play only the lower section (7 rounds) to keep it under 20 minutes.
watchOut: A full 13 round game with 4 people runs long; it suits a slow night. The drinking is light until the end, so do not stack it with another heavy game.
duration: 30 to 45 min per full game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine but on the slow side; each player waits through three other turns of up to three rolls. Keep a second conversation going.
notes: There is no standard published Drunken Yahtzee ruleset; the drinking triggers here are the common house version (zero equals a drink, Yahtzee hands out drinks) layered on official Yahtzee scoring.

name: Midnight (1-4-24)
howToPlay: Roll six dice and keep at least one each throw until none are left. You must bank a 1 and a 4 to qualify; the other four dice are your score, max 24. Lowest score drinks, anyone who fails to qualify drinks double.
tip: With 4 people a round takes a minute, so play to a set number of wins.
setup: Get six dice and a flat surface.
Agree on the drink for losing a round (1 drink) and for failing to qualify (2 drinks).
Roll one die each to pick who goes first; play moves left.
rules: On your turn, roll all six dice.
After each roll you must set aside at least one die. You can keep more.
Re-roll the dice you did not keep. Repeat until all six are set aside.
To qualify you must keep a 1 and a 4 at some point. They score nothing themselves.
Your score is the total of the other four kept dice. The best possible is 24 (four 6s).
If you never keep both a 1 and a 4, you score 0.
Everyone takes a turn, then compare.
Lowest score of the round drinks. Anyone who scored 0 drinks 2.
Ties for lowest: all tied players drink.
First player to win 3 rounds wins the game; everyone else finishes their drink.
drinkTriggers: Lowest score in the round: drink 1
Failed to qualify (no 1 and 4): drink 2
Someone scores a perfect 24: everyone else drinks 1
Game ends: everyone but the overall winner finishes their drink
variations: 2-4-24: qualify with a 2 and a 4 instead of a 1 and a 4. Slightly harder.
Chicago style: rather than lowest drinks, the highest score each round hands out 3 drinks, so the game rewards greed.
Pot: everyone antes a chip and the highest score takes it; ties carry the pot to the next round.
watchOut: Pure luck, so it is a filler. The temptation to keep rolling for 6s is where people lose; remind them a safe 1 and 4 early is usually right.
duration: About 1 min per round; a 3 win game takes 10 to 15 min
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal. Turns are quick and there is always one clear loser.
notes: The drinking rules are a house adaptation; Wikipedia describes the base dice game only.

name: Pig
howToPlay: Roll one die as many times as you dare, adding up the points. Stop and bank them whenever you like, but roll a 1 and you lose the turn's points and drink. First to 100 wins.
tip: Set the target at 50 with 4 players so a game stays under 15 minutes.
setup: Get one die and something to track scores (phone notes is fine).
Agree on the target: 100 is standard, 50 keeps it quick.
Roll to see who goes first; play moves left.
rules: On your turn, roll the die.
If it shows 2 to 6, add it to your turn total. Decide: roll again or hold.
If you hold, add the turn total to your score and pass the die.
If you roll a 1, your turn ends, you lose the whole turn total, and you drink.
Keep going around until someone reaches the target.
First player to the target wins. Everyone else drinks the difference to the winner divided by 10.
Optional pressure rule: if you hold with fewer than 10 points in the turn, drink 1.
drinkTriggers: Roll a 1: drink 1 and lose the turn total
Lose a turn total of 20 or more to a 1: drink 2
Hold under 10 points: drink 1 (optional)
Game ends: losers drink the point gap to the winner divided by 10, max 5
variations: Two dice Pig: roll two dice and add both. A single 1 ends the turn with no points; double 1s (snake eyes) wipe your whole score and you finish your drink.
Hog: you roll any number of dice once; any 1 among them zeroes the turn.
Dare Pig: instead of drinking for a 1, the group picks a dare for you.
watchOut: Very light drinking unless people get greedy, which is the point. It drags if someone is cautious; use the hold-under-10 penalty to force action.
duration: 10 to 20 min per game to 100
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine. Enough players for someone to blow a big turn each round, and the wait between turns is short.
notes: Wikipedia covers the base game and strategy only; the drinking layer is a common house adaptation.

name: Beer Pong (2v2)
needs: 20 cups, ping pong balls, a table
howToPlay: Ten cups in a triangle each side. Throw balls into the opponents' cups; they drink any cup you hit. Sink all ten to win; losers finish whatever is left.
tip: Two re-racks per team keeps it fair.
setup: Set a long table (a beer pong table is 8 feet; a dining table works) with 2 teams of 2 at opposite ends.
Arrange 10 cups in a triangle at each end, point facing the other team.
Fill each cup about a third full with beer (or use water in the cups and drink from your own beer on the side).
Put a cup of water nearby to rinse the balls.
Agree on house rules: bounces, re-racks (2 per team is standard), elbows behind the table edge, and redemption.
Decide who shoots first (eye to eye shootout or a coin flip).
rules: Each team shoots both balls per turn, one player then the other.
Throw or bounce the ball at the other team's cups. Keep your elbow behind the edge of the table.
If a ball lands in a cup, a defender drinks that cup and removes it from the table.
A bounced ball may be swatted away by the defenders once it has touched the table. If a bounce shot goes in, it counts for 2 cups.
If both players sink a cup in the same turn, they get the balls back and shoot again.
Both balls in the same cup: that cup plus 2 more come out.
A ball spinning around the rim may be blown out by the defending team (if that house rule is on).
A team may ask for a re-rack when they have 6, 4, 3, 2 or 1 cups left, up to 2 times per game.
When a team sinks the last cup, the other team gets redemption: they shoot until they miss. If they clear all the remaining cups it goes to overtime with 3 cups each.
The losing team drinks whatever is left in their own cups.
drinkTriggers: Opponent sinks one of your cups: one defender drinks that cup
Bounce shot sinks a cup: drink 2 cups
Both balls in the same cup: drink 3 cups
You knock over your own cup: drink it and remove it
Game ends: losers finish all their remaining cups
Shutout (lose without sinking a single cup): losers do the agreed penalty, usually finish a full beer each
variations: Death cup: a made cup is left on the table; if it gets hit again, the game ends instantly.
Island: once per game you may call a single cup that is not touching any other. If you hit it, 2 cups come out; if you hit anything else, nothing counts.
World Series rules: no bounce bonus, no blowing, and only one re-rack. Cleaner, less arguing.
watchOut: Ten cups a side is a lot of beer for 4 people; use water in the cups and a drink on the side if you want more than two games. Needs a full length table and a floor you do not mind getting wet.
duration: 15 to 25 min per game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is the classic 2v2 format and exactly right.

name: Flip Cup (2v2)
howToPlay: Teams line up on opposite sides. In relay, drink your cup then flip it upside down from the table edge using one finger. The next teammate goes only once the flip lands. First team to finish wins.
tip: Best of 5 so a single bad flip doesn't decide it.
setup: Two teams of 2 stand on opposite sides of a table, facing each other.
Each player gets a plastic cup filled to the same line (the first ridge of a Solo cup is standard).
Line the cups up along the table edge in front of each player.
Agree on best of 5 and whether anyone can nudge a cup that falls off the table back on.
rules: The first player on each team taps cups with their opposite number, says cheers, and goes on 'go'.
Drink your whole cup.
Put the empty cup on the table edge so it hangs over, and flick the bottom with one hand so it flips and lands upside down.
If it does not land, grab it, reset it on the edge and try again. No two hands, no blowing.
Your teammate may not touch their cup until yours is upside down.
When your teammate's cup lands, your team is done.
First team to finish both cups wins the round.
Refill and switch order for the next round. Best of 5 wins.
drinkTriggers: Every round: each player drinks one full cup
Losing team: drink 1 extra from your own drink
Knocking over a landed cup or starting early: refill and redo that cup
Losing the whole series: losers fill and chug one more cup
variations: Survivor flip cup: after each round the losing team votes one of their own out. Needs more than 4 to be interesting, but with 4 you can play 'loser swaps': the slowest flipper swaps teams.
Reverse round: the second player on each team goes first in even rounds so the same person is not always the anchor.
Flip back: once your cup lands, flip it back upright before your teammate can start.
watchOut: The drinking is fast; five rounds is five cups each. Pour small or use half cups after round 2. Cups fly off the table, so clear the floor.
duration: About 1 min per round; best of 5 takes 10 min
playerSweetSpot: 4 works as 2v2 but is a stretch. The game shines with longer lines; with 4 it is over in seconds so play more rounds.

name: Stack Cup (Rage Cup)
needs: Cups, 2 ping pong balls, a center cup
howToPlay: Two players start bouncing a ball into their own cup. When you make it, pass the cup left. If you catch the person next to you (the stack reaches them while they're still trying), they drink the center cup and refill it. First bounce in wins instantly.
tip: Works fine with 4; the stack comes around fast.
setup: Put 10 to 15 cups in a tight cluster in the middle of a table and fill each about a third full.
Fill one extra cup to the top and set it in the center of the cluster: this is the center cup (also called the bitch cup or rage cup).
Everyone stands around the table.
Pick two players standing opposite each other and give each a ping pong ball.
Optional: name a scorekeeper to count stacks.
Count down from 3.
rules: On 'go', both starting players grab the nearest cup from the middle, drink it, and start bouncing their ball off the table into that empty cup.
Keep bouncing until you make it. The ball must bounce on the table before going in.
When you make it, pass your cup and ball to the player on your left. They start bouncing right away.
If you make it on your very first bounce, you may pass the cup to anyone at the table instead of just left.
If the player on your left is still bouncing when you make yours, you have caught them. Stack your cup on top of theirs.
The player who got stacked takes the stack and the ball, passes the whole stack to their left, then grabs a new cup from the middle, drinks it, and starts bouncing into that new empty cup.
If your ball accidentally bounces into one of the full middle cups, you must drink that cup and keep going.
If you catch someone who is on the center cup's turn, or you bounce into the center cup, you drink the center cup.
The stacks get taller and harder to hit. Keep passing until the middle cups are gone.
Last cup: whoever has to take the center cup drinks it and the game ends. Most stacks wins if you kept score.
drinkTriggers: Start of the game: both starters drink one middle cup
Getting caught (stacked): drink a new cup from the middle
Ball lands in a full middle cup: drink that cup
Ball lands in the center cup: drink the whole center cup, then refill it
Last person holding a stack when the middle is empty: drink the center cup
variations: Refill rule: whenever the center cup is drunk, the drinker refills it from their own drink and the game continues until the middle is gone.
Slap Cup: same setup, but instead of stacking you slap the slower player's cup off the table. See the Slap Cup entry.
Beer only in the middle: fill the cluster with beer and put a shot in the center cup, so the bitch cup is the real penalty and the small cups are just pace.
watchOut: The drinking is relentless; every stack is a fresh cup. Fill cups low and keep water around. The stack gets tall and wobbly, so clear anything breakable off the table.
duration: 5 to 10 min per game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine and fast: with the two balls starting opposite each other, the gap is only one player on each side, so stacks happen constantly. Expect to get caught a lot.
notes: Both sources describe stacking onto the player to your left and the first-bounce free pass. Neither spells out a formal rule for when the center cup is drunk; the common version (drink it when your ball lands in it or when you are the last one holding the stack) is used here and marked as house practice.

name: Quarters
howToPlay: Bounce a quarter off the table into a glass. Make it and pick someone to drink; keep going until you miss.
tip: Agree on a bounce rule to prevent lobs.
setup: Sit around a table with a hard surface (wood or laminate, not a tablecloth).
Put a glass in the middle filled with a drink; this is the penalty glass.
Give each player a quarter, or share one.
Agree on how much a drink is (one swallow is standard) and whether the quarter must bounce on its face.
rules: On your turn, bounce the quarter off the table and try to get it into the glass.
If it goes in, pick someone to drink. Then shoot again.
Keep shooting until you miss.
If you miss, your turn ends and the quarter passes left.
A shot that does not bounce off the table counts as a miss.
If you make 3 in a row you may make a rule (for example no pointing, no saying 'drink'). Anyone who breaks it drinks. Only one rule at a time.
If the quarter lands in the glass and someone argues, the shooter re-shoots.
Play until the group wants to stop.
drinkTriggers: Shooter makes it: chosen player drinks 1
Breaking an active rule: drink 1
Shooter misses with a shot that never bounced: shooter drinks 1
Shooter makes 3 in a row and chooses not to make a rule: everyone drinks 1 (optional)
variations: Chasing version (Wikipedia's main rules): two players opposite each other each have an empty glass. Shoot until you make it, then pass the glass left. If you catch the next player while they still have a glass, tap it; they drink from the center glass and refill it.

Speed quarters: two glasses go around at once and when one catches up to the other, the slower player stacks them and gets two shots at the top glass. Fail both and the player to their right spins a quarter while they drink until it stops.
Chandelier (Super Quarters): a big center drink with a shot glass per player around it. Sink your own, drink your own. Sink the center, everyone drinks and the last to finish drinks the center too.
watchOut: A good shooter can make 10 in a row and single someone out, so cap consecutive makes at 3 or rotate who drinks. Quarters fly into drinks and onto the floor, so rinse the coin.
duration: Open ended; 15 to 20 min is plenty
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine. Enough targets to pick on, and turns come back fast when someone misses.

name: Civil War
howToPlay: 2v2 beer pong but everyone throws at once, no turns. Each player defends 3 cups. When your cups are gone you're out. Last team standing wins.
tip: Loud and fast. Not a sipping game.
setup: Two teams of 2 stand at opposite ends of a long table.
Each player builds their own small triangle of 3 cups (6 cups per side; the full size version uses 6 cups each but that is a lot of beer for 4).
Fill each cup about a third full.
Put 2 ping pong balls on each side of the table (4 total), one per player.
Clear the floor around the table; balls will be everywhere.
Count down from 3.
rules: On 'go' everyone shoots at once. There are no turns.
Whenever you get a ball in your hands you may shoot immediately.
You may only shoot at the other team's cups, any player's triangle.
When a ball lands in one of your cups, you must drink that cup and remove it before you shoot again.
A bounced ball that goes in counts for 2 cups. Defenders may swat a ball once it has bounced on the table.
When all 3 of your cups are gone you are out. Step back from the table and stop shooting, but you may still fetch balls for your teammate.
A team wins when both players on the other team are out.
Losers finish whatever is left in their cups.
drinkTriggers: Ball lands in your cup: drink it and remove it
Bounce shot lands in your cup: drink 2 cups
Both balls in the same cup: drink 2 cups
Game ends: losers finish their remaining cups
Losing without sinking a single opponent cup: losers each chug a fresh beer
variations: Revive rule: if your team sinks 3 cups after you are out, you come back with 1 cup.
Island: once per game you may call a cup that is not touching any other; hitting it removes 2 cups, hitting anything else that shot counts for nothing.
Full rack: 6 cups each for a longer, heavier game. Only sensible with water in the cups.
watchOut: Loud, fast and messy. Four balls flying at once means spilled cups, so no glass anywhere near. The drinking is heavy and compressed into a few minutes, so take a break after each game.
duration: 5 to 10 min per game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is a stretch but works: standard Civil War is 3v3, so with 2v2 each player gets 3 cups and the game is short. Good for a quick burst.

links.label: Civil War beer pong rules at gamerules.com

notes: The cited rules describe 3v3 with 6 cups per player and 4 balls. The 2v2 with 3 cups each version here is the small table adaptation that several guides mention but do not detail.

name: Slap Cup
howToPlay: Like Stack Cup but when you catch the next person you slap their cup away and they drink a cup from the center pile.
tip: Interchangeable with Stack Cup; pick one.
setup: Put 10 to 15 cups in a cluster in the middle of a table and fill each about a third full.
Keep 2 cups empty and give them, plus a ping pong ball each, to two players standing opposite each other.
Optional: fill one center cup to the top as the final penalty.
Everyone stands around the table. Count down from 3.
rules: On 'go', both players with an empty cup bounce their ball off the table into their cup.
When you make it, pass your cup and ball to the player on your left.
If you make it on your first bounce, you may pass the cup to anyone at the table.
If the player on your left is still bouncing when you make yours, slap their cup off the table (or out of their hand). Use an open hand and go for the cup, not the person.
The slapped player grabs a full cup from the middle, drinks it, and keeps bouncing into that cup.
The slapper then passes their own cup to anyone at the table.
If your ball bounces into a full middle cup, drink it and carry on.
The round ends when the middle is empty. If you kept score, most slaps wins.
The player holding a cup when the last middle cup is taken drinks the center cup if you set one out.
drinkTriggers: Your cup gets slapped: drink a fresh cup from the middle
Ball lands in a full middle cup: drink it
Last player stuck with a cup when the middle is empty: drink the center cup
Slapping someone who had already made their shot: slapper drinks 1 (keep slaps honest)
variations: Stack Cup: identical game but instead of slapping, you stack your cup on theirs. Less chaotic and fewer spilled drinks.

Single target version: one big cup in the middle, everyone takes turns bouncing at it; whoever lands it shouts 'slap' and swats the other players' cups out of their hands. Anyone caught holding a cup drinks it.
Any direction: the slapped player passes to anyone, not left, to keep the cup moving around the table.
watchOut: Slapping sends cups flying, so use plastic and expect a wet table and floor. Agree that slaps hit the cup only. Drinking pace is the same as Stack Cup: fast.
duration: 5 to 10 min per round
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine but tight: the two balls start one player apart, so slaps come constantly. Rules sites suggest 6 to 8 for a longer game.

links.label: Slap Cup rules at officialgamerules.org (single center cup version)

name: Boat Race
howToPlay: 2v2 relay chug. Each person drinks their cup fully and turns it upside down on their head before the next teammate starts.
tip: Two minutes of chaos, then move on.
setup: Two teams of 2 stand or kneel in a line on opposite sides of a table.
Each player gets the same drink in the same size cup, filled to the same line.
Put all drinks on the table; nobody touches them until the start.
Pick a referee (or just use a phone countdown) and agree on the spill penalty.
Agree on the order: who is first and who is anchor on each team.
rules: On 'go', the first player on each team picks up their drink and drinks it all.
When your cup is empty, turn it upside down on your head. Spilling on your head proves it was not empty.
The next teammate may pick up their drink only once your cup is on your head.
Keep your cup on your head until the race ends.
The first team with both cups on both heads wins.
If a cup falls off a head or a drink is spilled, that player refills a splash and goes again (or the team takes a 5 second penalty if you prefer).
Refill, swap the order, and race again if you want a best of 3.
drinkTriggers: Every race: each player drinks one full cup
Spilling or a cup falling off your head: drink a refill of about a quarter cup and re-flip
Losing team: drink 1 extra each
Losing a best of 3: losers chug a fresh cup
variations: Flip instead of head: flip your cup on the table edge like Flip Cup before the next person starts (some sources treat this as the same game).
Two cups each: each player drinks two cups in sequence, which gives the anchor a chance to catch up.
Bierjunge (German version): a one on one race where the challenger names the drink and the loser buys the next round.
watchOut: It is a pure chug race, so it is heavy by design. One race per night is plenty; do not stack it after Flip Cup. Hard glass should never go on heads.
duration: About 1 min per race; 5 min including refills and a rematch
playerSweetSpot: 4 is a stretch: 2v2 races are over in 15 seconds. Works as a quick burst but boat races really want lines of 4 or 5 a side.

name: Drunk Jenga
howToPlay: Write a rule on each block (drink 2, give 3, truth, dare, make a rule, waterfall, etc.). Pull a block, do the rule. Knock it down and finish your drink.
tip: Leave a few blocks blank as "safe" pulls.
setup: Write one rule on each of the 54 blocks with a ballpoint or Sharpie. Mix drink rules (drink 2, give 3, waterfall), socials, truths, dares and a few blank safe blocks.
Build the tower: three blocks per layer, each layer turned 90 degrees from the one below.
Put the tower on a sturdy flat table with drinks out of the drop zone.
Agree on the penalty for knocking it over (finish your drink is standard).
Pick a starter; play goes clockwise.
rules: On your turn, pull one block out from anywhere below the top completed layer using one hand.
Read the rule out loud and do it straight away.
Put the block on top of the tower, keeping the three per layer pattern.
Rules that say 'until your next turn' or 'for the rest of the game' stay active; everyone enforces them.
If you touch a block and decide not to pull it, push it back in gently.
If the tower falls on your turn (or while you are placing a block), you knocked it over: do the penalty.
Rebuild and start again, or call it there. Blocks keep their rules so the next game is different.
drinkTriggers: Block says drink: drink the number written (usually 1 to 3)
Block says give: hand out that many drinks
Waterfall block: everyone drinks, you stop first and the others stop in order
Breaking a standing rule from an earlier block: drink 1
Refusing a dare or truth: drink 3
Knocking the tower over: finish your drink
variations: Non-dominant hand: every pull must use your weaker hand, which makes towers fall sooner and games shorter.
Numbered blocks: write numbers 1 to 54 on the blocks and keep the rules on a sheet so you can change the list every party.
Phone blocks: 'show your last text', 'post a story', 'call the third contact in your phone'. Only use them if the group is in the mood.
watchOut: Marker setup takes 20 minutes; do it earlier in the day. Mean dares and heavy drink blocks pile up late in a game, so balance the deck with blanks and socials. Keep drinks off the table so the collapse does not take them out.
duration: 15 to 30 min per tower
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal. Turns come around often enough to stay engaged and the tower lasts long enough for everyone to hit a few rules.

links.label: Drunk Jenga rules and block ideas at officialgamerules.org

name: Drunk Uno
howToPlay: Draw 2 = drink 2, Draw 4 = drink 4, Reverse = everyone drinks, Skip = give a drink, Wild = make a rule, forgetting to say Uno = finish your drink.
tip: Works especially well with 4.
setup: Shuffle a standard Uno deck and deal 7 cards each.
Flip the top card to start the discard pile (if it is a Wild Draw Four, re-draw).
Agree on the drink table before the first card: this entry uses the common house version.
Agree whether draw cards can be stacked and passed on.
rules: Normal Uno: on your turn play a card that matches the top of the pile by color, number or symbol, or play a Wild.
If you cannot play, draw a card. If it plays, you may play it; otherwise your turn ends.
Draw Two played on you: draw 2 and drink 2 (or pass it on with another Draw Two if stacking is allowed; the final victim draws and drinks the total).
Wild Draw Four played on you: draw 4 and drink 4.
Reverse: everyone drinks 1 and the direction flips.
Skip: the skipped player drinks 1, and the player of the Skip may give 1 more to anyone.
Wild: pick the color and make a rule that lasts the rest of the round (for example drink with your left hand).
When you go down to one card, say 'Uno'. If someone catches you before the next player acts, draw 2 and finish your drink.
First player to empty their hand wins the round; everyone else drinks the number of cards left in their hand (cap at 5).
Play a few rounds; whoever wins the most hands out a final 5.
drinkTriggers: Hit by Draw Two: drink 2
Hit by Wild Draw Four: drink 4
Reverse played: everyone drinks 1
Skipped: drink 1
Breaking a Wild rule: drink 1
Caught not saying Uno: draw 2 and finish your drink
Round ends: drink 1 per card left in your hand, max 5
Calling Uno on someone who had more than one card: you drink 2
variations: Drunko (Davis wiki version): skipped players drink, draw cards stack and pass on, and anyone forced to draw 8 cards in a row takes a shot. Wrongly calling Uno on someone is a shot.
Shots version: Draw Two is one shot, Draw Four is two shots, Reverse is two shots for the reversed player, Skip is one shot. Only for short games.
Number cards count: 0 is a social, 7 means the player on your right drinks, which keeps every card doing something.
watchOut: Draw Four stacking with 4 players can turn into an 8 or 12 drink chain; cap chains at 8 drinks or ban stacking. Wild rules pile up, so write them on a napkin.
duration: 5 to 10 min per round; play 3 to 5 rounds
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal. Reverse and Skip matter, draw cards go around fast, and rounds stay under 10 minutes.

links.label: Drunko (Uno drinking rules) on Davis Wiki

notes: Drunk Uno has no official rules; the main table here is the common house version matching the seed howToPlay. The Davis wiki version differs in amounts and is listed under variations.

name: Chandelier
needs: Cups, a bowl, 2 ping pong balls
howToPlay: A full center cup sits on an upturned bowl with everyone's cup in a ring around it. Bounce balls at the cups: hit someone's cup and they drink it. Hit the center cup and everyone drinks and flips; last to flip drinks the center cup.
tip: With 4 people take turns instead of free for all so the balls do not vanish.
setup: Turn a bowl upside down in the middle of the table and put one cup on top of it, filled to the top. That is the chandelier.
Each player fills their own cup about a third full and puts it on the table in a ring around the center cup.
Give ping pong balls to two players sitting opposite each other.
Agree on turns (take turns clockwise, or free for all) and on who refills the center cup.
rules: On your turn, bounce the ball off the table at the ring of cups.
If the ball lands in another player's cup, that player drinks it and refills.
If it lands in your own cup, you drink it and refill.
If you miss everything, pass the ball to the player on your left.
If someone catches your ball before it hits the floor, they go next.
If the ball lands in the center cup: everyone drinks their own cup, then flips it upside down on the table edge.
The last player to land a flip drinks the whole center cup.
Refill the center cup and all the small cups and play on.
Play a set number of center hits (3 is plenty) or until people want out.
drinkTriggers: Ball lands in your cup: drink it
Ball lands in the center cup: everyone drinks their own cup
Last to flip after a center hit: drink the center cup
Ball bounces off the table onto the floor three times in a row: shooter drinks 1 (keeps shots honest)
variations: Scored game: a referee counts how many cups each player sinks; most sinks wins, but losing the flip after a center hit makes you the loser regardless.
Quarters version: use a quarter instead of a ball, with shot glasses around a big center drink.
Mixed cups: put a different drink in each cup so shooters aim for what they want to hand out.
watchOut: A center hit means a full cup for everyone plus a big cup for one person; keep the center cup beer, not liquor. Balls fly everywhere, so play on a floor you can mop.
duration: 10 to 15 min per game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is the minimum most rules give and it works, but the ring is small so hits come fast. Take turns to keep it controlled.

name: Beer Ball
needs: 4 cans of beer, a ping pong ball, a table
howToPlay: 2v2. Each player sets a full can on their end of the table. Teams take turns throwing a ball at the other side's cans. Hit a can and the owners drink from it until the defenders grab the ball and slam it on the table. First team to finish the other team's beers wins.
tip: Exactly 4 players is the standard format.
setup: Two teams of 2 stand at opposite ends of a long table.
Each player opens a can of beer and sets it on their end, anywhere on their half.
Optional: tape a line across the middle so halves are clear.
Get one ping pong ball and flip a coin for first throw.
rules: The throwing team throws the ball at the other team's cans. One throw per player, then the other team throws.
If the ball hits a can, both players on the hit team grab their cans and start drinking.
The throwing team chases down the ball and slams it on the table. The moment it hits the table, the drinkers must stop.
Put the cans back down and the turn passes.
If you knock a can over, that team drinks whatever spilled out as a penalty (or you pick it up fast and keep going, house choice).
When a can is empty, flip it upside down. That player is done drinking but keeps throwing.
The first team to empty both of the other team's cans wins.
Losers finish whatever is left in their own cans.
drinkTriggers: Your can is hit: drink until the ball is slammed on the table
Game ends: losers finish their cans
Throwing out of turn: your team drinks for 3 seconds
Can knocked over by the ball: owner drinks for 3 seconds
variations: Hit team drinks: in some houses the team that HITS the can drinks it (racing to empty their own beer), with the defenders slamming the ball to stop them. Agree before starting.
Two cans each: doubles the length and adds strategy over which can to shoot at.
Pong hybrid: a ball that bounces on the table can be swatted back by the defenders before it reaches the cans.
watchOut: Fast chugging in bursts; a long chase for the ball means a long drink. Clear the floor so the ball can be grabbed quickly, and stop at one game per night.
duration: 5 to 10 min per game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is exactly the standard format: 2v2, one can each.
notes: Sources disagree on who drinks when a can is hit (hit team or throwing team); the main rules use the hit team version, which is what bargames101 describes.

name: Never Have I Ever
howToPlay: Say something you've never done. Anyone who has done it drinks. Use the ten-fingers version so the game ends when someone's fingers are down.
tip: Set a "no work stories" rule if things get too personal.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Everyone holds up ten fingers (or five for a shorter game).
Agree on any off-limits topics before you start.
rules: The first player says something they have never done, starting with the words never have I ever.
Anyone who HAS done that thing takes a sip and puts one finger down.
If nobody drinks, the person who made the statement drinks instead.
Play passes to the next player clockwise.
When all your fingers are down you are out and finish your drink.
The last player with fingers still up wins the round.
drinkTriggers: You have done the thing: drink 1 and drop a finger
Nobody has done the thing: the statement maker drinks 1
All ten fingers down: finish your drink and you are out
variations: Lone drinker explains: if only one person drinks on a statement, they have to tell the story behind it.
No fingers: skip the counting and just play until the questions run dry, which makes it an endless background game.
watchOut: Statements go personal fast. Set topic limits up front, and with 4 people the same person tends to get targeted, so rotate who is being picked on.
duration: 15 to 30 min per game
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. You get fewer surprising reveals than a big group, but it moves faster and everyone gets plenty of turns.

links.label: Never have I ever on Wikipedia

name: Most Likely To
howToPlay: Read a prompt ("most likely to get kicked out of a bar"). On three, everyone points at someone. The person with the most fingers drinks that many sips.
tip: Have everyone pre-write prompts on scraps of paper.
setup: Sit so everyone can see everyone else.
Optionally write a stack of prompts on scraps of paper and shuffle them.
Pick who reads the first prompt.
rules: The reader says a prompt, like most likely to cry at a wedding.
The reader counts down three, two, one.
On one, everyone points at the person they think fits the prompt best. You can point at yourself.
Count the fingers on each person.
The person with the most fingers drinks that many sips.
On a tie, everyone tied drinks the number of fingers pointed at them.
The person who just drank reads the next prompt.
drinkTriggers: Most fingers pointed at you: drink 1 sip per finger
Tie for most fingers: everyone tied drinks their finger count
variations: Explain it: whoever gets the most votes can ask one voter to explain why, and if the explanation gets a laugh from the group the voter drinks too.
Secret vote: everyone closes their eyes and the reader taps the shoulder of the winner, who then drinks without knowing who voted.
watchOut: With 4 people the max is 4 sips, so it stays light. The real risk is prompts that sting; keep them funny not cruel.
duration: About 1 min per prompt; play 15 to 30 prompts
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. Votes are rarely unanimous so it stays fair, but pre-written prompts help because 4 people run out of ideas quicker than a crowd.

name: 21 (Twenty-One)
howToPlay: Count around the circle from 1. Saying one number passes clockwise, two numbers reverses direction, three numbers skips a player. Whoever says 21 drinks and replaces a number with a word or rule for the next round.
tip: After five rules it's nearly impossible, which is the point.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Pick who starts and which direction play goes.
Agree the penalty size: one sip for a mistake, a bigger drink for hitting 21.
rules: The starter says one, and the count goes up around the circle.
On your turn you say one, two, or three numbers in a row.
Say one number: play passes to the next player in the current direction.
Say two numbers: direction reverses and play goes to the player on your other side.
Say three numbers: direction stays the same but the next player is skipped.
Hesitate, say a wrong number, or speak out of turn: you drink and the count restarts at one.
Whoever says 21 takes a big drink.
That player then makes a new rule, usually replacing a number with a word, sound, or action, and starts the next round at one.
Rules stack for the rest of the game. Breaking a rule counts as a mistake.
Play until nobody can get past about 10, or until the group calls it.
drinkTriggers: Wrong number, hesitation, or out of turn: drink 1 and restart the count
Broke an added rule: drink 1 and restart the count
Said 21: drink 3 (or finish your drink) and add a rule
variations: Four numbers: some groups allow saying four numbers, which reverses direction AND skips a player.
No sandbagging: banning three single-number calls in a row, or banning a string of numbers that would land 21 on a specific person, stops people from gaming the count.
Roman numerals, binary, or themed words instead of plain numbers for a much harder round.
watchOut: Needs a strict referee on hesitation or it drags. With 4 players the skip and reverse moves land on the same people constantly, so 21 tends to hit the same person twice in a row.
duration: 20 to 40 min per game
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. Fast turns and lots of reverses, though a skip with 4 players means only 2 people are in play for that moment, which gets predictable.

links.label: Tasting Table: how to play the 21 drinking game

name: 7-14-21 (Fizz Buzz)
howToPlay: Count up around the circle. Multiples of 7 and numbers containing 7 are replaced with a word or reverse the direction. Mistakes and hesitations drink.
tip: Add a second trigger number for round two.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Pick the replacement for seven: a word like fizz, or a clap.
Pick who starts and the direction.
rules: The first player says one. Count up around the circle, one number per person.
Any multiple of 7 (7, 14, 21, 28...) must NOT be said. Say the replacement word or clap instead.
Any number with a 7 in it (17, 27, 37...) also gets the replacement word.
Every time someone says the replacement word, the direction of play reverses.
Numbers like 70 to 79 all count, so it gets messy fast in the 70s.
Say a forbidden number, say the word at the wrong time, hesitate, or go out of turn: you drink and the count restarts at one.
The round ends when someone messes up. Play as many rounds as you like, or aim for a target like 50 or 100.
drinkTriggers: Said a number you should have replaced: drink 1 and restart
Said the replacement word on a normal number: drink 1 and restart
Hesitation or wrong turn: drink 1 and restart
Group reaches the agreed target number: everyone takes a victory sip
variations: Fizz Buzz proper: replace multiples of 3 with fizz and multiples of 5 with buzz (fizz buzz for both). Add 7 as a third rule for a brutal round.
Claps instead of words: multiples of 7 get a clap and numbers containing 7 get two claps, which is harder to track by ear.
watchOut: Getting past 21 is rare once people are tipsy, so rounds are short. The reverse rule with 4 players bounces the count between two people a lot; drop the reverse if it feels stale.
duration: About 1 to 3 min per round; play 10 or more rounds
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. Everyone gets a number every few seconds, which keeps attention high. Fewer players would make it too easy to predict your numbers.
notes: The name 7-14-21 also belongs to a completely different bar dice game where players count aces rolled and the 7th, 14th and 21st trigger pick, buy, and drink actions. This entry describes the no-equipment counting game only.

name: Fuzzy Duck
howToPlay: Say "fuzzy duck" around the circle. Anyone can say "does he?" which reverses direction and changes the phrase to "ducky fuzz". Say it wrong (or spoonerize it) and you drink.
tip: Gets harder with every drink.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Pick who starts; play goes clockwise to begin.
rules: The first player says fuzzy duck. The next player clockwise says fuzzy duck, and so on.
On your turn you can instead say does he? This reverses the direction.
After a does he?, the phrase changes to ducky fuzz and goes the other way.
Another does he? flips it back to fuzzy duck and reverses again.
Keep the rhythm steady. Say the wrong phrase, jumble the words, speak out of turn, or hesitate and you drink.
A round ends on a mistake. The person who drank starts the next round with fuzzy duck.
Play until the group gives up, which happens sooner than you think.
drinkTriggers: Said the wrong phrase or spoonerised it: drink 1
Spoke out of turn or hesitated: drink 1
Two people speak at once: both drink 1
variations: No double does he: ban saying does he? twice in a row, which stops two neighbours trapping each other forever.
Speed round: anyone who takes more than two seconds drinks, enforced by the person opposite.
watchOut: The classic trap is saying does he? while looking at the wrong person so they jump in out of turn. Fun with 4, but two people can bounce does he? back and forth endlessly, so add the no-double rule.
duration: About 30 seconds to 2 min per round; play 10 to 20 rounds
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. Reverses land often enough to catch people, but it is better with 6 or more where a reverse surprises people further round the circle.

name: Thumper (Thumb Master)
howToPlay: One person is the Thumb Master. Whenever they put their thumb on the table, everyone must follow. Last to do it drinks and becomes the new Thumb Master.
tip: Runs in the background of any other game.
setup: Pick a starting Thumb Master, by rock paper scissors or whoever volunteers.
Make sure everyone can see the table edge at all times.
Start another game or just chat; this runs in the background.
rules: At any time, the Thumb Master quietly puts their thumb on the table edge.
As soon as you notice, put your thumb on the table too. Do not announce it.
The last player to notice and put their thumb down drinks.
That player becomes the new Thumb Master.
The Thumb Master can wait as long as they like before using the power, which is the whole trick.
Keep playing whatever else you are doing. The game only ends when you agree to stop.
drinkTriggers: Last to put your thumb on the table: drink 2
Thumb Master takes it too fast and nobody saw it (group decision): Thumb Master drinks 1
variations: Thumper (the full game): everyone picks a hand gesture, the group drums on the table and does the call-and-response (what are we playing? Thumper!), then the leader does their gesture followed by someone else's gesture to pass it. Hesitate or do the wrong gesture and you drink and become leader.
Swap thumbs for other signals: nose on the table, hand on your head, or a silent raised fist. Same rule: last to copy drinks.
watchOut: Can be forgotten entirely if nobody uses it, or abused by a Thumb Master who waits for someone to go to the toilet. With 4 people, decide whether absent players count as last.
duration: Runs in the background all night; each trigger takes about 10 seconds
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4 as a background rule. The gesture-chain Thumper game is also fine with 4 but gets better at 6 or more.
notes: No Wikipedia page for Thumper exists as of Oct 2026 (both Thumper_(drinking_game) and Thumper_(game) return 404). The seed name mixes two games: Thumb Master, a single-rule background game, and Thumper, the gesture-chain game, which is described in variations.

name: Medusa
howToPlay: Heads down. On three, everyone looks up at another player. If you lock eyes with someone, both drink.
tip: With 4 it happens constantly.
setup: Sit or stand in a tight circle so everyone can see every face.
Everyone holds their drink.
Pick someone to count.
rules: Everyone puts their head down and looks at the table.
The counter says one, two, three.
On three, everyone looks up and stares directly at one other player. No looking at the table or the ceiling.
If the person you are staring at is staring back at you, you both shout Medusa and drink.
If nobody matches, nobody drinks. Heads back down.
Repeat. Rotate who counts each round.
Play a set number of rounds, like 10, or until you want a break.
drinkTriggers: You lock eyes with someone: both drink 1
Looked anywhere other than at a person: drink 1
Looked up late or early: drink 1
variations: Shots version: the classic rule is a shot on a match. With 4 people this is too much; use sips.
Two matches: if two pairs lock eyes in the same round, all four drink double.
watchOut: With 4 players each person has only 3 targets, so a match happens most rounds. Use sips not shots and cap it at 10 rounds or it gets heavy quickly.
duration: About 10 seconds per round; play 10 to 15 rounds
playerSweetSpot: A stretch with 4 because matches are nearly guaranteed. Still works as a quick heavy burst between other games; just keep the pours small.

name: Would You Rather
howToPlay: Pose a dilemma; everyone picks a side. The minority drinks.
tip: Ties mean everyone drinks.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Pick who asks the first question.
Optionally keep a phone-free rule: questions must come from your own head.
rules: The asker poses a dilemma: would you rather A or B.
The asker counts down three, two, one.
On one, everyone including the asker points left for A or right for B. No abstaining.
Count the sides. The smaller group drinks.
If it is 2 against 2, everyone drinks.
The next person clockwise asks the next question.
Play until the questions run dry.
drinkTriggers: You are in the minority: drink 1
Tie (2 vs 2): everyone drinks 1
Refused to pick a side: drink 2
variations: Defend it: the minority can get out of drinking by convincing the majority with a one-sentence argument. If anyone switches sides, the majority drinks instead.
Guess the group: before the reveal, the asker predicts the split. Right guess, everyone else drinks one extra; wrong guess, the asker drinks.
watchOut: With 4 people a 1 versus 3 split means one person drinks alone a lot. Mix in silly dilemmas, not just gross ones, so it does not stall.
duration: About 1 min per question; play 15 to 30 questions
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. Ties happen often, so the everyone-drinks rule matters, and small groups let people actually explain their choice.

name: Truth or Drink
howToPlay: Ask someone a question. They answer honestly or drink.
tip: Use a question app or site if you run out.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Agree on any off-limits topics.
Pick who asks first.
rules: The asker picks any player and asks them one question.
The player answers honestly, or refuses and drinks.
The group decides if an answer was a dodge. A dodge counts as a refusal.
If the player answers, the asker drinks one sip for making them say it.
The player who was just asked becomes the next asker.
Nobody can be asked twice in a row.
Play until everyone has been asked 3 or 4 times, or until you want to stop.
drinkTriggers: Refuse to answer: drink 2
Dodged the question (group vote): drink 2
Player answered: the asker drinks 1
variations: Truth or Drink or Dare: refusers can take a dare instead of drinking.
Everyone answers: the asker poses one question and every player must answer or drink, which spreads the heat around.
watchOut: Goes from funny to too real fast. Keep questions about the group, not exes and family. With 4 people, the asker rotation means you cannot hide.
duration: 15 to 30 min per game
playerSweetSpot: Ideal with 4. Small enough that answers get heard and nobody waits long for a turn.

name: Categories
howToPlay: Name a category (cereal brands, NBA teams, Marvel movies). Go around naming items. Repeat, hesitate, or blank and you drink.
tip: Loser picks the next category.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Pick who names the first category.
Agree on a hesitation limit, about 3 seconds.
rules: The starter names a category, like cereal brands, and gives the first answer.
Go clockwise. Each player names something in the category.
No repeats. No made-up answers. The group can challenge anything shaky.
Take longer than 3 seconds, repeat an answer, or blank, and you drink.
The round ends when someone drinks.
The player who drank picks the next category and gives the first answer.
Play until you run out of categories or patience.
drinkTriggers: Hesitated past the limit: drink 1
Repeated an answer: drink 1
Failed a challenge or made one up: drink 2
Challenged a correct answer: challenger drinks 1
variations: Rhythm version: slap knees twice, clap twice, and answer on the clap. Missing the beat counts as a hesitation.
Niche picks: whoever names the category must be able to list at least 10 answers themselves, or they drink.
watchOut: Someone picking a category only they know (obscure anime, 90s cricketers) kills the fun. Make the picker drink if they choose something the group cannot play.
duration: About 1 to 2 min per round; play 10 or more rounds
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. Your turn comes back fast so categories empty out quickly, which is exactly the pressure you want.

name: Rhyme Time
howToPlay: Say a word; go around rhyming it. Fail or stall and you drink.
tip: Ban "orange".
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Pick who says the first word.
Agree on a hesitation limit, about 3 seconds.
rules: The starter says a one-syllable word, like cat.
Go clockwise. Each player says a word that rhymes with it.
No repeats and no made-up words. Near rhymes are the group's call.
Take longer than 3 seconds, repeat, or fail to rhyme and you drink.
The round ends when someone drinks.
The player who drank picks the next word.
Play as many rounds as you like.
drinkTriggers: Hesitated or blanked: drink 1
Repeated a word: drink 1
Picked a starting word with almost no rhymes (orange, silver): picker drinks 2
variations: Rhythm version: keep a slap-slap-clap-clap beat and answer on the claps.
Sentence rhyme: instead of a word, each player says a short line that rhymes with the previous one, building a terrible poem.
watchOut: Rounds get very short once the easy rhymes are used. Ban starting words with fewer than 10 rhymes and mix in longer words occasionally to keep it interesting.
duration: About 1 min per round; play 10 to 20 rounds
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. Turns come round quickly, which is where the pressure comes from.

name: Word Association
howToPlay: Say a word related to the previous one, fast. Pauses, repeats, or unrelated words drink.
tip: Add a 3-second timer.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Pick who says the first word.
Agree on a hesitation limit, 2 or 3 seconds.
rules: The starter says any word.
The next player clockwise instantly says a word connected to it.
Keep the chain going as fast as you can around the circle.
Pause too long, repeat a word already used, or say something nobody can connect and you drink.
The group can challenge a weak link. If the player cannot explain the connection in one sentence, they drink. If they can, the challenger drinks.
The round ends on a drink. The drinker starts the next chain.
Play until you get bored or run out of words.
drinkTriggers: Hesitated past the limit: drink 1
Repeated a word from this round: drink 1
Lost a challenge: drink 1
Made a bad challenge: challenger drinks 1
variations: Banned words: the group picks 3 words that cannot be said all game. Saying one is a drink.
Opposites: each word must be the opposite of the last, which is much harder.
watchOut: Needs someone to actually enforce the timer or it turns into a chat. Also drifts into inside jokes fast, so challenge connections nobody else gets.
duration: About 1 to 2 min per round; play 10 or more rounds
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. Fast enough that nobody waits, and the chain is short enough to remember what has been said.

name: Paranoia
howToPlay: Whisper a question to the person next to you ("who here would survive longest in a zombie apocalypse"). They answer out loud with a name. The named person can drink to hear the question, or stay paranoid.
tip: The best questions are specific and a little mean.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Pick who whispers first and the direction.
Agree that questions must be about people in the room.
rules: Whisper a question to the player on your left so nobody else hears it. The answer must be someone in the group.
That player says the answer out loud: just a name.
The named person now has a choice: drink to hear the question, or stay paranoid and never find out.
If they drink, the asker repeats the question out loud for everyone.
If they do not drink, the question stays secret forever.
The player who just answered now whispers a new question to their left.
Keep going around. Stop after everyone has been named a few times.
drinkTriggers: You were named and want to hear the question: drink 2
You answered yourself as the name: drink 1
Asked a question with no one in the group as the answer: asker drinks 1
variations: Flip a coin: instead of choosing, the named person flips a coin. Heads, the question is revealed for free. Tails, they drink and it stays secret.
Everyone drinks to reveal: the whole group drinks together to unlock the question, which spreads the cost.
watchOut: The whole game is the questions, so mean ones can sour the night. With 4 players the same names come up a lot, so keep questions specific and funny rather than brutal.
duration: About 1 min per question; play 15 to 25 questions
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. There are only 3 possible answers to each question, so the paranoia is milder than in a big group, but it moves fast.

name: I'm Going on a Picnic
howToPlay: Each player repeats the growing list of items and adds one. Forget an item, drink.
tip: Alphabetical order makes it easier; random order makes it harder.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Pick who starts and the direction.
Decide: random items, or items in alphabetical order (easier).
rules: The first player says I am going on a picnic and I am bringing, then names one item.
The next player repeats the whole sentence with all items so far in order, then adds one new item.
Keep going around. The list grows by one every turn.
Forget an item, get the order wrong, or hesitate for too long and you drink.
After a mistake, the player who drank restarts the list from scratch with a new first item.
Play until you want to stop, or set a goal like reaching 20 items without a mistake.
drinkTriggers: Forgot or misordered an item: drink 1
Hesitated for more than 5 seconds: drink 1
Group reaches the target list length: everyone drinks 1 to celebrate
variations: Secret rule version: the starter has a hidden rule for what can be brought (only things starting with your initial, only red things). Others guess by trying items; wrong items get a no and a sip.
Themed trips: swap picnic for a desert island, a space mission, or a jail cell for different item vibes.
watchOut: Gets genuinely hard past 15 items and some people just cannot do it, so keep penalties small. Needs quiet to hear the list.
duration: About 5 min per round; play 3 to 5 rounds
playerSweetSpot: Ideal with 4. The list grows at a manageable pace and each player hears it from the others 3 times before their turn comes back.

name: One Word Story
howToPlay: Build a story one word per person. Stalling, breaking grammar, or laughing drinks.
tip: Record it and read it back at the end.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Pick who starts and the direction.
Optionally start a voice memo on a phone to replay the story at the end.
rules: The starter says one word, usually once or upon.
Each player adds exactly one word to the story.
Keep it a real sentence. Words have to make sense after the previous one.
Pause too long, say a word that breaks the sentence, or laugh so hard you cannot speak, and you drink.
Someone can end a sentence by saying full stop or period on their turn, which counts as their word.
A round ends when the story reaches an ending the group accepts, or after a few minutes.
Replay it or retell it. Play again with a new opening word.
drinkTriggers: Hesitation over 3 seconds: drink 1
Word breaks grammar or makes no sense: drink 1
Laughing so you cannot say your word: drink 1
Story ends: everyone drinks 1 to toast it
variations: Genre lock: pick a genre (horror, romance, news report) and stay in it. Drifting out of genre is a drink.
Two words each: slightly easier and the story goes somewhere faster.
watchOut: The game can stall when one person keeps steering it somewhere dumb. Stories with 4 people loop fast, so each person shapes a lot of it; agree to steer it somewhere.
duration: About 3 to 5 min per story; play 3 to 5 stories
playerSweetSpot: Ideal with 4. Enough voices to be chaotic, few enough that you can actually follow the sentence.

name: Drink While You Think
howToPlay: Name a celebrity. The next player must name one whose first name starts with the last letter of the previous celebrity's last name. You drink the whole time you're thinking. Same-letter names (like Michael Moore) reverse direction.
tip: Movie or athlete only versions are fun.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Agree on the category: celebrities is standard, or narrow it to athletes or actors.
Pick who starts and the direction.
rules: The starter says any famous person's full name, like Tom Hanks.
The next player must say a famous person whose first name starts with the first letter of the previous surname. After Tom Hanks you need an H name, like Harry Styles.
From the moment it is your turn, you drink continuously until you say a valid name. Think fast.
If you say a name whose first and last initials match (Michael Moore, Ryan Reynolds), the direction reverses and the player who just went has to answer again.
No repeats. Say someone already used and you drink an extra sip and go again.
If someone is stuck for more than about 20 seconds, the group lets them stop drinking, they take a penalty sip, and they pick any new name to restart.
Play until the group gets bored or the obvious names run out.
drinkTriggers: Thinking on your turn: drink continuously until you say a valid name
Repeated a name: drink 1 extra and try again
Said a name out of turn: drink 1
Gave up: drink 2 and restart with any name
variations: Last letter version: some groups link to the last letter of the surname rather than the first letter, which is harder because of all the names ending in S or N.
Fictional characters: use movie characters or video game characters instead of real people so the pool of names feels fresh.
watchOut: Someone who freezes can sip for a very long time; the 20 second mercy rule matters. Double-initial names are a weapon, so expect reversals to hammer whoever is slowest.
duration: 10 to 20 min per game
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. Reversals bounce between neighbours a lot, so the two fastest thinkers can gang up on the slowest; swap seats between games.

links.label: UNiDAYS: drinking games freshers should know (Name Game entry)

notes: Sources differ on whether the next name links to the first letter or the last letter of the previous surname. The first-letter version is more common and is used here; the last-letter version is in variations.

name: Cheers to the Governor
howToPlay: Count from 1 to 21. On 21 everyone says "cheers to the governor" and drinks, and the person who hit 21 replaces a number with a rule. Mistakes drink and restart.
tip: Almost identical to 21; choose one.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each, cups at least half full.
Pick who starts and the direction.
Optionally agree one starting rule so the tutorial round has a twist.
rules: Count up from one around the circle, one number per person, in order.
When someone says 21, everyone raises their glass, shouts cheers to the governor, and drinks.
The player who said 21 makes a new rule tied to a number: swap two numbers, skip a number, replace one with a sound or action, or make whoever says it drink.
The next round starts at one with every rule still in play. Rules stack all game.
Say a wrong number, forget a rule, or hesitate and you drink. The count restarts at one.
Keep going until the group cannot get past about 10, or until everyone agrees to stop.
drinkTriggers: Wrong number or forgot a rule: drink 1 and restart at one
Hesitated: drink 1 and restart at one
Group reaches 21: everyone drinks 1 and toasts
Any number-specific drink rule that has been added
variations: Count backward from 21 to 1 for a longer, harder round.
Accent rule: numbers must be said in a bad British accent, and breaking character is a drink.
watchOut: Nearly the same game as 21, minus the pass, reverse and skip mechanics. Pick one or the other. Rules pile up to where nobody gets past 5, which is the ending: stop there rather than restarting forever.
duration: 20 to 60 min per game
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. Each person gets the same numbers every round (1, 5, 9, 13...) unless a rule skips or swaps, so add a reverse rule early to shake it up.

name: Waterfall
howToPlay: Everyone starts drinking at once. Nobody can stop until the person to their right stops. The starter stops whenever they want.
tip: Use it as a punishment or round-ender rather than a full game.
setup: Everyone stands or sits in a circle holding a full-ish drink.
Pick who starts (usually whoever drew the card or lost the last round).
Check everyone knows who is on their right.
rules: On go, everyone starts drinking at the same time.
The starter can stop whenever they like.
You may only stop drinking once the person to your right has stopped.
So the chain runs around the circle: the starter stops, then their left neighbour can stop, and so on.
The last person in the chain gets the longest drink.
Once everyone has stopped, the waterfall is over.
drinkTriggers: Waterfall starts: everyone drinks continuously
You stop before the person on your right: drink 2 extra
Run out of drink mid-waterfall: you are done, top up for next time
variations: Reverse waterfall: play it to the right instead so the chain hits the starter last.
Short waterfall: cap the starter at a 5 second count so nobody gets wrecked.
watchOut: The starter can hold people hostage. Agree a cap, and remember with 4 people the last person is only 3 links from the start, so it is shorter than in a big group but still a lot if the starter is cruel.
duration: About 30 seconds per waterfall; use once per round of another game
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. Short chains keep it from going too far. Best used as a penalty inside another game rather than on its own.

name: Buzz
howToPlay: Count aloud around the circle, replacing any multiple of a chosen number (say 5) with "buzz". Miss it and drink.
tip: Layer "fizz" on a second number for a harder version.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Pick the buzz number, usually 5 or 7.
Pick who starts and the direction.
rules: The starter says one. Count up around the circle, one number per person.
Any multiple of the buzz number must be replaced with the word buzz.
Any number containing the buzz digit also gets replaced (with 5: 15, 25, 51, 52...).
Say a forbidden number, say buzz at the wrong time, or hesitate and you drink.
After a mistake, the count restarts at one from the player who drank.
Aim for a target like 50 or 100. Reaching it ends the round with a group sip.
drinkTriggers: Said a number instead of buzz: drink 1 and restart
Said buzz on a normal number: drink 1 and restart
Hesitated: drink 1 and restart
Group reaches the target: everyone drinks 1
variations: Fizz buzz: add a second number (3 for fizz, 5 for buzz). A number that fits both is fizz buzz.
Buzz reverses: saying buzz flips the direction of play, which with 4 players bounces the count around a lot.
watchOut: Very easy up to about 30, then the 50s wipe everyone out. If it drags, add the reverse rule or a second word. Needs a quiet room to hear mistakes.
duration: About 1 to 3 min per round; play 10 or more rounds
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. Everyone counts every few seconds so attention stays high.

name: Power Hour / Century Club
howToPlay: Take a shot of beer every minute for 60 minutes (Power Hour) or 100 (Century Club).
tip: A one-minute-per-song playlist does the timing for you.
setup: Get a shot glass each (1 to 1.5 oz, about 30 to 45 ml).
Stock enough beer: 60 shots is roughly 60 to 90 oz, which is 5 to 7 standard 12 oz beers per person.
Set a timer that goes off every minute, or queue a playlist where the song changes every 60 seconds.
Have water and food nearby.
rules: Start the timer.
Every time it goes off or the song changes, everyone drinks one shot of beer.
Refill your shot glass right away so you are ready for the next minute.
Keep going for 60 minutes. That is one Power Hour.
Anyone can stop at any time with no penalty. Finishing is not a dare.
Century Club is the same thing for 100 minutes: 100 shots, about 8 to 12 beers each. It is genuinely dangerous and most people should not attempt it.
The game ends when the timer ends or when everyone has stopped.
drinkTriggers: Every minute: drink 1 shot of beer (1 to 1.5 oz)
Missed a minute while out of the room: catch up with 1 shot when you return, no doubling up
variations: Half hour: 30 shots in 30 minutes for a group that wants the format without 6 beers each.
Mixed shots: replace some beer shots with water, soda, or shandy on a fixed schedule, like every fifth shot.
Themed playlist: everyone adds songs, and the person whose song is playing picks one rule for that minute.
watchOut: This is 5 to 7 beers in an hour, which pushes most people past a safe pace. Century Club nearly doubles that and carries real alcohol poisoning risk. Never use liquor, let people drop out freely, and stop the clock if anyone looks unwell.
duration: 60 min (Power Hour) or 100 min (Century Club)
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4; player count does not change the pace. Small groups actually make it easier to notice when someone needs to stop.
notes: Wikipedia does not state a shot volume. The 1 to 1.5 oz figure and the resulting 5 to 7 beer total are standard US shot sizing applied to 60 shots.

name: Song drinking games (Roxanne, Thunderstruck, Sweet Caroline)
howToPlay: Roxanne: split into two groups, one drinks on every "Roxanne", the other on every "red light". Thunderstruck: pass the drink on every "thunder"; whoever is holding it drinks until the next one. Sweet Caroline: drink on every "so good".
tip: Short, loud, and a good break between card games.
setup: Queue the song on a speaker or phone.
Everyone has a drink in hand before you press play.
For Roxanne, split into two teams of 2. For Thunderstruck, pick who holds the drink first and the direction.
rules: Roxanne (The Police, about 3 min): Team A drinks every time the word Roxanne is sung. Team B drinks every time the words red light are sung. The song ends and so does the game.
Thunderstruck (AC/DC, about 5 min): one player starts drinking at the first thunder. They keep drinking until the next thunder, then the player on their left takes over.
Thunderstruck: the drink passes on every thunder. Whoever is holding it when the song ends finishes their drink.
Sweet Caroline (Neil Diamond, about 3 min): everyone drinks on every so good in the chorus, and everyone shouts the three-beat crowd chant after the title line.
In all three, you can stop and swap to water whenever you want. These are sprints, not endurance tests.
Each song is one game. Pick a different one for the next round.
drinkTriggers: Roxanne: your team's cue word is sung, drink 1 sip each time
Thunderstruck: you are holding the drink, drink continuously until the next thunder
Thunderstruck: holding the drink when the song ends, finish it
Sweet Caroline: every so good, drink 1 sip
variations: Roxanne solo: no teams, everyone drinks on Roxanne only, which is about 27 sips.
Thunderstruck choose your victim: when your turn ends you pick who drinks next instead of passing left.
Thunderstruck endurance: loop the song; anyone who taps out is out, and the last one standing wins.
watchOut: Roxanne has the cue word roughly 27 times in 3 minutes, so the Roxanne team gets hammered; swap teams for round two. Thunderstruck has long stretches between cues in the verses, which means one person drinks for 20 plus seconds. These are heavy; one song is plenty.
duration: 3 to 5 min per song
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. Roxanne teams of 2 work well. Thunderstruck with 4 means each player gets the drink about 8 times, which is a lot; consider sips not chugs.
notes: No authoritative source was found for the Sweet Caroline version; the so good cue is the widely played house rule. The Roxanne two-team rule is confirmed across several party guides but none is authoritative. The count of about 27 Roxannes is from memory and unverified.

name: Wisest Wizard
howToPlay: Tape each empty can to the last to build a staff. The longest staff is the Wisest Wizard and can make others drink.
tip: Set a height limit.
setup: Get a roll of strong tape (duct or packing tape) and plenty of canned beer.
Agree the boss level: usually every 5 cans means a shot before you can continue.
Play somewhere with room to stand and swing a staff, ideally outdoors.
rules: Everyone drinks their own cans at their own pace.
When you finish a can, tape your next can on top of the empty before you open it. The stack is your staff.
Every can is one level. You must carry your staff with you all night.
At each boss level (every 5 cans), take a shot before you can open the next can.
When your staff is taller than you, you are a full wizard and can make one other player drink once per can you add.
If your staff breaks or falls apart, you are out, or you start again from level 1.
At the end of the night the longest staff is the Wisest Wizard.
drinkTriggers: Every level: finish one can
Boss level (every 5 cans): 1 shot
A full wizard points at you: drink 1
Saying you are drunk: chug a beer that does not count toward your staff (feeling wise rule)
variations: White wizard duel: at level 10 you become a white wizard. When another player reaches level 10 you duel with staffs, and whoever breaks the other's staff takes the title.
No bosses: skip the shots entirely, which makes this just a beer count with a trophy.
watchOut: This is an all-night endurance game and the boss shots turn it heavy fast. A staff taller than a person is 10 plus cans, so most 4 person groups should set a height limit like 6 cans and call it there. Needs space and gets sticky.
duration: Runs all night; 2 to 4 hours
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4 since everyone plays solo and compares. It is really a party-wide game, so with 4 the fun is the ridiculous staffs more than the competition.
notes: The power to make others drink is a common house rule and is not in the Wikipedia article; the seed description includes it so it is kept as a once-per-can limit.

name: Pizza Box Game
needs: An empty pizza box, a marker, a coin
howToPlay: Each player draws a circle with their name. Flip the coin onto the box. Land on a name, that person drinks. Land on blank space, draw a new circle with a new rule.
tip: The box fills up over the night and gets wild.
setup: Eat the pizza. Open the empty box flat on the table.
Each player writes their name on the box and draws a circle around it.
Get a marker and a coin, and pick who flips first.
rules: On your turn, flip or bounce the coin onto the box.
Lands in someone's name circle: that person drinks.
Lands in your own name: you drink.
Lands on blank box: draw a circle around where the coin landed and write a new rule or dare in it. Anything goes: finish your drink, swap shirts, sing a chorus.
Lands in a rule circle: you do what it says.
Lands on a line between two circles: both apply (group decides if unclear).
Coin misses the box completely: you drink and your turn is over.
Pass the coin to the left. Keep going until the box is full of circles, then stop or start a fresh box.
drinkTriggers: Coin lands in a name: that person drinks 1
Coin lands in your own name: drink 1
Coin lands in a rule: follow the rule, usually a drink
Coin misses the box: drink 1 and lose the turn
variations: Shapes: draw any shape you like instead of a circle, so the box fills with weird overlapping zones.
Trace your cup: draw name circles by tracing the bottom of your drink, which keeps circles small and makes misses more common.
Two tries: you get two flips per turn, and only drink if both miss the box.
watchOut: Early rounds are dull because most of the box is blank. Later the box is all rules and every flip costs someone. With 4 players, 4 names take up little space, so expect a lot of rule writing before it bites.
duration: 30 to 60 min per box
playerSweetSpot: Fine with 4. Rules pages say 6 to 10 is ideal, but 4 works; you just end up writing more rules each and it takes longer for the box to fill.

links.label: Bar Games 101: Pizza Box drinking game

notes: Sources disagree on misses: one says a miss costs a drink and the turn, another gives two tries. The one-try version is the main rule; the other is in variations. Landing on a line is not covered by sources; both-apply is a common house ruling.

name: Two Truths and a Lie
howToPlay: Say three things about yourself: two true, one false. Everyone else votes on which is the lie. Wrong guessers drink; if everyone guesses right, you drink.
tip: With 4 you get three guessers, so make the lie something they half know about you.
setup: Sit in a circle with a drink each.
Give everyone a minute to think of two truths and a lie.
Pick who goes first.
rules: On your turn, say three statements about yourself in any order. Two are true and one is a lie.
Count down three, two, one. On one, everyone else holds up 1, 2, or 3 fingers for the statement they think is the lie.
Reveal the lie.
Everyone who guessed wrong drinks.
If every guesser got it right, you drink instead.
The player to your left goes next.
The game ends when everyone has had a turn. Play more rounds if people still have good material.
drinkTriggers: Guessed the wrong statement: drink 1
Everyone guessed right: the teller drinks 2
Nobody guessed right: the teller gets to hand out 1 extra drink
variations: Three lies bluff: tell three outlandish things that all sound false so the guessers have to pick which one is actually true, then explain it.
Story time: whoever guesses right can ask the teller to tell the full story behind one of the truths.
watchOut: Works best early when people are still sharp. Friends who know each other well find it too easy, so steer toward childhood or travel stories rather than recent stuff.
duration: About 2 to 3 min per turn; 10 to 15 min per round of 4
playerSweetSpot: Ideal with 4. Three guessers is enough for a real vote and each person gets several turns in an evening.
