name: Questions Only
howToPlay: Have a conversation where every line must be a question. Make a statement, hesitate, repeat a question, or answer with a rhetorical question and you drink. Pairs face off; loser steps out and the next player steps in.
tip: With 4, run it as a round robin so each pair plays everyone once.
setup: Pick two players to start. The other two watch and judge.
Agree on a topic for the first bout, like last weekend.
Decide how many fouls lose a bout, usually first to 3.
rules: Player one asks a question on the topic. Player two must reply with a question, and so on, as fast as you can.
A foul is: making a statement, hesitating, repeating a question already asked, asking a rhetorical question, or asking something unrelated.
The two judges call fouls. Fouled player drinks and the other player scores a point.
First to 3 points wins the bout. The loser steps out and a judge steps in against the winner.
Keep rotating until everyone has played everyone, or until the group is done.
The player with the most bout wins at the end hands out a final drink to whoever they like.
drinkTriggers: Made a statement or hesitated: drink 1
Repeated or rhetorical question: drink 1
Lost a bout: drink 2
Judge missed an obvious foul (group decides): judge drinks 1
variations: Whole-circle version: play it around all 4 at once instead of in pairs, so each person must answer the previous question with a question to the next person.
Topic lock: fouls also include changing the subject, which makes it much harder to keep going.
watchOut: Needs attentive judges or every foul becomes an argument. Bouts between two sharp people can run long, so cap each bout at about 2 minutes.
duration: About 2 min per bout; 6 bouts for a full round robin
playerSweetSpot: Ideal with 4. Two play and two judge, which solves the refereeing problem that the game has with 2 or 3.
notes: Wikipedia describes the base game and its fouls but not a drinking version. The drink amounts here are the usual sip-per-foul house adaptation, not from a published source.

name: Picolo
howToPlay: Enter everyone's name. The app reads out rules, dares, and challenges addressed to specific players. Just follow along.
tip: Free base mode is plenty; paid packs add spicier categories.
setup: Install Picolo (free on the App Store and Google Play) on one phone.
Everyone grabs a drink and sits where they can all see the phone.
Open the app and type in every player's name.
Pick a pack. The free base pack is fine; Getting Crazy, Caliente, Bar and War are paid add-ons.
Put the phone in the middle or hand it to one reader and tap start.
rules: One prompt shows on screen at a time. Whoever has the phone reads it out loud.
The prompt names one or more players by name and tells them what to do, or gives the whole group a mini game.
If you are named, do the task, answer the question or play the mini game.
If you refuse or lose, take the number of sips written on the card.
Some cards are rules or viruses: they stick to a player or the whole table for several turns. Break the rule, drink.
A later card tells you when a virus or rule is over.
Tap for the next card. Pass the phone around or keep one reader, your choice.
There is no score and no winner. Stop when the group has had enough or the pack runs dry.
drinkTriggers: Named on a card and you do not do it: drink the sips shown on the card
Lose a group mini game: the loser or losing side drinks the amount shown
Break an active rule or virus: drink the penalty each time
Maximum penalty card: the group decides what that means, usually finish your drink
variations: Team mode: the app lets you play as teams instead of one by one, which keeps the sips spread out in a bigger group.
Paid packs (Getting Crazy, Caliente, Bar, War) change the tone of the prompts. Caliente is the flirty one; Bar is written for a night out.
watchOut: The free pack repeats after a few sessions and the premium subscription is pricey. Prompts pick names at random, so one person can get hammered early; agree up front that any card can be swapped for a sip.
duration: About 1 min per card; 20 to 40 min per session
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal. Every name comes up often, the group challenges work, and nobody waits long for a turn.

Remote play: share the screen on a video call and let one person flip; skip the cards that need people in the same room.
watchOut: It is a plain card flipper, so it is only as fun as the group reading it. The cookie and age prompts appear every visit as a guest.
duration: About 30 sec per card; 20 to 30 min to get through the deck
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal. Vote cards need at least 3 and name call-outs come around often.
notes: Checked in a browser in Oct 2026: free, 100+ cards as a guest, extra 50 free with a login, Add players or Quick start, then flip the card and do what it says, with some cards lasting multiple turns. I stopped at the age gate rather than accept it, so I did not see the cards themselves; sip counts above are typical values. The site operator is not named on the page.

name: Heads Up!
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: Hold the phone on your forehead; teammates describe the word. Each pass is a drink for the guesser; the describers drink for every word missed in the round.
tip: Paid app ($1.99), some packs cost extra.
setup: Buy and open Heads Up! on one phone (paid app, about $1.99 on the App Store as of Oct 2026, extra decks cost more).
Split into two teams of two, or play one guesser against three describers.
Pick a deck everyone knows (Act It Out, Celebrities, Accents, or a friend-group custom deck).
Everyone has a drink in hand and the guesser sets theirs down.
Agree on the drink sizes before the timer starts: a sip per word, nothing bigger.
rules: The guesser holds the phone flat against their forehead with the screen facing the others.
A word appears. The describers shout clues without saying the word or any part of it.
Guesser gets it right: tilt the phone down. Correct. Next word.
Guesser is stuck: tilt the phone up to pass. Next word.
The round is 60 seconds. When the timer ends the app shows the score and a replay video.
Rotate the guesser clockwise. Everyone guesses once per deck.
After everyone has guessed, compare scores. Lowest scorer that round takes the big penalty.
Play as many decks as you like. Swap decks every rotation so nobody memorizes cards.
drinkTriggers: Each pass: the guesser drinks 1.
Each word the guesser missed or timed out on: all describers drink 1.
Describer says the word or part of it: that describer drinks 2 and the word is skipped.
Lowest score of the rotation: finish your drink or take 5 sips.
Guesser scores 10 or more in one round: hand out 3 sips to anyone.
variations: Team mode: two teams of two alternate rounds. Losing team drinks the difference in words, one sip per word.
Replay roast: watch the recorded replay after each round. Anyone caught making a stupid face drinks 1.
Charades only: use the Act It Out deck, no talking allowed. Every spoken clue is a drink for the speaker.
watchOut: Passing in a panic stacks up fast for the guesser, so cap passes at 3 drinks per round. Describers shouting over each other is the whole fun but gets loud.
duration: About 1 min per round plus replay; a 4-person rotation takes 6 to 8 min, play 3 or 4 decks
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: one guesser and three describers means constant clues, and a 2v2 team mode works cleanly.

links.label: Heads Up! on the App Store

notes: App Store listing confirmed at $1.99 with in-app deck purchases ($1.99 each) and an update on Oct 2026. Google Play page confirmed as the Warner Bros listing updated Oct 14, 2026 with in-app purchases; the Play Store price could not be read from the page and is assumed to also be about $1.99 (unverified).

name: Psych!
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: Everyone writes a fake answer to a trivia question, then votes for the real one. Pick a fake, drink. Fool someone, give a drink.
tip: The "And the Truth Comes Out" category is built for friend groups.
setup: Install Psych! Outwit Your Friends on one phone (free with ads, extra decks are in-app purchases).
One person hosts a game and chooses a deck. Three base decks are free; And the Truth Comes Out costs about $1.99.
Pass-and-play works on a single phone: each player enters their name when prompted.
Everyone has a drink and keeps it within reach.
Agree on the number of rounds (the app defaults to a short set, 5 to 7 questions).
rules: The phone shows a question. Pass the phone around and each player secretly types a fake answer.
The app mixes the fakes with the real answer and shows the full list.
Pass the phone again. Each player picks the answer they think is real.
The app reveals the truth and who picked what.
Points go to anyone who picked the real answer and to anyone whose fake fooled someone.
Drink according to the reveal, then hit next for the following question.
After the last question the app shows final scores. Lowest total takes the end penalty.
drinkTriggers: You picked a fake answer: drink 1.
Your fake fooled someone: give 1 drink per person fooled.
You picked your own fake by mistake: drink 2.
Nobody picked the real answer: everyone drinks 1.
Lowest score at the end: finish your drink.
variations: And the Truth Comes Out deck: questions are about the players themselves. The person the question is about drinks 1 for every fake that got more votes than the truth.
Doubles: if two players write the same fake, both drink 1 for lack of imagination.
watchOut: Typing on one shared phone slows the game down; keep decks to 5 or 6 questions. The app has not had a major update since 2023, so expect ads and the odd crash.
duration: About 2 min per question; 10 to 15 min per deck
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine: three fakes plus the truth is enough to fool people. It is funnier with 5 or 6 but 4 still works.
notes: App Store listing confirmed free with in-app purchases including And The Truth Comes Out at $1.99; latest listed version is from Aug 2023. Google Play page confirmed as the Warner Bros listing with ads and in-app purchases, last updated May 2026.

name: Charades! / Reverse Charades
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: 2v2 timed rounds. Losing team drinks per word short of the winners.
tip: Reverse Charades (three act, one guesses) is funnier.
setup: Install Charades! by FatChicken Studios on one phone (free with ads, Remove Ads is $0.99).
Split into two teams of two.
Pick a deck both teams agree on (Movies, Animals, Actions are the easy ones).
Set the timer to 60 seconds in the app settings.
Everyone gets a drink. Actors put theirs down before each round.
rules: Team A goes first. One player holds the phone to their forehead, screen facing their teammate.
The teammate acts out the word with no talking. The phone holder guesses.
Correct guess: tilt the phone down. Pass: tilt it up.
When the timer ends, note the score. Then Team B plays the same way.
After both teams have played, compare scores. The lower score loses the round.
Swap guesser and actor within each team every round.
Reverse Charades mode: one player guesses while the other three act together. Rotate the guesser.
Play to a set number of rounds, usually 4 or 6, and tally total words.
drinkTriggers: Losing team each round: drink 1 per word short of the winners.
Any spoken word or sound from the actor: actor drinks 1 and the word is passed.
Each pass: guesser drinks 1.
Tie: both teams drink 1.
Reverse Charades, guesser scores under 3: guesser drinks 3.
variations: Reverse Charades (three act, one guesses) is the funnier version with 4. Everyone acts at once and the guesser is never idle.
Free-for-all: no teams. Each person guesses once with the other three acting. Lowest single score finishes their drink.
Heads Up! works the same way if you already own it, just use its Act It Out deck.
watchOut: Needs a bit of standing room for acting. The free app shows ads between rounds, which kills momentum; paying $0.99 to remove them is worth it for a party.
duration: About 1 min per round; 10 to 15 min for 6 rounds
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: clean 2v2 teams, and Reverse Charades with three actors and one guesser is at its best.
notes: App Store listing confirmed free with in-app purchases (Remove Ads $0.99); last listed update is Oct 2023. Did not verify a separate official Reverse Charades app, so the entry treats reverse charades as a way to play the same app.

name: Cards Against Humanity (web)
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: Pass the device; each player picks a card, the Czar picks a winner, losers drink.
tip: Sites like allbad.cards run it free.
setup: Open a free online Cards Against Humanity clone on one phone or laptop. Pretend You're Xyzzy (pretendyoure.xyz) is the long-running one the official CAH site points to.
Create a game and set it to the number of players, or just use one browser tab and pass the device.
If the site insists on separate players, open one tab per player on the same laptop and switch tabs on each turn.
Pick who is Card Czar first, usually whoever most recently bought a round.
Everyone fills a drink.
rules: The Czar reads the black card out loud.
Pass the device around. Each of the other three players picks a white card from their hand without showing anyone.
The device goes to the Czar, who reads all the answers out loud without knowing who played what.
The Czar picks the funniest answer. That player wins the black card.
The two losing players drink. Pass the Czar role clockwise.
First to 5 black cards wins. Everyone else finishes a round of drinks to close out.
drinkTriggers: Your card was not picked: drink 1.
Your card made the Czar laugh out loud but still lost: drink 1 anyway, it is a cruel game.
Czar picks a card and admits they did not get it: Czar drinks 2.
Winner of the round: give 2 sips to anyone.
Game winner at 5 black cards: everyone else finishes their drink or takes 5 sips.
variations: Pass-and-play by hand: deal 7 white cards each on screen, read them aloud yourself and let the Czar judge from memory. Faster than tab-switching.
Haiku rule: on a black card marked Pick 3, losers drink 3 instead of 1.
Rebuttal: a losing player can read a second card to argue their case. If the Czar changes their mind, the original winner drinks 2; if not, the challenger drinks 2.
watchOut: Online clones are built for one device per player, so the pass-around flow is clunky; two tabs per person is already too fiddly after a few drinks. If it drags, the physical game or printed PDF is smoother.
duration: About 2 min per black card; 15 to 25 min to 5 cards
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine: three answers per round is the minimum for real choice. More players is funnier but 4 keeps rounds quick.
notes: allbad.cards (named in the seed tip) did not resolve at all as of Oct 2026 and appears to be offline, so it is listed as unverified. Pretend You're Xyzzy loaded and describes itself as a Cards Against Humanity clone still in development; the official CAH site links to it while saying it cannot vouch for it. Neither clone offers a true single-device pass-and-play mode.

name: Bomb Party (JKLM.fun)
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: Say a word containing the given syllable before the bomb goes off. Explode and drink.
tip: Also works with one device per person.
setup: Open jklm.fun on one phone or laptop and tap Start a new room, then pick Private.
Choose BombParty from the game list and join as a guest with one shared name.
Only one player needs to be in the room; the others play by voice and take turns at the keyboard.
Set the dictionary to English and leave the default bomb timer.
Sit in a circle so the device can be passed quickly. Drinks within reach.
rules: The screen shows a short syllable like ING or TRA and a lit fuse.
The player holding the device types a word containing that syllable and hits enter before the bomb explodes.
Valid word: pass the device to the next player, who gets a new syllable.
Bomb explodes while you are holding it: you lose a life and drink.
Words already used in the round do not count. Try again fast.
A round ends when the shared player runs out of lives. Note who caused each explosion.
Start a new round. Play 5 rounds and count explosions per person.
drinkTriggers: Bomb explodes in your hands: drink 2.
You submit a word that is not in the dictionary: drink 1 and keep going.
You reuse a word from this round: drink 1.
You use every letter of the alphabet and earn a bonus life: give 2 sips.
Most explosions after 5 rounds: finish your drink.
variations: Spoken only: nobody types. Each player says their word out loud before the bomb goes off and the device holder types nothing; a referee judges and the holder presses enter on any valid word to pass.
One device each: everyone joins the same private room with the code on the screen. The app tracks lives per person and whoever gets eliminated first finishes their drink.
Hard mode: turn the timer down in room settings. Every explosion is 3 sips.
watchOut: Passing one device around is slower than the bomb timer likes, so hand it over the instant your word is accepted. Gets heavy fast once everyone is tipsy and blanking on words.
duration: About 2 to 4 min per round; play 5 rounds in 15 min
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal for the pass-around version: the device comes back to you every 15 seconds or so, which is enough time to think but not relax.
notes: jklm.fun confirmed as the host of BombParty with free guest play and private rooms. The site does not state pricing anywhere, but no paid tier was visible.

name: Skribbl.io (passed around)
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: One person draws, others guess out loud. Last to guess or nobody guessing drinks.
tip: Better with one device each.
setup: Open skribbl.io on one laptop and click Create Private Room.
Set rounds to 3 and draw time to 60 seconds. Add custom words about your friend group if you like.
Only one player needs to join; the others guess out loud.
Put the laptop where everyone can see the screen but only the drawer can reach the trackpad or mouse.
Everyone has a drink.
rules: The drawer picks one of the three words the game offers.
The drawer draws on the laptop. The other three shout guesses out loud.
The drawer may not speak, write letters, or write numbers.
First correct shout wins the word. The drawer types it in to end the turn, or lets the timer run out.
If nobody gets it before the timer ends, everyone who guessed loses.
Pass the laptop clockwise. Next player draws.
A game is one full rotation, 4 drawings. Play 3 games.
drinkTriggers: Last of the three guessers to get the word, or anyone who never got it: drink 1.
Nobody guesses the word: drawer drinks 2, everyone else drinks 1.
Drawer writes a letter or number, or talks: drawer drinks 2.
First guess within 10 seconds: drawer gives 2 sips.
Fewest correct guesses after 3 games: finish your drink.
variations: One device each: everyone joins the private room with the link. The game scores automatically; lowest score each round drinks 2, lowest at the end finishes their drink.
Custom words only: tick Use custom words exclusively and fill the list with inside jokes. Any word nobody guesses makes the person who wrote it drink.
watchOut: Drawing on a trackpad is awful; bring a mouse. The seed tip is right that it is better with one device each, but the pass-around version works fine if the screen is big.
duration: About 1 min per drawing; 5 min per rotation of 4, play 3 rotations
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine: three guessers is enough competition and the drawer comes around often. With one device each it scales up better.

name: Trivia (Sporcle, Trivia Crack, quiz sites)
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: Run a Sporcle quiz like "name all 50 states" or "name every NBA team". Every miss, everyone drinks. Or play Trivia Crack and drink per wrong answer.
tip: Make a custom Sporcle quiz about your friend group.
setup: Open sporcle.com on one laptop and find a list quiz everyone can play together: 50 States, Countries of Europe, NBA Teams, Harry Potter Characters.
Sporcle is free to play with ads; a membership removes ads and is optional.
Pick a scribe who types what the group shouts. Rotate the scribe each quiz.
Decide team or solo: for 4, play as one team against the quiz, or 2v2 on two different quizzes of the same size.
Drinks within reach, screen visible to all.
rules: Start the timer. Everyone shouts answers and the scribe types them.
Each correct answer fills a slot. Wrong answers just do nothing.
When the timer ends, the quiz shows what you missed.
Count the misses. That is the drinking total for the group.
Next quiz, new scribe. Each player picks one quiz per game.
Trivia Crack option: open the app, play a solo match and pass the phone each question. The person holding the phone answers.
In Trivia Crack, a wrong answer is on the person who tapped it.
drinkTriggers: Sporcle, each item the group missed: everyone drinks 1 (cap at 10).
Sporcle, a player shouts an answer that is already on the board: that player drinks 1.
Sporcle, 100 percent: nobody drinks, and the scribe hands out 3 sips.
Trivia Crack, wrong answer: the person who answered drinks 2.
Trivia Crack, losing a crown question: drink 3.
variations: Custom quiz: anyone with a free Sporcle account can build a quiz about the friend group (every roommate you have had, every bar on your street). Misses count double.
2v2: each team gets the same quiz back to back. Team with fewer correct drinks the difference.
Minefield quizzes: a wrong click ends the quiz. The clicker finishes their drink.
watchOut: A 50-item quiz you half know means 20 misses, which is way too much. Use the cap and pick quizzes near your level. Trivia Crack pushes ads and in-app purchases hard.
duration: About 3 to 5 min per quiz; 20 to 30 min per game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: one team shouting together covers the gaps in everyone's knowledge, and 2v2 is a clean split.
notes: Sporcle confirmed free to play with optional paid membership to remove ads. The Trivia Crack site loaded with that title but gave almost no details; the app is free with ads and in-app purchases as of the last time it could be checked (unverified).

name: Spin the Wheel (any wheel site)
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: Load a wheel with rules and penalties. Spin on your turn.
tip: Great for "what do we play next".
setup: Open wheelofnames.com (free, ad supported) on a phone or laptop.
Delete the sample entries and type your own, one per line: Drink 2, Give 2, Everyone drinks, Waterfall, Truth, Dare, Safe, Pick next game.
Aim for 10 to 16 slices with about a third of them Safe or Give so it is not all punishment.
Optional: add each player's name as a slice so the wheel can pick a victim.
Put drinks within reach and sit where everyone can see the screen.
rules: Go clockwise. On your turn, tap the wheel to spin it.
Do whatever the slice says. No re-spins.
If the slice names a drink, drink it now before the next spin.
If the slice is a Dare or Truth, do it or drink 3 instead.
If the slice is Pick next game, you choose the next game from this list and the wheel is done.
Otherwise, pass the device to the next player.
Play until everyone has spun 3 times, or until the wheel sends you to another game.
drinkTriggers: Drink 2 slice: drink 2.
Give 2 slice: hand 2 sips to anyone.
Everyone drinks: all 4 drink 1.
Waterfall: start drinking; the player to your left cannot stop until you do, and so on.
Refused dare or truth: drink 3.
Spin lands on your own name: drink 3.
variations: Game picker: fill the wheel with game names from this app and spin to decide what to play next. The spinner drinks 1 for luck.
Shot wheel: replace sips with shot types and mixers. Heavy; use only a couple of real slices and lots of Safe.
Advanced mode on wheelofnames lets you weight slices, so make Safe twice as likely as Finish your drink.
watchOut: The wheel is only as sane as the slices you put on it. One Finish your drink slice on a 10-slice wheel hits someone every few spins; keep heavy slices rare.
duration: About 30 sec per spin; 5 to 10 min per game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine: turns come around fast and name slices still land on someone else most of the time. Works at any count.

name: YouTube challenge videos
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: "Guess the song in 1 second", "impossible quiz", lyrics quizzes. Everyone shouts; wrong or last drinks.
tip: Endless supply.
setup: Put YouTube on the TV or a laptop with the speaker turned up.
Search for a quiz video: guess the song in 1 second, finish the lyric, guess the movie from one frame, guess the logo.
Pick a video with 20 to 30 questions so it ends in about 10 min.
Decide a scorekeeper or just count drinks as you go.
Everyone has a drink and sits facing the screen.
rules: Play the video. Each question shows a clip and then a pause.
Everyone shouts their answer during the pause. First clear answer counts.
Pause the video if you need a ruling on who said it first.
The video reveals the answer. Drink according to the reveal.
Keep going until the video ends.
Whoever got the most right picks the next video.
After 3 videos, add up totals. Lowest total takes the end penalty.
drinkTriggers: You shouted a wrong answer: drink 1.
Nobody got it: everyone drinks 1.
You got it first: give 1 sip.
You got it first three times in a row: give 3 and someone else picks the next video.
Lowest total after 3 videos: finish your drink.
variations: Silent round: write answers on your phone and reveal together. Wrong answers drink 2, no first-shout bonus.
Era rule: pick a decade video (90s hits, 2010s hits). Anyone born after the decade drinks double for wrong answers.
Impossible quiz: play a deliberately brutal quiz. Every miss is 1 sip for the group, cap at 10 per video.
watchOut: Shout-out scoring causes arguments, so name a referee or play the silent variation. Skip ads with Premium or the pacing dies.
duration: About 10 min per video; 30 min for a 3-video set
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: shouting over three other people is chaotic enough to be fun and small enough to hear who was first.

name: GeoGuessr (free mode)
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: Pass the laptop; each person places a guess. Farthest from the real location drinks.
tip: Country-only mode speeds it up.
setup: Open geoguessr.com on one laptop and sign in with a free account.
As of Oct 2026 the free tier is limited: a free daily challenge plus a small number of games per day, with Pro (about $7 a month, unverified) unlocking unlimited play.
Start a classic world game or the daily challenge. Set no time limit so the laptop can be passed.
Sit in a circle. Everyone has a drink.
Agree on scoring: use the game's own distance score per guess.
rules: The screen drops you somewhere in street view. Everyone looks together for 30 seconds without touching the controls.
Pass the laptop to player 1. They can move and look around for 30 seconds, then place a pin on the map but do not confirm.
Take a screenshot or write down their guess, then clear the pin and pass to player 2. Repeat for all four.
After all four have guessed, confirm the last pin to reveal the real location.
Compare each guess to the real spot on the map. Farthest drinks.
Next round. A game is 5 rounds.
After 5 rounds, whoever was farthest most often takes the end penalty.
drinkTriggers: Farthest guess of the round: drink 2.
Second farthest: drink 1.
Wrong continent: drink 3 instead.
Closest guess within 50 km: give 2 sips.
Farthest most often after 5 rounds: finish your drink.
variations: Country only: each player just names a country out loud, no pins. Wrong country drinks 2, right country gives 1. Much faster.
One confirmed guess: skip the pass-around and let one player per round place the pin after group discussion. If the group is more than 1000 km off, everyone drinks 2.
Party mode with Pro: GeoGuessr party and battle royale modes let everyone join from their phones; lowest score each round drinks 2.
watchOut: The free tier is thin now, so expect to hit the daily limit after a couple of games; the Country only variation needs no pins and stretches it. Pass-around guessing with hidden pins is fiddly, so write guesses on paper.
duration: About 3 min per round; 15 to 20 min per 5-round game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine: four guesses per round give a clear farthest and closest without the pass-around taking forever.
notes: GeoGuessr's own pages confirm a free daily game and that a free account can play a limited number of games per day, with Pro unlocking unlimited play. The exact Pro price was not confirmed from the official site; third-party pages list around $6.99 a month (unverified).

name: NYT Games (Wordle, Connections, Mini Crossword)
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: Pass the phone around taking turns. Every wrong guess the group makes means everyone drinks.
tip: Good "winding down" game.
setup: Open the NYT Games app (free with in-app subscription) or nytimes.com/games on one phone.
Wordle and Connections are playable free each day; the Mini is free on the day, the archive needs a subscription.
Sit in a circle and pass the phone clockwise. Everyone has a drink.
Pick an order: Wordle first, then Connections, then the Mini.
Agree that the group shares one attempt per puzzle, so nobody should have played today's puzzle already.
rules: Wordle: each player in turn types one 5-letter guess. Discuss, but the phone holder decides.
After each guess, read the colors out loud. Drink according to the result.
Keep rotating until the word is solved or the 6 guesses run out.
Connections: each player in turn submits one group of four. A wrong submission counts as a mistake.
Four mistakes ends Connections. Solved groups are safe.
Mini Crossword: pass the phone after every filled clue. Wrong letters cost drinks when the puzzle is checked.
After all three puzzles, whoever caused the most drinks takes the end penalty.
drinkTriggers: Wordle guess with no green letters: the guesser drinks 1.
Wordle fail after 6 guesses: everyone drinks 3.
Wordle solved: the solver gives 1 sip per guess remaining.
Connections wrong group: the submitter drinks 1; one away drinks only a sip.
Connections purple group solved first: the submitter gives 2 sips.
Mini: each wrong square at the end, the person who filled it drinks 1.
Most drinks caused across all three: finish your drink.
variations: Everyone drinks: the seed rule. Any wrong guess by anyone means all 4 drink 1. Simpler, heavier.
Race: with a subscription, play the Mini one at a time with the timer on. Slowest time finishes their drink.
Spelling Bee: pass the phone, each player must find one new word in 30 seconds or drink 1. Reaching Genius means everyone gives 2.
watchOut: This is a wind-down game, not a party starter. Puzzles reset at midnight local time, so if someone already played today you are stuck with Connections only.
duration: About 10 to 15 min for all three puzzles
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine: Wordle's 6 guesses rotate well through 4 people and Connections' 4 groups split evenly.

The web page redirected to the NYT crosswords hub which lists all three games; which puzzles are free without a subscription could not be confirmed from the page itself and is based on current public knowledge (unverified).

name: Akinator
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: Think of a character. If Akinator guesses it, you drink. If it fails, everyone else drinks.
tip: Obscure characters are the strategy.
setup: Open en.akinator.com in a browser or install the free Akinator app (Elokence) on one phone.
Sit in a circle. Decide who goes first.
Everyone has a drink.
Agree on a time cap: if Akinator has not guessed after 25 questions, the round is over.
rules: The player whose turn it is thinks of a real or fictional character and says it out loud to nobody.
They hold the phone and answer Akinator's yes, no, probably, probably not, or don't know questions.
Everyone else watches the questions and tries to guess the character before Akinator does.
If Akinator guesses right, the player admits it and drinks.
If Akinator guesses wrong, say no and continue. Akinator gets 3 wrong guesses total.
If Akinator is still wrong after 3 guesses or 25 questions, the player wins and everyone else drinks.
Pass the phone clockwise. Each player goes twice.
drinkTriggers: Akinator guesses your character: drink 2, plus 1 more if it took under 15 questions.
Akinator fails: everyone else drinks 2.
Another player shouts the right character before Akinator: the thinker drinks 3 and the shouter gives 2.
A wrong shout: the shouter drinks 1.
Akinator nails it with a first guess under 10 questions: the thinker finishes their drink.
variations: Objects and animals modes: same rules, different categories. Harder for Akinator, so the group drinks more.
Lie allowed: the thinker may answer one question falsely. If Akinator still wins, they drink double.
Friend mode: think of someone in the room. If Akinator somehow gets it (it has entries for your boyfriend, your older brother and so on), everyone drinks 3.
watchOut: Obscure characters make the rounds long and the group restless; the 25-question cap keeps it moving. Akinator needs an internet connection and the app pushes premium potions.
duration: About 2 to 4 min per round; 15 to 20 min for two rounds each
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine: one person plays while three watch and shout guesses, and the phone comes back around before anyone gets bored.
notes: The Akinator website blocks automated fetches but loaded in a browser and is the Elokence site, free to play. App Store listing confirmed free with in-app purchases, updated Oct 2026.

name: Chrome Dino / Flappy Bird
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: Pass it around. Lowest score drinks.
tip: Harder than it sounds after round three.
setup: On a laptop, type chrome://dino in Chrome's address bar. On a phone, open flappybird.io or any Flappy Bird clone in the browser.
Sit in a circle. Pass the device clockwise.
Everyone has a drink.
Decide the number of rounds, usually 3.
rules: On your turn, play one run. Space or tap to jump.
When you die, read your score out loud and pass the device.
After all four have played, the lowest score drinks.
Start the next round. Order stays the same.
After 3 rounds, add up each player's scores.
Lowest total takes the end penalty. Highest total hands out drinks.
drinkTriggers: Lowest score of the round: drink 2.
Second lowest: drink 1.
Die within 3 seconds (Flappy Bird under 1 pipe, Dino under 100 points): drink 3.
New group high score: give 3 sips.
Lowest total after 3 rounds: finish your drink.
variations: Drink and play: you must take a sip every time the Dino passes 100 points, without pausing. Dying while drinking is 2 extra.
Elimination: lowest score is out each round. Last player standing gives out 5 sips.
Off-hand: play with your non-dominant hand. Any score under 10 finishes a drink.
watchOut: Skill gap gets obvious by round two and the same person keeps drinking; the elimination variation evens it out. Dino runs can go long for good players, so cap a run at 60 seconds.
duration: About 30 sec to 1 min per turn; 10 to 15 min for 3 rounds
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine: short turns mean nobody waits long, and four scores give a clear bottom two.
notes: flappybird.io loaded with the title Play Flappy Bird Online, Free, No Download, but the game itself renders in JavaScript so gameplay could not be confirmed from the fetch.

name: Google Feud
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: Open googlefeud.com, pick a category, and the site shows the start of a real Google search. Pass the device around guessing how Google autocompletes it; the top ten answers score, wrong guesses are strikes and drinks.
tip: With 4, play one shared board and rotate who types; the Questions and People categories are the funniest.
setup: Open googlefeud.com in a browser on one phone or laptop. It is free, ad supported.
Pick a category: Culture, People, Names, Questions, Animals, Food or Entertainment.
Sit in a circle. The device goes clockwise, one guess per hand-off.
Everyone has a drink.
rules: The screen shows a search like why does my cat with the autocomplete hidden.
The first player types one guess for how Google finishes it and hits enter.
If it is on the board of 10 answers, it flips up and scores. Higher on the board scores more.
If it is not on the board, that is a strike. The site allows 3 strikes per round.
Pass the device to the next player after every guess, hit or miss.
The round ends at 3 strikes or when the board is full.
Reveal the remaining answers. Everyone drinks per unrevealed answer.
Play 5 rounds, new category each time. Track strikes per player.
drinkTriggers: Your guess is a strike: drink 1.
Your guess is the number 1 answer: give 2 sips.
Third strike ends the round: the striker drinks 2.
Each unrevealed answer at round end: everyone drinks 1, cap 5.
Most strikes after 5 rounds: finish your drink.
variations: Teams: 2v2, alternating guesses. The team that causes the third strike drinks the number of blank answers.
Easy Mode: the site's Easy Mode shows extra hints. Use it late in the night and double every drink.
watchOut: Rounds can end in three quick strikes with the board barely revealed, which makes the unrevealed-answers rule brutal; keep the cap. The site is a parody not run by Google and sometimes loads slowly.
duration: About 2 min per round; 10 to 15 min for 5 rounds
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: guesses come around fast and three strikes spread across four people keeps everyone involved.
notes: The site loaded and shows categories and a guess counter; the exact strike count and scoring were not readable from the fetched page and are based on how the game has worked in play (unverified).

name: Quordle
subcategory: Non-drinking apps with a drinking rule
howToPlay: Quordle is Wordle times four: solve four 5-letter words at once with 9 shared guesses. Pass the phone, one guess each; a guess that helps nobody is a drink, and every unsolved word at the end is drinks for all.
tip: With 4 each player owns one of the four grids and drinks when their word is the one left unsolved.
setup: Open merriam-webster.com/games/quordle on one phone. Free, no account needed.
Choose Daily for one shared puzzle or Practice for unlimited rounds.
Sit in a circle and pass the phone clockwise.
Assign each player one of the four grids: top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right.
Everyone has a drink.
rules: Player 1 types any 5-letter word. It is checked against all four grids at once.
Read out the colors: green is right place, yellow is right letter wrong place.
Pass the phone. Each player types one guess per turn.
A guess that solves a grid is a win for whoever owns that grid.
You have 9 guesses total for all four words.
The game ends when all four are solved or the 9 guesses are used.
Drink for whatever is left unsolved. Then start a Practice round if you want more.
drinkTriggers: Your guess scored zero green and zero yellow on every grid: drink 2.
Your guess solved a grid: give 2 sips.
Your own grid is still unsolved at the end: drink 3.
All four unsolved after 9 guesses: everyone finishes their drink.
Reusing a letter already shown grey: drink 1.
variations: Plain Wordle rotation: play regular Wordle instead with the same pass-the-phone rule. Lighter and shorter.
Blind guess: the first two guesses must be made without looking at the screen. Drink 1 if it still helps, give 1 if it does not.
watchOut: Four grids on one phone screen are hard to read after a few drinks; put it on a tablet or cast it. Nine guesses go fast, so do not waste the first two.
duration: About 5 to 8 min per puzzle
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: four grids, four players, one grid each is the whole point.

name: TV show / movie drinking games
howToPlay: Pick a show and a rule sheet. The Office: drink when Michael says "that's what she said". Friends: drink when Joey eats. The Bachelor: drink on "journey". TV Tropes has a DrinkingGame page for most shows.
tip: Choose an episode everyone has seen.
setup: Pick a show or movie everyone has seen at least once, so nobody is upset about missing the plot.
Look up its rule sheet: TV Tropes has a DrinkingGame subpage for most shows and games, and reddit threads cover the rest.
Trim the sheet to 5 to 8 triggers. Any more and nobody remembers them.
Write the triggers on a card and put it where everyone can see it.
One person holds the remote and is allowed to pause for drinking.
Everyone has a full drink before pressing play.
rules: Press play. Watch like normal.
When a trigger happens, whoever spots it first shouts it. Everyone drinks the listed amount.
If people disagree whether it counted, the remote holder decides. No rewinds.
Some triggers are personal: pick a character each, and drink when your character does their thing.
At a big moment on the sheet (the catchphrase, the title drop, the kiss), everyone finishes what is in their glass.
Refill during credits or at the ad break, not mid-scene.
The game ends when the episode or movie ends.
drinkTriggers: Standard trigger on the sheet: everyone drinks 1.
Your chosen character's signature move: you drink 1, or give 1 if the sheet says so.
Catchphrase or title drop: everyone drinks 2.
Movie climax or season-finale cliffhanger: everyone finishes their drink.
Example sheet, The Office: Michael says That's what she said, drink 1; Jim looks at the camera, drink 1; Dwight says Fact, drink 1.
Example sheet, Friends: Joey eats, drink 1; Ross says We were on a break, drink 2; Janice says Oh my God, finish your drink.
variations: Bingo instead of sips: make a 4x4 card of triggers each; a full row means everyone else drinks 3. Much lighter.
Character draft: each player picks one character and only drinks for that character's triggers. Keeps drinks spread out.
Reality TV: The Bachelor, Love Island and Drag Race have the most active communities; drink on journey, connection, I'm not here to make friends.
watchOut: Sitcoms with a catchphrase every 30 seconds get heavy fast, so cut the sheet down and use a 2-hour movie rather than a 4-episode binge. TV Tropes sheets are written as jokes, not as a sane night; never use one in full.
duration: Length of the episode or movie: 20 to 45 min per episode, 90 to 120 min per movie
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: enough people to spot triggers and argue about them, few enough that the TV is not blocked by someone going to the fridge.
notes: TV Tropes blocks automated fetches but the index page loaded in a browser and links to per-show DrinkingGame subpages. Example triggers for The Office and Friends are the widely circulated community ones and were not checked against a single source.

name: Power Hour playlist
howToPlay: Play a YouTube Power Hour mix (60 one-minute clips). Shot of beer at every change.
tip: Same as the no-device Power Hour, just automated.
setup: Search YouTube for Power Hour mix and pick one with 60 one-minute song clips and an on-screen counter.
Get a shot glass per person (1 to 1.5 oz) and plenty of beer. Light beer is the standard for a reason.
Fill each shot glass with beer before the video starts.
Sit where everyone can see the screen and hear the song change.
Agree the exit rule now: anyone can stop at any time, no shame, no catch-up.
rules: Press play. The first song starts.
Every time the song changes, everyone takes one shot of beer.
Refill your shot glass right after, so it is ready for the next change.
No pausing the video. Bathroom breaks mean you miss shots, not make them up.
The video ends after 60 songs. That is one hour and 60 shots of beer, about 5 to 7 beers each.
Anyone still drinking at song 60 has finished. Everyone else is a graceful dropout.
drinkTriggers: Every song change: one shot of beer (1 to 1.5 oz).
Miss a change because you were not paying attention: no catch-up, just drink the next one.
Spill your shot: refill and drink it, that is all.
Optional: a song from your own suggestion comes up, give one extra shot to someone.
variations: Half hour: play 30 songs instead of 60. Much saner, still a party.
Century Club: 100 shots in 100 minutes. This is a lot and is not recommended with hard liquor under any circumstances.
Mixed drinks: use a weak mixer drink instead of beer, same shot size. Easier on the stomach for people who hate beer.
watchOut: Sixty shots of beer is 5 to 7 beers in an hour, which is heavy for anyone; use light beer, eat first, and treat dropping out as normal. Never do this with spirits.
duration: 60 min exactly; 30 min for the half version
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine: Power Hour is the same at any player count, and 4 people is easy to keep an eye on each other.

name: Music Roulette
howToPlay: Shuffle a playlist. First to name artist and song is safe; the others drink.
tip: Build the playlist from everyone's top songs.
setup: Build a shared playlist on Spotify, Apple Music or YouTube: each player adds 10 to 15 songs they think the others will know.
Connect one phone to a speaker and put the playlist on shuffle.
Pick a DJ who holds the phone and can see the title; the DJ rotates each round.
Everyone has a drink.
Decide the skip rule: if nobody has it after 20 seconds, the DJ reveals it.
rules: The DJ hits play on a shuffled track without saying anything.
Everyone else listens. Shout the artist and song title as soon as you know them.
First person with both correct is safe. The DJ confirms.
The other guessers drink. The DJ does not drink or win this round.
If nobody gets it in 20 seconds, the DJ reveals it and whoever added the song drinks.
Pass the phone clockwise. New DJ, next track.
Play until the playlist runs out or 30 min, whichever comes first.
drinkTriggers: Did not name the song first: drink 1.
Got the artist but not the title, or the other way round: drink only a sip.
Nobody got it: the person who added the song drinks 2.
Wrong shout: drink 1 and you are out for that track.
You guessed your own song: drink 2, it does not count.
variations: Guess the adder: name who put the song on the playlist instead of the title. Wrong guess drinks 1, right guess gives 1.
One second: the DJ plays only the first second, then 3 seconds, then 10. Guessing on the first second gives 3 sips.
Sing it: the first guesser must sing the next line to be safe. Mumble, drink 1.
watchOut: If one person built most of the playlist they will win every round, so enforce equal song counts. Obscure picks that nobody knows drag it out; the 20-second reveal keeps it moving.
duration: About 30 sec per track; 20 to 30 min per playlist
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: three guessers racing is enough competition and the DJ role rotates fast.

name: Mario Kart
howToPlay: Drink per shell hit, finish your drink for last place, and the classic rule: you must finish a beer before the race ends but cannot drink while moving.
tip: 150cc, items on.
setup: Four controllers, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe or any Mario Kart on one console, 4-player split screen.
Settings: 150cc, items on, normal or frantic items, a 4-race Grand Prix or a custom cup.
One full beer per racer per race (half a beer each is the sane option for a 4-race cup).
Put the beers on the floor or table next to each racer, not on the couch.
Pick a scorekeeper: it does not need to be a sober referee, but someone has to track who got hit by what.
Agree on the rule set before the first race: Beerio Kart rule, item rules, or both.
rules: Beerio Kart rule: you must finish your beer before you cross the finish line, and you cannot drink while your kart is moving.
To drink, stop your kart completely, take the controller out of your hands, drink, then pick it back up.
Chug at the start, sip at each stop, or park before the finish line and chug: any strategy is fine.
Cross the finish line with beer left: you are disqualified from that race and score zero for the cup.
Item rules run on top: when you get hit, drink the listed amount after the race (or right away if your kart is stopped anyway).
The race ends when all four humans finish. Settle item drinks before the next race starts.
Last place in each race drinks the end-of-race penalty.
After the cup, lowest total points finishes a fresh drink.
drinkTriggers: Beerio Kart: finish your beer before the finish line, drinking only while fully stopped.
Hit by a green or red shell, or by a banana: drink 1.
Hit by a blue shell, a Bob-omb or lightning: drink 2.
Fall off the track: drink 2.
You used a star, bullet bill or blue shell: drink 1.
Last place at the end of the race: drink 3.
Race winner: give 2 sips.
Lowest points after the cup: finish your drink.
variations: Pure Beerio Kart: only the beer-before-the-finish rule, no item drinks. Winner is the first to cross the line with an empty can. The classic version.
Place drinks: at the end of each race drink the number of your finishing place among humans, 1st drinks 1, 4th drinks 4. Or reverse it so the winner drinks the most to handicap good players.
Once you start you cannot stop: alternate rule where you may drink while driving, but once the beer touches your lips you have to finish it in one go.
watchOut: A full beer per race across a 4-race cup is four beers in 20 minutes on top of item sips, which is heavy fast; use half beers or run the item rules only on every other race. No referee is needed, but the scorekeeper should write hits down because nobody remembers them by race three.
duration: About 3 to 4 min per race; 15 to 25 min per 4-race cup
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: full split screen with every human on the track, and position rules work cleanly with four places.

name: Mario Party
howToPlay: Drink per lost mini-game, finish your drink for last place, drink when you lose a star.
tip: Ten turns is plenty.
setup: Four controllers, any Mario Party on one console (Super Mario Party, Superstars or Jamboree all work).
Set the game to 10 turns. Fifteen is the upper limit for a drinking night.
Pick a board everyone knows. Avoid boards with long movement animations if you can.
Everyone has a drink and a backup drink within reach.
Agree on the rule set out loud before turn 1, especially the star rules.
rules: Play the board game as normal. The console runs everything.
After every minigame, the loser or losers drink. In 1v3 and 2v2 minigames the losing side drinks.
When someone buys a star, everyone else drinks.
When someone loses a star (Boo, Bowser, a bad item), that player drinks the big penalty.
Landing on a Bowser space or a bad luck space is a drink.
Items used on another player: the target drinks, not the user.
After the final turn, bonus stars are awarded. Drink for lost positions.
Last place at the end finishes their drink. Winner hands out drinks.
drinkTriggers: Lost a minigame: drink 1 (free-for-all: everyone but the winner drinks 1).
Someone buys a star: everyone else drinks 2.
You lose a star: finish your drink.
Bowser space or bad luck space: drink 1.
Could have bought a star but could not afford it: drink 1.
Hit by someone's item: drink 1.
Bonus stars at the end drop you a place: drink 2.
Last place at the end: finish your drink. Winner gives out 5 sips.
variations: Minigames only: skip the board and play the minigame mode (Mount Minigames or free play). Loser of each drinks 2, winner gives 1. Much faster.
All-CPU mode: set all four players to CPU, pick a character each, and drink whenever your CPU loses a minigame or a star. Great for people who do not want to play.
Team drinks: in 2v2 minigames the losing pair drink together and must finish at the same time.
watchOut: A 20-turn game runs over an hour and the star rules stack up: with 4 stars changing hands you can be 10 drinks deep before the last 5 turns. Keep it at 10 turns and put the finish-your-drink star rule on the half-beer scale.
duration: About 4 min per turn; 40 to 60 min for a 10-turn game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: Mario Party is built for four and every minigame format (free-for-all, 2v2, 1v3) works without CPU players.

name: Super Smash Bros
howToPlay: Drink per stock lost. Winner hands out drinks.
tip: Items on for chaos.
setup: Four controllers, Super Smash Bros. Ultimate (or Melee, Brawl, Wii U) on one console.
Set up a 4-player free-for-all, 3 stock, items on medium, no teams.
Turn off Final Smash meter unless you want the 3-sip Final Smash rule to fire often.
Pick characters. Picking the same main every match is allowed but boring.
Everyone has a drink within reach. No pausing to drink: drink between matches or when you are on the respawn platform.
rules: Play a 3-stock match. Every stock you lose is a drink.
Drink for a lost stock while you are on the respawn platform, or right after the match if you forgot.
Losing a stock to your own mistake (fell off, self-destruct, your own bomb) costs extra.
Losing a stock to a Final Smash costs extra.
The match ends when one player has stock left. Note the finishing order from the results screen.
The winner hands out drinks. Last to be eliminated drinks the loser penalty.
Play best of 5 matches, then settle the overall loser.
drinkTriggers: Lost a stock: drink 1.
Lost a stock by self-destruct or falling off: drink 2.
Lost a stock to a Final Smash: drink 3.
Used a Final Smash and KO'd nobody: drink 2.
Hit while taunting: drink 1.
Finished the match with zero KOs: finish your drink.
Match winner: give 3 sips.
Lost the most matches after 5: finish your drink.
variations: Handicap drinks: at the end of each match drink by placement reversed, winner drinks 4, 2nd drinks 3, 3rd drinks 2, 4th drinks 1. Levels out skill fast.
Timed match: 3-minute matches, KO counts. Every KO you take is a drink, every KO you deal gives 1.
Crowd rule: if the crowd chants your name, everyone else drinks 1.
watchOut: Items on means random stock losses and the sips add up; cap at 3 stock, not 5. A clear skill gap means one person drinks every match, so switch to handicap drinks if it gets lopsided.
duration: About 3 to 5 min per match; 20 to 30 min for best of 5
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: free-for-all with four humans is exactly what Smash is built for and placements give clear drink amounts.

name: Overcooked
howToPlay: Drink on every burned dish and every failed order. Everyone drinks if you fail the level.
tip: Cooperative, so nobody gets singled out.
setup: Four controllers, Overcooked or Overcooked 2 (or All You Can Eat) on one console or PC. Both support 4-player couch co-op.
Pick a level everyone has already beaten once so the drinking does not stop you from clearing it.
Everyone has a drink. Put drinks far from the controllers.
Assign loose roles before the level starts: chopper, cook, plater, washer.
Agree how many stars you are aiming for; 2 stars is a fair target when drinking.
rules: Start the level. Play as normal; the game scores you.
Every time a pan or pot burns, everyone drinks.
Every time an order times out and fails, everyone drinks.
Serving a dish nobody ordered is a drink for whoever plated it.
When the timer ends, check the star count.
Drink for every star you missed out of 3.
Zero stars means everyone finishes their drink.
Play 3 or 4 levels, then stop while you can still cook.
drinkTriggers: Burned a dish: everyone drinks 1 (the person who left the pan drinks 2).
Failed order: everyone drinks 1.
Served a dish that was not ordered: the plater drinks 1.
Dropped something in water, lava or off the map: that player drinks 1.
End of level: everyone drinks 1 per star missed.
Zero stars: everyone finishes their drink.
Three stars: nobody drinks and everyone cheers.
variations: Food words: saying the name of any ingredient out loud (onion, tomato, rice) costs a sip. You will slip up constantly.
Versus mode: 2v2 in Overcooked 2's versus levels. Losing team drinks the difference in points divided by 20.
Silent kitchen: no talking allowed for one level. Every word is a sip.
watchOut: Cooperative, so nobody is singled out, but burned dishes come in waves once everyone is tipsy and the everyone-drinks rule can run away. Cap burns at 5 drinks per level.
duration: About 4 to 6 min per level; 20 to 30 min for 4 levels
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: the kitchens are designed around four cooks and the roles split naturally.
notes: The Chuggernauts rules are heavier (3 drinks per burn, 3 per missed star); amounts here are scaled down for a 4-level session.

name: Just Dance / Wii Sports
howToPlay: Lowest score drinks.
tip: Good physical break.
setup: Any Just Dance on Switch or Wii, or Wii Sports on a Wii. Clear floor space in front of the TV.
Just Dance: one phone or Joy-Con per dancer; 4 can dance at once on Switch with the phone app.
Wii Sports: bowling and tennis are the 4-player ones; take turns on the others.
Everyone has a drink, held in the non-controller hand for Just Dance if you are brave.
Agree on 3 songs or 1 full bowling game per round.
rules: Just Dance: pick a song. All four dance. The game scores each dancer.
At the end of the song, read the scores. Lowest score drinks.
Holding your drink while dancing is allowed; spilling costs a sip.
Wii Sports bowling: play a full 10-frame game, 4 players.
Gutter balls and splits left open are drinks. Strikes hand out drinks.
Wii Sports tennis: 2v2 doubles. Losing pair drinks per game lost.
After the round, whoever lost the most songs or games takes the end penalty.
drinkTriggers: Just Dance, lowest score on a song: drink 3.
Just Dance, spilled your drink while dancing: drink 1 (and clean it up).
Just Dance, highest score: give 2 sips.
Wii Sports bowling, gutter ball: drink 2. Strike: give 2. Spare: give 1.
Wii Sports tennis, lost a game: losing pair drink 1 each.
Most losses of the round: finish your drink.
variations: The Chuggernauts Just Dance rule: everyone opens a fresh drink as the song starts and holds it the whole song. Lowest score finishes their own drink plus whatever is left of everyone else's. Heavy.
Spectator swap: if only 2 can dance, the other two call out who looked worse. The dancers' loser drinks 2, and the judges swap in next song.
Wii Sports golf or boxing: solo events. Worst score per hole or the knockout loser drinks 2.
watchOut: Needs real space and sober-ish footing; dancing with a drink in hand ends with a spill on the carpet. Keep this to 3 or 4 songs as a physical break, not the main game.
duration: About 3 min per song; 10 to 15 min per round. A bowling game is about 15 min
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine: Just Dance on Switch fits 4 dancers, Wii Sports bowling and tennis take 4, and lowest-score rules work with four scores.
