notes: Wii Sports rules are house rules without a single source; there is no widely cited Wii Sports drinking rule set.

name: Gang Beasts
howToPlay: Four wobbly jelly people brawl on rooftops, trucks and ferris wheels, trying to throw each other off. Rounds last a minute. Whoever gets knocked out drinks, and the drink size is set by a playing card flipped before the round.
tip: With 4 use free-for-all melee stages; the last one standing hands out drinks.
setup: Gang Beasts on Switch, PlayStation, Xbox or PC with 4 controllers. It supports 4 local players.
Set up a local melee match, free-for-all, best of 5.
Put a shuffled deck of playing cards on the table.
Before each round, each player flips one card face up in front of them. That is their drink count if they lose.
Everyone has a drink. Controllers down while drinking.
rules: Start the round. Grab, punch, headbutt and throw the others off the stage.
When you are knocked out, start drinking the number on your card right away. Ace is 1, face cards are 10.
Last player standing wins the round and gives out drinks.
A round that ends in a draw (everyone falls together) means nobody drinks.
Flip new cards and play the next round.
First to 3 round wins takes the match.
Whoever won zero rounds finishes their drink.
drinkTriggers: Knocked out: drink the number on your flipped card (face cards count as 10, so cap at 5 sips if you want to survive).
Round winner: give 3 sips.
Fell off by yourself with nobody touching you: drink 2 extra.
Threw someone off who was holding a ledge: give 1.
Zero round wins in the match: finish your drink.
variations: Flat rate: skip the cards. Knocked out drinks 2, winner gives 2. Simpler.
Soccer mode: 2v2 in the football stage. Flip one card per goal; the team scored on splits that many sips.
watchOut: Face cards at full value are 10 sips and three losses in a row is a disaster, so cap card value at 5. Rounds are chaotic and short, so the drinks come fast.
duration: About 1 min per round; 10 to 15 min per best-of-5 match
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: the stages are built for four-way brawls and every round ends with one clear winner.

links.label: The Chuggernauts: Gang Beasts drinking game

name: Ultimate Chicken Horse
howToPlay: A party platformer where each round everyone places one trap or platform, then all four try to run the course. You only score if you reach the goal and someone else did not. Dying on the course drinks; dying on your own trap drinks double.
tip: With 4 the scoring balance is perfect: enough people to fail and enough to make it.
setup: Ultimate Chicken Horse on Switch, PlayStation, Xbox or PC with 4 controllers. 4-player local is supported.
Pick Party mode and a familiar level. Set the score target to the default or lower.
Everyone picks an animal.
Everyone has a drink. Set it down before the run phase.
rules: Build phase: each player picks one item from the shared wheel and places it on the level.
Run phase: all four try to reach the goal at once.
You score points only if you reach the goal and at least one other player did not.
Reaching the goal when everyone makes it scores nothing, and placing a trap that kills someone scores you a bonus.
After the run, drink for how you died.
Repeat build and run until someone hits the score target and wins.
The winner gives out drinks. Lowest score finishes theirs.
drinkTriggers: Died on the course: drink 1.
Died on the trap you placed: drink 2.
Killed by someone else's trap: you drink 1 and the trap owner gives 1 sip to anyone.
Everyone reached the goal: everyone drinks 1 for a boring course.
Nobody reached the goal: everyone drinks 2.
Game winner: give 4 sips. Lowest score: finish your drink.
variations: Trap tax: placing a black hole, wrecking ball or any instant-kill item costs the placer 1 sip up front.
Free play: build a monstrous level together with no scoring. Each failed run is 1 sip, first to complete it gives 3.
watchOut: Rounds get long once the level is crowded with traps and everyone dies instantly, which means everyone drinks 2 every round; lower the score target or reset the level after 10 rounds.
duration: About 1 min per round; 15 to 25 min per game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: the game's scoring needs some players to fail and some to succeed, which happens most reliably with four.
notes: No reputable published drinking rule set exists for this game; the rules above are sane house rules built on the game's own scoring.

name: Jackbox Party Packs
needs: One laptop or TV running the game, phones to join at jackbox.tv
howToPlay: Quiplash (lose a matchup, drink), Fibbage (fooled, drink), Drawful, Trivia Murder Party (die, finish your drink), Tee K.O., Blather Round, Survive the Internet, Guesspionage, Job Job, Dictionarium. Simplest rule: last place each round drinks.
tip: The best option for exactly 4 with phones. Party Pack 3 and 7 are strong picks.
setup: One person launches a Party Pack on a laptop, console or TV box and picks a game from the pack menu.
Mirror or cast that screen to the TV so all four of you can see it, and turn the volume up.
The screen shows a 4-letter room code. Everyone else opens jackbox.tv on their phone, types the code and a name.
Wait until all four names show on the main screen, then the host presses start on the TV.
Agree on the drinking rule for this game before round one (see variations for a rule per game).
Everyone has a full drink within reach; phones stay in hand, the TV is the only shared screen.
rules: Each game runs itself. Read the prompt on the TV, answer or draw on your own phone, then vote on your phone.
Most Jackbox games are 2 or 3 rounds of about 3 to 5 minutes each, then a final round worth more points.
After every round the TV shows the standings. Apply the drinking rule you picked for that game.
At the end of the game the winner is announced. Last place finishes their drink, or takes a big gulp if you are going easy.
The winner picks the next game from the pack and becomes the new host device if you want to rotate.
drinkTriggers: Default rule for any game: last place on the scoreboard after each round drinks 2, last place at the end drinks 5.
Quiplash: lose a head to head matchup, drink 1. Get zero votes in a matchup, drink 3.
Fibbage: fall for someone's lie, drink 1. Pick the truth, hand out 1 to the player whose lie got the most votes.
Drawful 2: nobody guesses your drawing, drink 2. Fooled by a fake title, drink 1.
Trivia Murder Party 2: die on the Killing Floor, drink 3. Wrong trivia answer, drink 1.
variations: Quiplash 3 (Party Pack 7, 3 to 8 players): every matchup is a direct duel, so the loser of each matchup drinks 1 and a Quiplash (one player takes all votes) means the loser drinks 3. Best pure 4 player game in the catalogue.

Fibbage 4 (Party Pack 9, 2 to 8 players): drink 1 every time you pick a lie; the liar who fooled you hands out an extra 1. Final Fibbage doubles everything. Trivia Murder Party 2 (Party Pack 6, 1 to 8 players): wrong answer drinks 1, losing a Killing Floor minigame drinks 3, being the ghost chasing in the final round means you drink whenever the leader gains a step.

Drawful 2 (standalone or Party Pack 1, 3 to 8 players): the artist drinks 2 if nobody picks the real title; everyone who picks a fake title drinks 1. Tee K.O. (Party Pack 3) and Survive the Internet (Party Pack 4) both work the same way: lose the vote, drink 1.
watchOut: Every pack has one or two games that drag at 4 or need 5+ (skip Monster Seeking Monster and Zeeple Dome). Join problems are almost always a phone on cellular while the host is on wifi; put everyone on the same wifi.
duration: 15 to 25 min per game; a pack night is 3 or 4 games
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal. Nearly every Jackbox game runs from 3 players, and at 4 each person gets maximum screen time and every vote matters.
notes: Player counts for Quiplash 3, Fibbage 4, Drawful 2, Trivia Murder Party 2, Tee K.O. and Survive the Internet were read from the official game pages in Oct 2026. Party Pack 12 is the newest pack listed on the site.

name: AirConsole
needs: One browser as the console, phones as controllers via a code
howToPlay: Free. Has a drinking games section: Racing Wars (drink for power-ups and crashes), Tower of Babel, ClusterPuck 99 (drink on goals), Castle Hustle, Quiz (drink on wrong answers), Pad Poker, Silly World Series, Balloon Party, Tiles of Doom, and more.
tip: Nothing to install on anyone's phone.
setup: Open airconsole.com in a browser on a laptop or smart TV and let it run its quick device check.
Cast or plug that browser into the TV so it is the one big screen.
The screen shows a numeric code. Everyone opens airconsole.com on their phone and types the code; the phone becomes the gamepad.
The host picks a game from the library; the Drinking Games category is under Games.
Agree on the drinking rule for the game you picked before pressing start.
Keep phones charged and screens from locking; a locked phone drops the controller.
rules: The TV runs the game and each phone shows the controls for it: a steering pad for racing, buttons for party games, a keyboard for the quiz.
Play one match or round of whatever game you picked. Most are 2 to 5 minutes.
When the result screen comes up, apply the drinking rule for that game.
Swap games whenever you like; the phones stay connected across games.
Stop after a set number of matches or when someone taps out.
drinkTriggers: Default for any game: last place on the result screen drinks 2, winner hands out 2.
Racing Wars or PolyRacer: get hit by a power-up or crash, drink 1; finish last, drink 3.
ClusterPuck 99: concede a goal, drink 1 per goal against your team.
Quiz: every wrong answer, drink 1; lowest score at the end, finish your drink.
Pad Poker: lose a hand you bet on, drink the number of chips lost divided by 10, max 3.
variations: The Drinking Games category on airconsole.com as of Oct 2026 lists: Tower of Babel, Racing Wars, Karaoke, ClusterPuck 99, Castle Hustle, PolyRacer, The Neighborhood, Quiz, Pad Poker, Silly World Series, Rakete, Spacebot Knights, Simoria, Balloon Party, AirShields and Tiles of Doom. Any of these works at 4.
Tournament night: pick 5 games, 1 point per win, everyone who did not win a game drinks 1 after each, and the overall loser finishes a drink at the end.
watchOut: Phones on cellular lag badly; everyone needs to be on the same wifi. A phone screen that locks drops you out mid race. Some games are shallow, so rotate quickly.
duration: 3 to 5 min per match; 30 to 60 min per session
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine to ideal. Most AirConsole games are 2 to 8 players, and the racing and sports games are at their best with exactly 4 on screen.
notes: The old airconsole.com/drinking-games URL is a 404; the live category is at /games/drinking-games. The site says games are free with no card required.

name: Kahoot! / Quizizz / Blooket
needs: One laptop host, phones to join
howToPlay: Host a quiz; everyone joins with a code. Wrong answer or lowest score each round drinks.
tip: Make a custom quiz about your friend group beforehand.
setup: One person makes a free account on kahoot.com, wayground.com (the new name for Quizizz) or blooket.com and either picks a public quiz or writes a custom one about the group.
The host opens the quiz, chooses Host live or Classic mode, and puts the host screen on the TV or laptop where all four can see it.
The screen shows a game PIN or Game ID. Everyone else goes to kahoot.it, joins at wayground.com, or play.blooket.com on their phone and enters it with a nickname.
Once all four names appear in the lobby the host presses start.
Agree on the drinking rule and whether you are drinking per question or per round.
rules: A question appears on the host screen with 2 to 4 answer colours. Tap the colour on your phone before the timer runs out.
Faster correct answers score more, so guessing late is nearly as bad as guessing wrong.
After each question the host screen shows who was right and the current scoreboard.
Drink for wrong answers as you go, or wait and drink for your rank at the end of each block of 5 questions.
The quiz ends after the last question with a podium. Bottom of the podium finishes their drink.
Rotate who hosts and writes the next quiz.
drinkTriggers: Wrong answer: drink 1.
No answer before the timer: drink 2.
Lowest score after every 5 questions: drink 2.
Last place at the end: finish your drink. Winner hands out 3.
Blooket game modes with stealing (Gold Quest, Crypto Hack): get robbed, drink 1.
variations: Friend group quiz: the host writes 15 questions about things that happened to the four of you. Anyone who gets a question about themselves wrong drinks double.
Blooket Gold Quest or Fishing modes add luck on top of trivia, so the lead swings around; drink 1 every time you lose the lead.
Kahoot streak rule: 3 correct in a row lets you hand out 2.
watchOut: Kahoot's free tier limits the number of players per live game (sources say around 10, fine for 4) and keeps pushing paid upgrades. The host cannot play on Kahoot, so with 4 people one person just runs it unless the host joins from a second phone.
duration: About 10 to 15 min per 20 question quiz
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine. These tools scale to classrooms, so the only issue at 4 is that the host is often not a player; have the host join from their own phone too.
notes: quizizz.com now redirects permanently to wayground.com. The blooket.com homepage is behind a Cloudflare bot check, but the play.blooket.com join page loaded and shows the Join a Game field. The exact free-plan player cap on Kahoot could not be confirmed from kahoot.com itself.

name: Trinks
howToPlay: Multi-device drinking game app; everyone joins from their own phone and prompts go out simultaneously.
tip: Mentioned in app roundups as the multi-device option.
setup: Search the App Store or Play Store for Trinks; if it is not there, use Jackbox, AirConsole or DrunkPals instead.
If you find it, one person installs it and creates a game, which shows a room code.
Everyone else installs it, enters the code and picks a name.
Fill drinks and put all four phones face up in front of you.
rules: Prompts, quizzes and dares go out to all phones at the same time.
Answer or vote on your own phone before the timer ends.
The app announces who drinks after each prompt.
Play until the app ends the session or the group agrees to stop.
drinkTriggers: Whatever the prompt says, usually drink 1 to 3.
Last to answer a timed prompt: drink 1.
Bottom of the leaderboard after each block: drink 2.
watchOut: The app appears to be gone. Its website now shows a domain-for-sale page and no store listing could be found. Treat this entry as historical and use one of the alternatives.
duration: 20 to 40 min per session (if the app can be found)
playerSweetSpot: The developer's old blog described live multiplayer for up to 12, so 4 would have been fine.
notes: As of Oct 2026 trinksapp.com redirects to a HugeDomains for-sale page, and searches of the App Store and Google Play found no listing for Trinks. The only description found was from the developer's own old blog (live multiplayer, room code, up to 12 players, iOS and Android). Could not confirm the app still exists; it most likely does not.

name: Multiplayer Games for Drinking (App Store)
howToPlay: Multi-phone drinking mini-games.
tip: iOS.
setup: Search the App Store for Multiplayer Games for Drinking by Peter Jones; the direct link returned a not-found page in Oct 2026.
If it installs, open it on one phone, add the four names and choose a mode (Drunk, Spicy or Kiss) and the number of rounds.
Set the drink type in the settings so the app's drink amounts match what you are drinking.
Put the phone in the middle of the table; despite the name, it is a pass-around single-phone app.
rules: The app picks a player and shows a challenge.
Do the challenge, or bail and take the drink penalty.
Tap complete or bail so the app can track who did what.
Spin the built-in bottle when the app asks, and the person it lands on gets the next challenge.
After the set number of rounds the app names a winner based on completed challenges.
drinkTriggers: Bail on a challenge: drink what the app says, usually 2 or 3.
Fewest completed challenges at the end: finish your drink.
watchOut: The listing could not be loaded, so the app may have been pulled. Even when it was listed it was a single-device pass-around app, not one phone each, so it does not really belong in this category.
duration: 15 to 30 min
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine if the app exists; it lets you add as many players as you like.
notes: The App Store page for id1480583929 returned a not-found page in both the US and PY storefronts on Oct 15 2026, although search indexes and a third-party tracker still show it (free, developer Peter Jones, 17+, last update March 2026). Could not confirm it is still available. Descriptions in the indexed listing suggest a single shared phone, not per-phone multiplayer.

name: Drawful 2 (standalone)
needs: One laptop, console or TV box running Drawful 2, phones to join at jackbox.tv
howToPlay: The cheapest way into Jackbox: a single drawing game sold on its own. Everyone draws a weird prompt on their phone, the drawings go up on the TV, everyone types a fake title, then everyone votes on which title is real. Fool people, score points; get fooled, drink.
tip: At 4 every drawing gets exactly 3 fake titles plus the real one, which is the perfect amount to read out.
setup: One person buys and launches Drawful 2 (about 10 dollars on Steam, also on Switch, Xbox and PlayStation) and puts the screen on the TV.
The screen shows a 4-letter room code. Everyone opens jackbox.tv on their phone, enters the code and a name.
Turn on the optional extended timers in settings if people are already a few drinks in.
Decide on the drinking rule and have drinks ready; phones stay in hand.
Host presses start once all four names are on screen.
rules: Every player gets a different silly prompt on their phone and draws it with their finger.
One drawing goes up on the TV. Everyone except the artist types a fake title that sounds like a real prompt.
All titles plus the real one show on screen. Everyone except the artist picks the one they think is real.
Points: you score for picking the real title; you score when someone picks your fake title; the artist scores for every correct pick.
Repeat for each drawing, then a second round with new prompts, then a final round with everyone drawing the same prompt.
Highest score wins; apply the end of game drink.
drinkTriggers: Pick a fake title: drink 1.
Nobody picks your real title: artist drinks 2.
Your fake title gets 2 or more votes: hand out 2.
Last place at the end: finish your drink.
variations: Write your own prompts: Drawful 2 lets you enter custom prompts before the game, so load it with inside jokes; getting fooled on an inside joke prompt drinks double.
Two colour mode: drawing with two colours is on by default; play a round with one colour only and halve the drinks.
watchOut: It is one game, so it gets repetitive after two plays in a row; it is best as a warm up before a full pack. Phones on different networks from the host sometimes fail to join.
duration: About 15 min per game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal. The game runs 3 to 8 and at 4 every drawing gets a manageable number of fake titles while everyone votes every time.
notes: Steam listed 3 to 8 players at $9.99 in Oct 2026; the official page lists Windows, Mac, Linux, Switch, Xbox and PlayStation.

name: Use Your Words
needs: One PC, Switch, Xbox or PlayStation running the game, phones to join at wordsgame.lol
howToPlay: A Jackbox-style party game for 3 to 6 players from a different studio. Phones connect through a website and act as controllers. Four mini games: subtitle a foreign film clip, fill in a blank in a news headline, write a photo caption, and a survey round. Everyone votes on the funniest answer; the game also slips in fake House Answers to trap voters.
tip: Hidden House Answers are the drinking hook: vote for one and you drink.
setup: One person buys Use Your Words (about 15 dollars on Steam, also on Switch, Xbox and PlayStation) and launches it on the TV.
The screen shows a room code. Everyone opens wordsgame.lol on their phone and enters the code and a name.
Pick a full game (all four mini games) or a single mini game from the menu.
Agree that voting for a House Answer is a drink before you start.
Host starts once all four are connected.
rules: Each mini game shows a prompt on the TV: a film clip to subtitle, a headline with a blank, a photo to caption, or a survey question.
Everyone types an answer on their phone before the timer ends.
All answers appear on the TV, mixed with one or two fake House Answers written by the game.
Everyone votes for the funniest answer; you cannot vote for your own.
Points go to the most voted answers; voting for a House Answer costs points.
After all four mini games the highest score wins.
drinkTriggers: Vote for a House Answer: drink 2.
Your answer gets zero votes: drink 1.
Your answer wins the round: hand out 2.
Last place at the end: finish your drink.
variations: Use Your Words 2 is a sequel with twice the content and a Family Mode filter; a Complete Collection bundle includes both.
Family Mode off and a house rule that the blandest answer each round (group pick) drinks 1 keeps people swinging.
watchOut: Less polished than Jackbox and the content set is smaller, so prompts repeat after a few sessions. Phones must reach wordsgame.lol, so a weak wifi signal will kick controllers.
duration: 20 to 30 min per full game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal. The game is built for 3 to 6 and at 4 everyone votes on 3 real answers plus the fakes, which is just enough to be tricky.

links.label: Use Your Words on Nintendo Switch

notes: Steam lists 3 to 6 players at $14.99 with phones or tablets as controllers; the Nintendo page confirms joining through wordsgame.lol. The Xbox store page also loaded.

name: Skribbl.io
subcategory: Browser games with a room code
howToPlay: Pictionary. Last to guess drinks; the drawer drinks if nobody guesses.
tip: Add custom words from inside jokes.
setup: One person opens skribbl.io, enters a name and clicks Create Private Room.
Set rounds (3 is good), draw time (60 to 80 seconds), and paste in 20 or more custom words from inside jokes; tick Use custom words only if you want.
Copy the invite link and drop it in the group chat. Everyone opens it on their own phone or laptop.
When all four names are in the room, the host presses Start.
Drinks within reach; a voice call or being in the same room makes it better.
rules: Each turn one player picks one of three words and draws it; the others type guesses in the chat box.
Correct guessers get points, more for guessing fast. The drawer gets points based on how many guessed.
The round ends when everyone has guessed or the timer runs out, then the word is revealed.
Apply the drinking rule for that turn, then the next player draws.
After all rounds the leaderboard shows the winner.
drinkTriggers: Last of the three guessers to get it: drink 1.
Nobody guesses your drawing: drawer drinks 2.
Never guessed it at all: drink 2.
Write the word on the canvas or use letters: drink 3 and skip your next turn.
Lowest score at the end: finish your drink.
variations: Hidden mode hides the word length hints, which makes guessing harder; use it with 1 drink per missed word instead of 2.
Speed night: 30 second draw time, 5 rounds, drink 1 every turn you do not guess.
watchOut: Drawing on a phone with a finger is rough; laptops or tablets help. With 4 players only 3 are guessing, so 'last to guess' comes fast. Public rooms are full of strangers, always use a private room.
duration: About 10 min per 3 round game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine. The game allows 2 to 20, and 4 keeps turns coming quickly, though 'last to guess' is less dramatic with just 3 guessers.

name: Gartic Phone
subcategory: Browser games with a room code
howToPlay: Telephone pictionary. At the reveal, drink every time the chain went off the rails on your turn.
tip: Funniest reveal of any game here.
setup: One person opens garticphone.com, picks a character and nickname, and clicks Start to create a room.
Choose a mode (Normal is the classic write, draw, guess chain) and leave the default time limits.
Copy the room link from the lobby and send it to the group; everyone joins on their own phone or laptop.
Get on a voice call or sit together; the reveal is the whole point.
The host starts the game once all four are in.
rules: Everyone writes a sentence on their own device.
Each sentence is passed to the next player, who has to draw it.
The drawing is passed on, and the next player writes what they think it shows.
This keeps going until the chain has visited everyone; with 4 players that is 4 steps.
The host plays back every chain on the big screen step by step.
During the replay, whoever caused each step to go wrong drinks.
drinkTriggers: Your drawing got guessed wrong by the next person: drink 1.
Your guess broke the chain even though the drawing was clear (group vote): drink 2.
Chain ends on something completely unrelated to the start: everyone in that chain drinks 1.
Chain survives intact start to finish: everyone not in it drinks 1.
variations: Animation mode: each player adds a frame, and the group votes on the worst frame; that artist drinks 2.
Knock-off and Sandwich modes change the order of write and draw; keep the same drink rules.
Speedrun mode cuts all timers short; drink 1 for every blank or unfinished step you submit.
watchOut: With 4 players chains are short, so you get fewer absurd detours; run 2 or 3 games back to back. The site forces everyone to enable JavaScript and can be slow on old phones.
duration: About 5 min per game plus 5 min of reveal; play 3 or 4
playerSweetSpot: 4 is a stretch but works. Chains are only 4 steps, so the drift is milder than with 8; use Normal mode and play several rounds.

links.label: Gartic Phone on the App Store

notes: garticphone.com sits behind a Cloudflare bot check for automated fetches but loaded normally in a real browser and shows the Start room screen. The App Store listing is by Gartic (seller Gartic Publicidade Digital, copyright Onrizon).

name: JKLM.fun (BombParty, PopSauce)
subcategory: Browser games with a room code
howToPlay: BombParty: type a word with the given syllable before the bomb. PopSauce: guess the image or song. Lose a life, drink.
tip: Free, no accounts.
setup: One person opens jklm.fun, types a nickname, and clicks Start a new room, choosing Private.
Pick BombParty or PopSauce in the room, and share the 4-letter room code shown at the top.
Everyone else opens jklm.fun on their phone, enters the room code and joins as a guest.
Players click Join round; the host adjusts lives and timer if needed and starts.
Drinks ready; no accounts needed.
rules: BombParty: the bomb lands on one player with a syllable like 'ING'. Type any word containing it and press enter before the bomb goes off.
A valid word passes the bomb to the next player. If it explodes on you, you lose a life (2 by default).
Lose all lives and you are out; last player standing wins the round.
PopSauce: an image, song clip or text appears and everyone types the answer; faster answers score more.
PopSauce rounds end when the score limit is reached.
Apply the drinking rule between rounds and start the next one.
drinkTriggers: BombParty: bomb explodes on you, drink 1 per life lost.
BombParty: eliminated, drink 2; first out drinks 3.
PopSauce: miss an answer everyone else got, drink 1.
PopSauce: lowest score at the end of the round, drink 3.
variations: Alphabet bonus: using every letter of the alphabet across your words gives you a life back, and the table drinks 1 when you earn it.
Hard mode: set the timer short and 1 life. Each explosion is a full gulp.
watchOut: BombParty is a typing game; phone keyboards are slow and the fast typist on a laptop will dominate. Rooms occasionally have rude strangers if left public, so keep it private.
duration: 3 to 5 min per BombParty round; 5 to 10 min per PopSauce round
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine. The bomb cycles fast enough to stay tense and nobody waits long for their turn.
notes: The homepage lists BombParty, PopSauce and Master of the Grid; a seed entry for one-device BombParty already exists under a different id.

name: Codenames (codenames.game)
subcategory: Browser games with a room code
howToPlay: 2v2. Spymasters give one-word clues. Losing team drinks; hit the assassin and finish your drink.
tip: Perfect for exactly 4.
setup: One person opens codenames.game, enters a nickname and clicks Enter Game to create a room.
Copy the room URL from the address bar and send it to the other three; they open it on their own devices.
Split into two teams of 2. On each team one person clicks Join as Spymaster, the other Join as Operative.
Spymasters see the key card with colours; operatives see only the 25 words.
The host picks the word pack and starts. Sit so operatives cannot see their spymaster's screen.
Everyone has a drink; teams agree on who drinks for team losses (both).
rules: The team shown as starting goes first. Its spymaster types a one-word clue and a number, like 'ocean 2'.
The operative taps words they think match. A correct word lets them keep guessing, up to the number plus one.
Tapping a neutral word ends the turn. Tapping the other team's word ends the turn and helps them.
Tapping the black assassin word loses the game on the spot.
Teams alternate turns until one team has found all of its words.
Drink for the result, swap spymasters, and play again.
drinkTriggers: Your operative reveals an enemy word: both on that team drink 1.
Reveal a neutral word: operative drinks 1.
Hit the assassin: the whole losing team finishes their drink.
Lose normally: losing team drinks 3 each.
Clue that is a word on the board or breaks the one-word rule: spymaster drinks 2.
variations: Duet rules: play cooperatively 2v2 against the deck using the Duet setting if available, and drink per mistake instead.
Pictures pack: picture cards instead of words, same drinking rules.
Timer: set a 60 second clue timer; a spymaster who runs out of time drinks 2 and the turn passes.
watchOut: Operatives must not peek at spymaster screens, so sit across from each other. A drunk spymaster accidentally saying a board word is the most common foul; agree the penalty first. Games can stall if clues get too cautious.
duration: 10 to 15 min per game
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal. Two teams of 2 is the minimum and the classic configuration, with one spymaster and one operative each.

name: Spyfall (spyfall.app)
subcategory: Browser games with a room code
howToPlay: One spy, everyone else knows the location. Spy caught, spy drinks. Spy guesses the location, everyone else drinks.
tip: Short rounds, play many.
setup: One person opens spyfall.app, which now sends you to spyfall.live, and clicks Start a game to create a private room.
Share the room code; the other three click Join a game and enter it on their phones.
The host sets the round timer (6 to 8 minutes is good) and starts.
Each phone privately shows either the secret location and a role, or just 'You are the spy'.
Everyone sits where they can see each other's faces, not their screens.
rules: The timer starts. The host asks any player a question about the location without naming it, like 'Would you wear a uniform here?'
The person who answered asks the next question to someone else.
Non-spies try to prove they know the place without giving it away. The spy bluffs and tries to work out where they are.
At any point a player can accuse someone; if everyone else agrees, that player is revealed.
If the spy is caught, the non-spies win. If an innocent is accused, the spy wins.
The spy can stop the clock and guess the location. Right guess, spy wins; wrong, spy loses.
Timer runs out with no accusation: spy wins.
drinkTriggers: Spy caught: spy drinks 3.
Spy guesses the location correctly: everyone else drinks 2.
Wrong accusation: the accuser drinks 2 and the spy wins, so everyone else drinks 1 more.
Answer a question with the name of the location by accident: drink 2.
Timer runs out: non-spies drink 1 each.
variations: Two round sets: play 6 rounds and keep score (spy win 2 points, catching the spy 1 point); lowest total finishes their drink.
No-vote variant: the spy must guess before the timer ends or loses; everyone drinks 1 per minute the spy survives.
watchOut: With 4 players one spy among 3 is easy to spot if people ask obvious questions; keep questions vague. spyfall.app itself redirects, so the bookmark is spyfall.live now.
duration: 6 to 8 min per round; play 4 to 6
playerSweetSpot: 4 is a stretch but workable. The site says 3 to 8; at 4 rounds are quick and the spy has a harder time hiding, so keep the timer short.

links.label: Spyfall online (spyfall.live, redirect target of spyfall.app)

notes: spyfall.app now returns a permanent redirect to www.spyfall.live, which loaded and describes private rooms with a shareable code.

name: Wavelength (longwave.web.app)
subcategory: Browser games with a room code
howToPlay: 2v2. Guess where a clue sits on a spectrum. Losing team drinks the point difference.
tip: Free browser version.
setup: One person opens longwave.web.app and creates a room; a room link or code appears.
Send the link to the others; everyone opens it on their own phone.
Split into two teams of 2 (left brain and right brain).
Fill drinks; the psychic each round should sit where only they can see their own screen.
rules: One player on the active team is the psychic. Their screen shows a spectrum like 'hot to cold' and a hidden target point on it.
The psychic gives a one or two word clue that sits exactly at the target, for example 'coffee'.
Their teammate drags the dial to where they think the target is and locks it in.
The other team guesses whether the target is left or right of the dial for a bonus point.
Reveal: 4 points for a bullseye, 3 or 2 for close, 0 for a miss.
Teams alternate psychics. First team to 10 points wins.
drinkTriggers: Miss entirely (0 points): the guessing team drinks 2 each.
Scoring 2 or 3: guessing team drinks 1 each.
Bullseye: the other team drinks 2 each.
Wrong left or right call: that team drinks 1.
Lose the game: losing team drinks the point difference, split between them.
variations: Co-op mode: all four play as one team against a round limit and drink 1 for every point short of the target total.
Psychic silence: the psychic is not allowed to react to the guess; any flinch costs them 1.
watchOut: The psychic must not react during the guess. The spectrum cards are the whole game, so if the group finds them too abstract, swap to a lighter game. The site is a fan adaptation and could vanish without notice.
duration: About 15 to 20 min per game to 10 points
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine. Two teams of 2 means each person is psychic every other round for their team, which keeps everyone involved.
notes: longwave.web.app loads (HTTP 200) and its page metadata reads 'Online adaptation of the Wavelength board game'. The app is a JavaScript shell so room and team flow above is based on the board game rules; it is an unofficial fan version.

name: Among Us
subcategory: Browser games with a room code
howToPlay: Eject the wrong person, everyone who voted drinks. Impostor caught, impostor drinks.
tip: Tight with 4; one impostor only.
setup: Everyone installs Among Us on their phone, PC or console; it is free on mobile and cheap on PC and consoles, and crossplay works between all of them.
One person taps Online, then Create Game, sets Impostors to 1 and picks a map (The Skeld is simplest).
The lobby shows a 6-letter code. Everyone else taps Online, Enter Code, and types it.
In the lobby, the host lowers the task count a bit and sets a short kill cooldown so rounds move.
Agree that nobody talks except during meetings, and that drinking happens at meetings and at the end.
Host starts once all four are in.
rules: Each round 3 crewmates do tasks around the map while the 1 impostor tries to kill them without being seen.
Nobody talks while moving around the map. Keep your drink next to you.
Finding a body or pressing the emergency button calls a meeting where everyone can talk and vote.
The player with the most votes is ejected; ties and skips eject nobody.
Crew wins by finishing all tasks or ejecting the impostor. The impostor wins by killing until only 1 crewmate is left.
Drink per the result, then start a new round with a new random impostor.
drinkTriggers: Eject an innocent: everyone who voted for them drinks 2.
Impostor ejected: impostor drinks 3.
Killed before the first meeting: drink 1 while you float.
Impostor wins: all surviving crew finish their drinks.
Call an emergency meeting with no real evidence: drink 1.
variations: Hide and Seek mode (built into the game): the impostor is known, crew just run; every time you get caught, drink 2.
Quiet kills: with 4 players, set kill cooldown to 15 seconds and 2 short tasks so a round lasts 3 minutes; the drinking rules stay the same.
Ghost rule: ghosts can still drink along with every meeting to stay in it.

howToPlay: Mario Party for people who do not all own a Switch. A board game with items you fire at each other, broken up by quick minigames. One person hosts an online lobby for the four of you. Drinks run on minigame placement and board hits: lose a minigame and drink, get hit by an item and drink, the winner of the board hands out.
tip: Set the board to 10 turns and skip bots; 4 real players is the best version of this game.
setup: Everyone installs Pummel Party (about 15 dollars on Steam, also on Switch, PlayStation and Xbox).
Get on Discord or party chat.
One person picks Online, creates a private lobby and shares the lobby code or invites the others from the friends list.
Choose Board mode, pick a map, set turns to 10 and the minigame set to all.
Agree on the drinking rules; drinks within reach of the controller.
rules: On your board turn, roll and move. Land on item spaces to pick up weapons and tools, and use them on other players.
The goal is to collect keys or reach the goal space on the map before anyone else.
After every round of board turns, everyone plays a short minigame together.
Minigame placement 1st to 4th decides who drinks for that round.
After the set number of turns, the player with the most keys or goals wins the board.
Minigames mode lets you skip the board and just play a string of minigames if time is short.
drinkTriggers: Last in a minigame: drink 2. Third: drink 1.
Hit by another player's item on the board: drink 1.
Lose a key or get sent back on the board: drink 2.
Win a minigame: hand out 1.
Lose the board game: finish your drink. Winner hands out 3.
variations: Minigame marathon: 15 minigames in Minigames mode, drink by placement every time; fewest wins finishes their drink.
Item tax: using an item on someone costs you 1 sip too, which stops the leader from being destroyed every turn.
watchOut: A full board game with 4 drinkers runs over an hour, so cap the turns at 10. Crossplay between PC and consoles is not stated on the store page, so buy on the same platform.
duration: 45 to 75 min per 10 turn board; 1 to 2 min per minigame
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal. The game is built for 4 to 8 and at 4 every minigame has everyone in it with no bots.
notes: Steam listed $14.99, 4 to 8 players (bots can fill slots), Online PvP and shared screen. Crossplay was not mentioned, so cross-platform play is unverified.

name: Drunk board games
category: Bonus: board games and purpose-made decks
subcategory: Bonus: board games and purpose-made decks
howToPlay: Catan: drink when robbed. Monopoly: drink on rent paid, finish on jail. Scrabble: sip per point below the leader. Chess or Checkers: sip per piece lost. Twister: drink per fall.
tip: Catan and Monopoly run long; set a time cap.
setup: Pick one board game the whole table knows: Catan, Monopoly or Scrabble are the usual three.
Set up the game as normal.
Agree on a time cap before you start: 60 min for Catan, 45 min for Monopoly, 45 min for Scrabble. Highest score at the cap wins.
Write the drink triggers for that game on a card and leave it on the table.
Everyone has a drink and a refill nearby.
rules: Play the game by its normal rules. The drink rules sit on top.
Catan: drink when the robber lands on your hex or you get robbed, when you discard on a 7, and when someone else scores a point.
Catan: whoever takes Longest Road or Largest Army from you makes you drink 2 extra.
Monopoly: drink when you pay rent, when you land on a tax space, Chance or Community Chest, and when you land on a free property and do not buy it.
Monopoly: jail is the big one. Going to jail means finishing your drink.
Scrabble: after each turn, drink 1 sip for every 10 points you are behind the leader, cap 3. A bingo (all 7 tiles) means everyone else drinks 3.
At the time cap or the normal end, the winner gives out drinks and last place finishes theirs.
drinkTriggers: Catan, robbed or robber placed on your hex: drink 1. Discard on a 7: drink 1 per 2 cards.
Catan, someone else scores a victory point: drink 1. Lose Longest Road or Largest Army: drink 2.
Catan, end of game: drink the point gap to the winner, cap 4.
Monopoly, pay rent: drink 1 (2 if there is a hotel). Tax, Chance, Community Chest: drink 1.
Monopoly, go to jail: finish your drink. Pass Go: give 1.
Scrabble, behind the leader: 1 sip per 10 points, cap 3. Bingo: everyone else drinks 3. Challenge a word and lose: drink 2.
Any game, last place at the end: finish your drink. Winner gives 5 sips.
variations: Lighter Catan: only the robber and the 7 trigger drinks. Trading and building are free. Good for a long game.
Monopoly Board Crawl: Hasbro's official 2024 drinking edition replaces money with sips and ends after one lap of the board. If you own it, use its rules instead.
Twister, Chess, Checkers: fall in Twister drink 2; lose a piece in chess or checkers drink 1, lose your queen finish your drink.
watchOut: Catan and Monopoly run long and the drinks pile up around the 45-minute mark, so the time cap is not optional. Rent and robber rules punish whoever is already losing; keep those sips small.
duration: 45 to 60 min with the time cap; Scrabble about 45 min
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: Catan and Monopoly are at their best with four and Scrabble takes four. Fewer players and the drinks hit the same person too often.

name: Purpose-made drinking card decks
category: Bonus: board games and purpose-made decks
subcategory: Bonus: board games and purpose-made decks
howToPlay: Buzzed, Do or Drink, These Cards Will Get You Drunk, Drunk Stoned or Stupid, Kings of Booze, Sotally Tober, Drink-A-Palooza. All designed for 4 or more.
tip: Buzzed and These Cards Will Get You Drunk are the most popular at 4.
setup: Buy one deck: Buzzed (about $20, 200 cards, 3+ players), These Cards Will Get You Drunk (about $16, 100 cards, 2 to 8 players), Drunk Stoned or Stupid (about $18, 250 cards, 4+ players) or Do or Drink (physical deck or free app).
Shuffle the deck and put it face down in the middle.
Everyone has a drink. These decks assume a drink in hand at all times.
Read the little rules card that comes in the box; each deck has one twist.
Pick a first player: whoever had the most drinks already.
rules: On your turn, draw the top card and read it out loud.
Do what the card says. It names who drinks and how much, or sets a mini game, vote or dare.
If the card is a vote (Buzzed, Drunk Stoned or Stupid), everyone points at once on the count of three. The person with the most fingers drinks or takes the card.
If the card is a dare (These Cards Will Get You Drunk, Do or Drink), do it or drink the stated penalty.
If the card sets a rule that lasts, keep it on the table face up until it is replaced.
Pass the deck clockwise. Next player draws.
Drunk Stoned or Stupid ends when someone collects 7 cards; that person loses. The others end when the deck runs out or when you decide to stop.
drinkTriggers: Buzzed: the card says who drinks, usually either the reader or everyone the statement applies to; 1 drink unless the card says more.
These Cards Will Get You Drunk: skipped dare or lost vote, drink the number on the card, typically 1 to 3; some cards say finish your drink.
Drunk Stoned or Stupid: tagged with the card, drink 1; reaching 7 cards, finish your drink.
Do or Drink: refuse the dare, drink the amount on the card, usually 2 to 5 sips or a shot.
Any deck: reading a card wrong or showing it early, drink 1.
variations: Mixed deck: shuffle two decks together. Drunk Stoned or Stupid plus Buzzed is a common combo so votes and confessions alternate.
Low tide: halve every number on the cards. The decks are written for a heavy night; half strength suits a 4-person evening.
Judge mode: in Drunk Stoned or Stupid, rotate a judge each turn who makes the final call on who gets tagged; ties go to the judge.
watchOut: These decks are built to get you drunk and they do; a full deck of Buzzed in one sitting is too much for four people, so stop at 30 cards or play half strength. Dares in Do or Drink escalate quickly, so agree on a veto word.
duration: About 1 min per card; 30 to 45 min for a session of 30 to 40 cards
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine: every deck lists 3 or 4 as the minimum and votes still work with four pointing fingers, though the vote-based decks are funnier with 6.

name: Exploding Kittens (drinking rules)
category: Bonus: board games and purpose-made decks
subcategory: Bonus: board games and purpose-made decks
needs: An Exploding Kittens deck, one center cup
howToPlay: Normal Exploding Kittens with a center cup. Every safe draw you pour a little of your drink into the cup. Nopes, steals and attacks cost sips, and whoever draws a kitten they cannot defuse is out and drinks the whole cup.
tip: With 4 use 3 Exploding Kittens so the deck stays tense; the NSFW or Party Pack decks work the same.
setup: Take all Exploding Kittens and Defuse cards out of the deck. Deal each player 1 Defuse.
Shuffle the rest and deal 7 cards each.
Put 3 Exploding Kittens (one fewer than the number of players) and the 2 leftover Defuses back in and shuffle.
Put an empty cup in the middle of the table.
Everyone has a drink, ideally all the same thing since it ends up mixed in the cup.
rules: On your turn, play as many action cards as you like, or none.
End your turn by drawing one card from the top of the deck.
Safe draw: pour a splash of your drink into the center cup, as much or as little as you like.
Drew an Exploding Kitten with a Defuse: play it, take a drink, and slide the kitten back into the deck anywhere you want.
Drew an Exploding Kitten with no Defuse: you are out. Drink the whole center cup.
Nope cancels any action. Nope wars go back and forth; the loser of the war drinks.
Attack ends your turn and makes the next player take two turns. Skip ends your turn without drawing.
Last player alive wins and hands out drinks.
drinkTriggers: Every safe draw: pour some of your drink into the center cup.
Your action gets Noped: drink 1.
Lose a Nope war: drink 1 per Nope played in the war.
A card of yours is stolen (Favor, two of a kind, three of a kind): drink 1, or 2 if they named the card.
Defuse an Exploding Kitten: drink 2.
Explode: drink the whole center cup and you are out.
Winner: give 3 sips.
variations: No cup: skip the pouring. Exploding means finish your own drink instead. Lighter and less gross.
Dodge drinks: if you See the Future and then Skip or Attack past a kitten you saw, everyone else drinks 1 for your smug face.
Cone of Shame: the exploded player wears the cone from the Imploding Kittens expansion, or any silly hat, while chugging the cup.
watchOut: The center cup is only as bad as what people pour in, so agree on one drink type. With 4 people the game is short and someone can explode on turn two, so the cup is sometimes nearly empty; the no-cup variation is more consistent.
duration: About 10 to 15 min per game; play 2 or 3
playerSweetSpot: 4 is ideal: the base game is for 2 to 5 and four players with three kittens is the tensest ratio.

name: Cards Against Humanity (physical deck)
category: Bonus: board games and purpose-made decks
subcategory: Bonus: board games and purpose-made decks
needs: A Cards Against Humanity box or the free printed PDF
howToPlay: Classic fill-in-the-blank party game with a drinking layer. The Card Czar reads a black card, everyone else plays their funniest white card, the Czar picks a winner, and the losers drink. The official site gives away the whole base game as a free PDF.
tip: With 4 deal 10 white cards instead of 7 so there is enough choice each round.
setup: Buy the box or print the free PDF from cardsagainsthumanity.com and cut it up.
Shuffle the white cards and black cards separately.
Deal 10 white cards to each player.
Whoever most recently pooped is the first Card Czar, per the official rules.
Everyone has a drink.
rules: The Czar reads the black card out loud.
Each other player picks one white card from their hand and passes it face down to the Czar.
The Czar shuffles the answers and reads each one with the black card.
The Czar picks the funniest. That player takes the black card as a point.
The two players who lost the round drink.
Everyone draws back up to 10 white cards. The Czar role passes clockwise.
Pick 2 black cards work the same with two white cards each.
First to 5 black cards wins and the others finish a round of drinks.
drinkTriggers: Your card was not picked: drink 1.
Pick 2 card and you lost: drink 2.
Round winner: give 2 sips.
Czar picks a card and then admits they do not get the joke: Czar drinks 2.
Played a card that does not fit the blank grammatically at all: drink 1 for laziness.
Game winner at 5 black cards: everyone else finishes their drink.
variations: Rebooting the universe: official house rule where you may trade in a black card point to discard your whole hand and redraw. Add: you also drink 2.
God is dead: official house rule with no Czar. Everyone votes on the best card; ties mean everyone drinks 1.
Happy ending: when you want to stop, play the Make a haiku black card as the last round. Losers finish their drinks.
watchOut: With 4 there are only three answers per round, so the Czar sees the same people's humor over and over; dealing 10 cards and rotating fast helps. It is a slow drinker, so it works better as a mid-night chill than a kickoff.
duration: About 2 min per black card; 15 to 25 min to 5 points
playerSweetSpot: 4 is fine: three answers per round is the floor for a real choice. The official box says 4 to 20 players.
